claim.chronic-mesenteric-ischemia.cta-ev.statement: CTA is the principal anatomic diagnostic study for suspected occlusive chronic mesenteric ischemia after compatible symptoms and reasonable evaluation for alternative causes.
claim.chronic-mesenteric-ischemia.cta-ev.limitation: Excludes acute mesenteric ischemia, nonocclusive disease, and patients who cannot receive iodinated contrast; no exact stenosis threshold is taught.
claim.chronic-mesenteric-ischemia.cta-ev.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with chronic postprandial pain, reduced intake or weight loss, atherosclerotic risk, and no acute-abdomen features.

claim.chronic-mesenteric-ischemia.multiv.statement: Compatible symptoms with significant celiac and superior mesenteric arterial disease support prompt expert vascular referral for revascularization planning without requiring a separate functional confirmation test.
claim.chronic-mesenteric-ischemia.multiv.limitation: The concept does not choose open versus endovascular repair, a device, or a target-vessel sequence; several recommendations rely on observational evidence and expert agreement.
claim.chronic-mesenteric-ischemia.multiv.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with compatible symptoms and confirmed multivessel occlusive chronic mesenteric ischemia after alternative GI causes have been evaluated.

claim.primary-aldosteronism.prepared-arr.statement: Primary aldosteronism screening measures aldosterone and renin to calculate the ARR, with potassium correction and safe management of interfering medications needed for interpretable results.
claim.primary-aldosteronism.prepared-arr.limitation: One adequate current guideline source; no universal assay cutoff or blanket medication-withdrawal rule is taught.
claim.primary-aldosteronism.prepared-arr.applicablePopulation: Adults with resistant hypertension and spontaneous hypokalemia undergoing safely prepared biochemical evaluation.

claim.primary-aldosteronism.ct-avs-befor.statement: An adult with confirmed primary aldosteronism who wants and is a candidate for adrenalectomy generally undergoes adrenal CT plus adrenal venous sampling before choosing unilateral surgery.
claim.primary-aldosteronism.ct-avs-befor.limitation: One adequate current guideline source; excludes the narrow very-young-patient exception and does not teach AVS indices or operative technique.
claim.primary-aldosteronism.ct-avs-befor.applicablePopulation: Adults with overt confirmed primary aldosteronism who desire and are candidates for surgical treatment.

claim.primary-aldosteronism.overt-phenot.statement: In resistant hypertension with spontaneous hypokalemia, immunoassay aldosterone above 20 ng/dL with plasma renin activity below 0.2 ng/mL/h is overt renin-independent aldosterone production for which a separate suppression test is not required before surgical-localization evaluation.
claim.primary-aldosteronism.overt-phenot.limitation: One adequate current guideline source; the authored 24 ng/dL aldosterone and 0.1 ng/mL/h PRA values are a case instance of this narrow branch, not universal screening cutoffs.
claim.primary-aldosteronism.overt-phenot.applicablePopulation: Adults with resistant hypertension, spontaneous hypokalemia, safely prepared sampling, and overt renin-independent aldosterone results.

claim.lactational-breast-abscess.targete.statement: Targeted breast ultrasound is appropriate for a stable lactating adult with a persistent focal tender or erythematous mass suspicious for an abscess.
claim.lactational-breast-abscess.targete.limitation: This does not make every episode of mastitis an imaging indication or exclude inflammatory cancer and other masses.
claim.lactational-breast-abscess.targete.applicablePopulation: Stable lactating adults with a persistent focal inflammatory breast mass suspicious for a collection.

claim.lactational-breast-abscess.selecte.statement: A confirmed uncomplicated drainable lactational abscess requires source control; image-guided aspiration with fluid culture is a reasonable initial option, with antibiotic care individualized.
claim.lactational-breast-abscess.selecte.limitation: Aspiration is not universal; repeated aspiration, catheter drainage, or surgery may be needed. This claim excludes sepsis, necrosis, rapidly progressive infection, and malignancy concern.
claim.lactational-breast-abscess.selecte.applicablePopulation: Stable lactating adults with a confirmed uncomplicated drainable breast abscess and no urgent complication.

claim.lactational-breast-abscess.continu.statement: Breastfeeding or expressed milk generally can continue from an affected breast when the infant's mouth and pump flange avoid purulent drainage, open infected tissue, and the drain site.
claim.lactational-breast-abscess.continu.limitation: Feeding safety remains individualized, including when an infant is immunocompromised or direct contact with infected tissue cannot be avoided.
claim.lactational-breast-abscess.continu.applicablePopulation: Lactating adults receiving care for a breast abscess whose infant and pump can avoid contact with purulent drainage, open tissue, and drains.

claim.post-thyroidectomy-voice.laryngeal.statement: Persistent voice change after thyroid surgery warrants laryngeal visualization with assessment of vocal-fold status.
claim.post-thyroidectomy-voice.laryngeal.limitation: Symptoms alone do not establish recurrent or external superior laryngeal nerve injury; edema, intubation injury, muscle or scar effects, and neural dysfunction can overlap.
claim.post-thyroidectomy-voice.laryngeal.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent voice change after thyroid surgery.

claim.post-thyroidectomy-voice.external-.statement: The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supplies the cricothyroid muscle; postoperative loss of high pitch or projection with preserved ordinary vocal-fold mobility supports cricothyroid or external superior laryngeal nerve dysfunction.
claim.post-thyroidectomy-voice.external-.limitation: This pattern supports but does not prove the localization; specialized voice testing or laryngeal electromyography may be needed.
claim.post-thyroidectomy-voice.external-.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated for persistent loss of upper vocal range or projection after thyroid superior-pole dissection.

claim.zenker-diverticulum.contrast-swall.statement: Contrast swallow with fluoroscopy is an appropriate first anatomic test when cervical dysphagia and regurgitation of retained food specifically suggest a proximal pharyngoesophageal pouch.
claim.zenker-diverticulum.contrast-swall.limitation: This does not generalize to all persistent esophageal dysphagia, for which endoscopy often leads after oropharyngeal disease is excluded.
claim.zenker-diverticulum.contrast-swall.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a classic presentation suggesting a proximal pharyngoesophageal pouch.

claim.zenker-diverticulum.false-pouch-an.statement: A posterior pouch containing mucosa and submucosa above the cricopharyngeus supports Zenker diverticulum and reflects impaired cricopharyngeal opening with increased pharyngeal pressure.
claim.zenker-diverticulum.false-pouch-an.limitation: A lateral pouch below the cricopharyngeus suggests another diverticulum; returned imaging supports the pattern without selecting a treatment technique.
claim.zenker-diverticulum.false-pouch-an.applicablePopulation: Adults with returned contrast-swallow anatomy showing a posterior pouch above the cricopharyngeus.

claim.peripheral-arterial-disease.restin.statement: Resting ankle-brachial index testing is an appropriate initial physiologic test for reproducible exertional calf discomfort relieved by rest with examination findings suggesting lower-extremity peripheral arterial disease.
claim.peripheral-arterial-disease.restin.limitation: Normal or high values can be misleading with noncompressible vessels; exercise ABI or toe-pressure assessment may be needed when suspicion persists.
claim.peripheral-arterial-disease.restin.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with classic exertional calf symptoms, suggestive examination findings, and no limb threat.

claim.peripheral-arterial-disease.struct.statement: Supervised exercise therapy or another structured exercise program is initial treatment for stable functionally limiting intermittent claudication before invasive revascularization when risk-reduction care is already addressed.
claim.peripheral-arterial-disease.struct.limitation: This excludes ischemic rest pain, tissue loss, acute ischemia, and ongoing limb threat and does not prescribe a universal duration or medication regimen.
claim.peripheral-arterial-disease.struct.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with functionally limiting intermittent claudication and no limb-threatening ischemia.

claim.asymptomatic-phpt.three-site-dxa.statement: For an adult with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism, skeletal assessment includes DXA at the lumbar spine, hip, and distal one-third radius.
claim.asymptomatic-phpt.three-site-dxa.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. This claim does not assign a universal DXA diagnostic threshold or determine surgery by bone density alone.
claim.asymptomatic-phpt.three-site-dxa.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism undergoing standard skeletal assessment.

claim.asymptomatic-phpt.age-under-50-sur.statement: For an otherwise asymptomatic patient with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism, age under 50 years is an independent guideline criterion supporting parathyroidectomy.
claim.asymptomatic-phpt.age-under-50-sur.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. Operative suitability, localization, genetic evaluation, and all other surgical criteria remain outside this focused pathway.
claim.asymptomatic-phpt.age-under-50-sur.applicablePopulation: Adults younger than 50 years with confirmed asymptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism and no other operative criterion described in this pathway.

claim.cushing.confirm-before-localizatio.statement: Cause-directed imaging follows confirmation of endogenous hypercortisolism rather than serving as an initial screening test for suspected Cushing syndrome.
claim.cushing.confirm-before-localizatio.limitation: This compact pathway excludes discordant screening, cyclic disease, pseudo-Cushing states, and individualized specialist testing.
claim.cushing.confirm-before-localizatio.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with unequivocally established endogenous hypercortisolism and no exogenous glucocorticoid exposure.

claim.cushing.acth-guides-adrenal-imagin.statement: After Cushing syndrome is established, plasma ACTH classifies the etiologic pathway; suppressed ACTH directs adrenal imaging.
claim.cushing.acth-guides-adrenal-imagin.limitation: One adequate supporting source was used. ACTH-dependent localization and definitive treatment decisions are outside this pathway; imaging does not alone establish functional etiology.
claim.cushing.acth-guides-adrenal-imagin.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with confirmed endogenous Cushing syndrome and a suppressed ACTH result.

claim.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessme.statement: MRI/MRCP is a preferred noninvasive study for assessing communication between a pancreatic cyst and the main pancreatic duct.
claim.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessme.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. Imaging does not definitively establish cyst subtype or malignancy.
claim.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessme.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an indeterminate pancreatic cyst who can undergo MRI/MRCP.

claim.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recogn.statement: A body or tail pancreatic cyst without main-duct communication supports a mucinous cystic neoplasm pattern rather than proving histology or cancer.
claim.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recogn.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. Management requires individualized risk assessment; cyst-fluid CEA can help classify mucinous lesions but does not identify high-grade dysplasia or pancreatic cancer.
claim.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recogn.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a returned pancreatic MRI/MRCP pattern compatible with mucinous cystic neoplasm.

claim.colon-cancer.preoperative-cross-se.statement: Preoperative staging of newly diagnosed colon cancer includes contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis to assess distant disease and local extension.
claim.colon-cancer.preoperative-cross-se.limitation: CT does not establish pathological nodal stage, and negative imaging does not prove node-negative disease; PET is not routine initial staging.
claim.colon-cancer.preoperative-cross-se.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with colonoscopy-confirmed nonobstructing, nonperforated invasive colon adenocarcinoma.

claim.colon-cancer.oncologic-regional-re.statement: Localized resectable colon cancer is treated by resection of the tumor-bearing colon together with its regional lymphatic drainage.
claim.colon-cancer.oncologic-regional-re.limitation: Operation extent depends on anatomy and patient factors; this claim does not select disputed splenic-flexure techniques or adjuvant therapy without pathological stage.
claim.colon-cancer.oncologic-regional-re.applicablePopulation: Adults with localized resectable colon adenocarcinoma and no distant or adjacent-organ invasion on staging.

claim.rectal-cancer.multimodal-response-.statement: Local response assessment after neoadjuvant treatment for rectal cancer combines digital rectal examination, endoscopic examination, and rectal-protocol MRI.
claim.rectal-cancer.multimodal-response-.limitation: Biopsy alone cannot establish complete response, and this pathway assumes systemic imaging has already excluded metastases.
claim.rectal-cancer.multimodal-response-.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with known mid or low rectal cancer after completed neoadjuvant treatment.

claim.rectal-cancer.selected-watch-and-w.statement: For a fully informed patient with a clinical complete response who prefers nonsurgical care and can adhere to intensive follow-up in an experienced multidisciplinary program, watch-and-wait is a reasonable option.
claim.rectal-cancer.selected-watch-and-w.limitation: This is a conditional option, not proof of pathological cure or mandatory care; total mesorectal excision remains a valid alternative and surveillance must be intensive.
claim.rectal-cancer.selected-watch-and-w.applicablePopulation: Selected adherent adults with a clinical complete response after neoadjuvant rectal cancer treatment and access to an experienced program.

claim.carotid-stenosis.confirmatory-vasc.statement: After duplex suggests severe stenosis in a patient with a recent ipsilateral retinal or hemispheric ischemic event, CTA or MRA is used to confirm stenosis and define anatomy before revascularization planning.
claim.carotid-stenosis.confirmatory-vasc.limitation: One adequate supporting guideline source was used. CTA and MRA selection is individualized; this pathway uses CTA and assumes the acute stroke assessment is complete.
claim.carotid-stenosis.confirmatory-vasc.applicablePopulation: Stable adults after completed acute assessment for a resolved ipsilateral retinal or nondisabling hemispheric ischemic event.

claim.carotid-stenosis.symptomatic-endar.statement: A suitable patient with recent symptoms and severe 70–99% ipsilateral carotid stenosis should receive prompt assessment for carotid endarterectomy together with best medical therapy.
claim.carotid-stenosis.symptomatic-endar.limitation: This excludes near-occlusion, complete occlusion, large infarct, hemorrhage, disabling deficit, prohibitive anatomy, and unsuitable operative risk.
claim.carotid-stenosis.symptomatic-endar.applicablePopulation: Stable suitable adults with recent ipsilateral symptoms and confirmed severe carotid stenosis after completed acute stroke assessment.

claim.bread-butter.breast-mass.image-gui.statement: After diagnostic imaging identifies an accessible suspicious solid breast mass, image-guided core biopsy can establish a tissue diagnosis before definitive excision planning.
claim.bread-butter.breast-mass.image-gui.limitation: This pathway excludes clinically urgent infection and does not prescribe a particular imaging modality or biopsy device.
claim.bread-butter.breast-mass.image-gui.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an accessible solid breast mass categorized as suspicious on completed diagnostic imaging.

claim.bread-butter.fibroadenoma.concorda.statement: A small, asymptomatic, core-proven fibroadenoma that is radiologically and pathologically concordant and lacks atypia or concern for phyllodes tumor can be managed without routine excision.
claim.bread-butter.fibroadenoma.concorda.limitation: This does not apply to discordance, atypia, phyllodes concern, symptoms, substantial growth, or a patient preference for removal.
claim.bread-butter.fibroadenoma.concorda.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an asymptomatic concordant fibroadenoma proven by core biopsy.

claim.bread-butter.skin-infection.equivo.statement: When examination cannot distinguish cellulitis from a superficial abscess, targeted soft-tissue ultrasound can identify a drainable collection.
claim.bread-butter.skin-infection.equivo.limitation: An obvious superficial abscess does not need imaging before drainage; operator skill, depth, anatomy, and vascular mimics affect interpretation.
claim.bread-butter.skin-infection.equivo.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an equivocal superficial skin infection and no necrotizing, vascular, deep-space, breast, or perianal concern.

claim.bread-butter.cutaneous-abscess.inc.statement: A confirmed, clinically meaningful, uncomplicated cutaneous abscess is treated primarily with incision and drainage.
claim.bread-butter.cutaneous-abscess.inc.limitation: Very small collections, special sites, deep infection, vascular mimics, immunocompromise, and systemic illness require individualized management.
claim.bread-butter.cutaneous-abscess.inc.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a discrete superficial cutaneous abscess confirmed on ultrasound.

claim.bread-butter.cutaneous-abscess.ant.statement: After drainage of an uncomplicated cutaneous abscess, adjunctive MRSA-active antibiotics offer modest benefits and adverse effects, so a universal no-antibiotic rule is not supported.
claim.bread-butter.cutaneous-abscess.ant.limitation: Local resistance, allergy, comorbidity, severity, immune status, and adverse-effect risk affect the separate antibiotic decision.
claim.bread-butter.cutaneous-abscess.ant.applicablePopulation: Adults after drainage of an uncomplicated cutaneous abscess.

claim.bread-butter.inguinal-hernia.watch.statement: Watchful waiting is a safe option for informed men with asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic reducible inguinal hernias, although later repair is common when symptoms develop.
claim.bread-butter.inguinal-hernia.watch.limitation: This does not apply to women, femoral hernias, activity-limiting symptoms, irreducibility, obstruction, or strangulation.
claim.bread-butter.inguinal-hernia.watch.applicablePopulation: Men with a confirmed reducible inguinal hernia and absent or minimal symptoms.

claim.bread-butter.femoral-hernia.timely.statement: A stable reducible femoral hernia warrants timely elective surgical repair planning even when symptoms are mild or absent.
claim.bread-butter.femoral-hernia.timely.limitation: Pain, irreducibility, obstruction, or ischemic concern changes the pathway to emergency assessment; the evidence base is largely observational.
claim.bread-butter.femoral-hernia.timely.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a confirmed reducible femoral hernia and no emergency feature.

claim.bread-butter.indirect-inguinal-her.statement: An indirect inguinal hernia enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels.
claim.bread-butter.indirect-inguinal-her.limitation: The vessel relationship classifies anatomy but does not establish acuity or select a repair technique.
claim.bread-butter.indirect-inguinal-her.applicablePopulation: Adults whose operative or imaging report directly describes a groin hernia's relationship to the inferior epigastric vessels.

claim.bread-butter.lfcn.post-laparoscopi.statement: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve supplies the anterolateral and lateral thigh, so isolated sensory symptoms there after inguinal surgery are compatible with irritation of this nerve.
claim.bread-butter.lfcn.post-laparoscopi.limitation: The pattern is compatible rather than diagnostic; weakness, progression, or a broader distribution requires evaluation for another lesion.
claim.bread-butter.lfcn.post-laparoscopi.applicablePopulation: Adults with isolated anterolateral-thigh sensory symptoms and preserved strength after laparoscopic inguinal repair.

claim.bread-butter.high-output-ileostomy.statement: Stable follow-up for persistently increased ileostomy output warrants assessment of renal function, electrolytes, and magnesium for fluid and salt depletion.
claim.bread-butter.high-output-ileostomy.limitation: This outpatient pathway excludes shock, acute kidney injury, infection, and obstruction and does not define a universal output threshold.
claim.bread-butter.high-output-ileostomy.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistently increased watery ileostomy losses and no acute complication.

claim.bread-butter.high-output-ileostomy.statement: After stabilization, a sodium-glucose oral rehydration plan is preferred to simply increasing hypotonic plain-water intake for high-output ileostomy losses.
claim.bread-butter.high-output-ileostomy.limitation: No exact output threshold, oral-rehydration formulation, total fluid target, or medication regimen is taught.
claim.bread-butter.high-output-ileostomy.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with high-output ileostomy losses who can drink and have no acute kidney injury, shock, infection, or obstruction.

claim.bread-butter.perianal-abscess.prom.statement: An acute, clinically evident superficial perianal abscess should be treated promptly with incision and drainage.
claim.bread-butter.perianal-abscess.prom.limitation: Occult, recurrent, Crohn-associated, deep, or complex disease may require imaging or examination under anesthesia.
claim.bread-butter.perianal-abscess.prom.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a clinically evident superficial perianal abscess.

claim.bread-butter.perianal-abscess.sele.statement: Routine antibiotics are generally unnecessary after adequate drainage of an uncomplicated anorectal abscess in a healthy patient; antibiotics are reserved for cellulitis, systemic infection, or immunosuppression.
claim.bread-butter.perianal-abscess.sele.limitation: The selective-antibiotic recommendation is weak and applies only after adequate drainage with explicit absence of cellulitis, systemic illness, and immunosuppression.
claim.bread-butter.perianal-abscess.sele.applicablePopulation: Healthy immunocompetent adults after adequate drainage of an uncomplicated anorectal abscess.

claim.bread-butter.beta-blocker.continue.statement: A patient taking a stable beta-blocker dose should generally continue it through noncardiac surgery when clinical circumstances do not create a contraindication.
claim.bread-butter.beta-blocker.continue.limitation: This does not override hypotension, bradycardia, shock, or another reason to hold therapy and does not support starting a beta blocker on surgery day solely for risk reduction.
claim.bread-butter.beta-blocker.continue.applicablePopulation: Adults on a tolerated stable chronic beta-blocker dose before elective noncardiac surgery.

claim.bread-butter.atrial-fibrillation.w.statement: For a patient receiving warfarin for atrial fibrillation who requires interruption for elective surgery, routine therapeutic-dose heparin bridging is not recommended.
claim.bread-butter.atrial-fibrillation.w.limitation: Selected very-high-thromboembolic-risk situations require individualized consideration; this does not concern ordinary postoperative VTE prophylaxis or mechanical-valve cases.
claim.bread-butter.atrial-fibrillation.w.applicablePopulation: Selected adults taking warfarin for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation without recent stroke, TIA, thrombosis, a mechanical valve, or another very-high-risk feature.

claim.bread-butter.antimicrobial-prophyl.statement: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis should be discontinued after incision closure; continuing it solely because a drain remains does not reduce surgical-site infection and adds antimicrobial harms.
claim.bread-butter.antimicrobial-prophyl.limitation: This concerns prophylaxis only, not treatment for an established infection or another therapeutic indication.
claim.bread-butter.antimicrobial-prophyl.applicablePopulation: Postoperative adults with a closed incision, no established infection, and a prophylactic antibiotic continued solely because a drain remains.

claim.bread-butter.cancer-surgery.extend.statement: After major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery, selected patients with high VTE risk and acceptable bleeding risk may receive extended postoperative pharmacologic prophylaxis for up to about four weeks; LMWH is an established option.
claim.bread-butter.cancer-surgery.extend.limitation: This is not universal for all cancer operations, and LMWH is not the only current agent; patient selection, renal function, and bleeding risk matter.
claim.bread-butter.cancer-surgery.extend.applicablePopulation: Selected high-VTE-risk adults after major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery with adequate renal function and low bleeding risk.

claim.bread-butter.postoperative-retenti.statement: For postoperative inability to void, bladder scanning provides an objective assessment before selecting a retention intervention.
claim.bread-butter.postoperative-retenti.limitation: No numeric scan threshold is taught, and suspected urethral trauma requires a different evaluation pathway.
claim.bread-butter.postoperative-retenti.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adults who cannot void and have no evidence of urethral trauma.

claim.bread-butter.postoperative-retenti.statement: Clearly symptomatic postoperative urinary retention with a large retained bladder volume warrants catheter decompression.
claim.bread-butter.postoperative-retenti.limitation: The claim does not set a universal volume threshold or choose between intermittent and indwelling catheterization for every patient.
claim.bread-butter.postoperative-retenti.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adults with symptoms and a bladder scan showing a large retained volume without urethral trauma.

claim.bread-butter.superficial-incisiona.statement: A localized superficial incisional surgical-site infection with purulence requires opening the involved incision and drainage, with removal of sutures or staples when needed for source control.
claim.bread-butter.superficial-incisiona.limitation: Systemic antibiotics depend on systemic response and operative site; deep, organ-space, and necrotizing infections require different care.
claim.bread-butter.superficial-incisiona.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with purulent superficial incisional infection, intact fascia, and no systemic toxicity.

claim.bread-butter.fascial-dehiscence-ev.statement: Postoperative abdominal wound separation with visible bowel is evisceration and requires immediate surgical escalation rather than delayed outpatient testing.
claim.bread-butter.fascial-dehiscence-ev.limitation: This claim addresses obvious evisceration; suspected fascial separation beneath intact skin can require a different urgent evaluation, and probing can worsen the defect.
claim.bread-butter.fascial-dehiscence-ev.applicablePopulation: Postoperative adults with visible bowel through a separated abdominal incision.

claim.bread-butter.evisceration.moist-co.statement: During immediate transfer for abdominal evisceration, exposed bowel should be protected with a sterile moist covering and should not be forcibly reduced.
claim.bread-butter.evisceration.moist-co.limitation: The explicit temporary-cover evidence comes from traumatic evisceration guidance; definitive postoperative management still requires immediate surgical care.
claim.bread-butter.evisceration.moist-co.applicablePopulation: Adults with exposed abdominal viscera awaiting immediate emergency surgical transfer.

claim.brief.adrenal-incidentaloma.one-mg.statement: A stable adult with an adrenal incidentaloma at least 1 cm should undergo biochemical evaluation for autonomous cortisol secretion with a 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test.
claim.brief.adrenal-incidentaloma.one-mg.limitation: Testing may be unwarranted in frail patients with limited life expectancy. An abnormal result requires contextual interpretation and does not by itself mandate adrenalectomy.
claim.brief.adrenal-incidentaloma.one-mg.applicablePopulation: Stable, nonfrail adults with an incidentally discovered adrenal mass at least 1 cm.

claim.brief.adrenal-incidentaloma.pheoch.statement: Before a management-changing biopsy of an indeterminate adrenal mass, pheochromocytoma should be excluded with plasma-free or urinary fractionated metanephrines; adrenal biopsy is otherwise rarely appropriate.
claim.brief.adrenal-incidentaloma.pheoch.limitation: This is restricted to imaging not typical of a benign adenoma and a specific situation in which tissue would change management. It does not teach routine adrenal biopsy.
claim.brief.adrenal-incidentaloma.pheoch.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with an indeterminate adrenal lesion and a separate malignancy for which biopsy could change treatment.

claim.brief.mammary-paget.full-thickness.statement: Persistent unilateral nipple-areolar skin change suspicious for mammary Paget disease requires histologic verification with a biopsy that includes the full thickness of the involved skin, such as an adequate punch or wedge biopsy.
claim.brief.mammary-paget.full-thickness.limitation: No single technique succeeds in every case. A superficial shave can be insufficient, and persistent concern after a nondiagnostic specimen requires further evaluation.
claim.brief.mammary-paget.full-thickness.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent unilateral eczematous, crusted, eroded, or scaly nipple-areolar skin change.

claim.brief.mammary-paget.underlying-bre.statement: After mammary Paget disease is suspected or confirmed, mammography and breast ultrasound evaluate for underlying in situ or invasive carcinoma; breast MRI can be added when conventional imaging is negative or extent remains uncertain.
claim.brief.mammary-paget.underlying-bre.limitation: MRI is not the automatic first and only study. Imaging does not replace tissue diagnosis, and treatment depends on the underlying pathology and extent.
claim.brief.mammary-paget.underlying-bre.applicablePopulation: Adults with biopsy-confirmed mammary Paget disease who have not yet undergone breast imaging for underlying malignancy.

claim.brief.ibc.core-biopsy-confirmation.statement: Inflammatory breast cancer is a rapid clinical pattern of breast erythema and edema or peau d'orange affecting at least one-third of the breast, with a history no longer than six months, and requires pathologic confirmation of invasive carcinoma by breast core biopsy.
claim.brief.ibc.core-biopsy-confirmation.limitation: Dermal lymphatic tumor emboli support the diagnosis but are not required. Infection and other locally advanced cancers remain in the differential, so appearance alone is not pathologic confirmation.
claim.brief.ibc.core-biopsy-confirmation.applicablePopulation: Nonlactating adults with rapid diffuse inflammatory breast change and no drainable abscess.

claim.brief.ibc.trimodality-sequence.statement: Nonmetastatic inflammatory breast cancer is treated with multidisciplinary care beginning with neoadjuvant systemic therapy, followed by modified radical mastectomy and postmastectomy radiation when the patient remains an operative candidate.
claim.brief.ibc.trimodality-sequence.limitation: Systemic regimen and biomarker-directed treatment depend on phenotype and oncology assessment. This sequence is limited to stage III disease and is not automatically applied to stage IV disease.
claim.brief.ibc.trimodality-sequence.applicablePopulation: Adults with biopsy-confirmed stage III inflammatory breast cancer after distant staging.

claim.brief.aaa.one-time-ultrasound-scre.statement: Men age 65 through 75 who have ever smoked should receive one-time abdominal ultrasound screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm.
claim.brief.aaa.one-time-ultrasound-scre.limitation: This claim is limited to asymptomatic men with a smoking history and no prior screening; it does not define screening for other populations.
claim.brief.aaa.one-time-ultrasound-scre.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic men age 65-75 who have ever smoked and have not previously undergone AAA screening.

claim.brief.aaa.six-cm-elective-repair-r.statement: An acceptable-risk patient with an asymptomatic 6-cm fusiform abdominal aortic aneurysm should receive prompt vascular-surgery evaluation for elective repair rather than routine surveillance alone.
claim.brief.aaa.six-cm-elective-repair-r.limitation: Anatomy and specialist assessment determine open versus endovascular repair. Pain or suspected rupture requires emergency care rather than this outpatient pathway.
claim.brief.aaa.six-cm-elective-repair-r.applicablePopulation: Stable acceptable-risk men with a newly identified asymptomatic 6-cm fusiform AAA and no rupture features.

claim.brief.fecal-incontinence.first-lin.statement: Dietary and medical measures that improve bowel habits and stool consistency are first-line care for stable fecal incontinence.
claim.brief.fecal-incontinence.first-lin.limitation: No single diet, medication, dose, or regimen is universally appropriate; care should respond to the patient's stool pattern and contributors.
claim.brief.fecal-incontinence.first-lin.applicablePopulation: Stable adults presenting for initial management of fecal incontinence without an acute neurologic, infectious, or obstructive feature.

claim.brief.fecal-incontinence.endoanal-.statement: Endoanal ultrasound is a selected anatomy study when sphincter repair is being considered after appropriate evaluation for persistent fecal incontinence.
claim.brief.fecal-incontinence.endoanal-.limitation: A sphincter defect alone does not predict symptom severity or mandate an operation. Ultrasound is not a routine test for every patient with fecal incontinence.
claim.brief.fecal-incontinence.endoanal-.applicablePopulation: Adults with persistent fecal incontinence for whom specialist evaluation has identified possible sphincter injury and repair planning is under consideration.

claim.brief.h-pylori.active-infection-te.statement: A patient with uncomplicated peptic ulcer disease who has not been evaluated for Helicobacter pylori should receive an active-infection test such as a urea breath test or stool antigen test rather than antibody serology.
claim.brief.h-pylori.active-infection-te.limitation: PPIs, antibiotics, and bismuth can reduce test sensitivity. The authored patients have completed appropriate medication holds and have no bleeding or acute complication.
claim.brief.h-pylori.active-infection-te.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a known uncomplicated duodenal ulcer who need initial H. pylori evaluation.

claim.brief.h-pylori.test-of-cure-plan.statement: After H. pylori treatment, eradication should be confirmed with an active-infection test at least four weeks after antibiotics, with PPIs held for two weeks and antibiotics or bismuth held for four weeks.
claim.brief.h-pylori.test-of-cure-plan.limitation: This is a future follow-up plan. The game visit does not simulate treatment completion or the washout interval, and serology is not a test of cure.
claim.brief.h-pylori.test-of-cure-plan.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed H. pylori infection for whom treatment and subsequent eradication confirmation are being planned.

claim.brief.diverticulitis.first-present.statement: CT should confirm a first suspected presentation of acute diverticulitis and assess for complications when no prior imaging-confirmed diagnosis exists.
claim.brief.diverticulitis.first-present.limitation: This does not require CT for every recurrent classic episode after an established diagnosis and does not delay emergency treatment in an unstable patient.
claim.brief.diverticulitis.first-present.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a first suspected mild presentation of acute diverticulitis and no prior imaging-confirmed episode.

claim.brief.diverticulitis.selected-no-r.statement: Routine antibiotics can be omitted in selected immunocompetent, nonfrail outpatients with mild CT-confirmed uncomplicated diverticulitis, no systemic inflammation or high-risk imaging feature, oral-intake tolerance, and reliable follow-up.
claim.brief.diverticulitis.selected-no-r.limitation: This selection does not apply to complicated disease, immunocompromise, frailty, systemic inflammation, inability to tolerate intake, or unreliable follow-up.
claim.brief.diverticulitis.selected-no-r.applicablePopulation: Carefully selected stable outpatients with mild CT-confirmed uncomplicated diverticulitis.

claim.brief.thyroglossal-duct-cyst.ultra.statement: Ultrasound is an appropriate initial study for a suspected thyroglossal duct cyst and should document a normally located thyroid before excision is considered.
claim.brief.thyroglossal-duct-cyst.ultra.limitation: Adult cystic neck masses require careful differential diagnosis. Ultrasound findings must not be used to declare every midline mass benign.
claim.brief.thyroglossal-duct-cyst.ultra.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a mobile midline upper-neck mass and no acute airway or infectious feature.

claim.brief.thyroglossal-duct-cyst.sistr.statement: A benign-appearing symptomatic or recurrent thyroglossal duct cyst with a normal orthotopic thyroid and no active infection should be referred for elective Sistrunk procedure evaluation.
claim.brief.thyroglossal-duct-cyst.sistr.limitation: Active infection should be treated before surgery. The game refers to a specialist and does not teach procedural steps or an exact recurrence estimate.
claim.brief.thyroglossal-duct-cyst.sistr.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a bothersome or recurrent benign-characterized thyroglossal duct cyst and normal orthotopic thyroid tissue.

claim.brief.rectal-prolapse.dynamic-defe.statement: Dynamic fluoroscopic or MRI defecography can be used selectively when external full-thickness rectal prolapse is suspected but cannot be reproduced on examination and the result will guide planning.
claim.brief.rectal-prolapse.dynamic-defe.limitation: Defecography is not required for obvious visible prolapse. Internal intussusception is not interchangeable with external full-thickness prolapse.
claim.brief.rectal-prolapse.dynamic-defe.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a convincing history of external prolapse that is not visible during clinic examination.

claim.brief.rectal-prolapse.surgical-ref.statement: External full-thickness rectal prolapse should be referred for colorectal surgical evaluation because medical measures can palliate associated symptoms but do not correct the prolapse.
claim.brief.rectal-prolapse.surgical-ref.limitation: The operative approach depends on patient and anatomic factors. The game does not mark one competing repair technique as universally correct.
claim.brief.rectal-prolapse.surgical-ref.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with dynamically confirmed external full-thickness rectal prolapse.

claim.brief.eoe.multilevel-esophageal-bi.statement: Suspected eosinophilic esophagitis should be evaluated by upper endoscopy with at least six targeted esophageal biopsies obtained from at least two levels, interpreted with symptoms and exclusion of other causes.
claim.brief.eoe.multilevel-esophageal-bi.limitation: Endoscopic appearance alone is insufficient. The authored patient has no current food impaction or unstable illness.
claim.brief.eoe.multilevel-esophageal-bi.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with chronic solid-food dysphagia or food sticking suspicious for eosinophilic esophagitis.

claim.brief.eoe.dilation-plus-anti-infla.statement: Symptomatic fibrostenotic eosinophilic esophagitis can require esophageal dilation for narrowing together with anti-inflammatory treatment for the underlying disease.
claim.brief.eoe.dilation-plus-anti-infla.limitation: Dilation does not replace anti-inflammatory care. Several anti-inflammatory strategies can be valid, so the game does not force a single medication or diet.
claim.brief.eoe.dilation-plus-anti-infla.applicablePopulation: Adults with biopsy-supported eosinophilic esophagitis and a symptomatic fixed narrowing or fibrostenotic phenotype.

claim.ipaa.pouchitis-frequency.statement: In the approved UC/IPAA counseling scope, pouchitis is the inflammatory pouch complication used for the frequency comparison.
claim.ipaa.pouchitis-frequency.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata is not itself clinician approved; the exact question wording is separately approved.
claim.ipaa.pouchitis-frequency.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved clinic variants.

claim.bile-duct-cyst.type-iva-anatomy.statement: In the approved imaging-classification scope, Type IVA is the multiple-cystic-dilatation pattern involving both intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.
claim.bile-duct-cyst.type-iva-anatomy.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata is not itself clinician approved; the exact question wording is separately approved.
claim.bile-duct-cyst.type-iva-anatomy.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved clinic variants.

claim.anal-hsil.hrhpv-association.statement: In the approved pathology-follow-up scope, anal HSIL is associated with persistent high-risk HPV; HIV is not the etiologic viral answer tested here.
claim.anal-hsil.hrhpv-association.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata is not itself clinician approved; the exact question wording is separately approved.
claim.anal-hsil.hrhpv-association.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved clinic variants.

claim.early.choledocholithiasis.intermed.statement: A stable patient with intermediate likelihood of a common-bile-duct stone can undergo MRCP to confirm or exclude a duct stone while avoiding diagnostic ERCP.
claim.early.choledocholithiasis.intermed.limitation: EUS is an equally guideline-supported alternative; this family selects MRCP as the locally available noninvasive route.
claim.early.choledocholithiasis.intermed.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with intermediate-risk features and no cholangitis.

claim.early.choledocholithiasis.confirme.statement: A common-bile-duct stone confirmed on MRCP requires a therapeutic duct-clearance pathway; preoperative therapeutic ERCP is one accepted pathway when that sequence is selected locally.
claim.early.choledocholithiasis.confirme.limitation: Postoperative ERCP and laparoscopic duct treatment are also valid according to local expertise; the cases explicitly select the preoperative endoscopic pathway.
claim.early.choledocholithiasis.confirme.applicablePopulation: Stable treatment candidates with a confirmed duct stone before planned cholecystectomy.

claim.early.bile-leak.ce-mrcp-anatomic-l.statement: After CT assesses postoperative collections, contrast-enhanced MRCP with a hepatobiliary agent can anatomically localize a suspected bile leak and evaluate duct continuity; scintigraphy can demonstrate active leakage but has limited spatial detail.
claim.early.bile-leak.ce-mrcp-anatomic-l.limitation: The dedicated hepatobiliary-contrast study is a distinct external service; this claim does not make MRCP the first test in an unstable patient.
claim.early.bile-leak.ce-mrcp-anatomic-l.applicablePopulation: Stable post-cholecystectomy adults after CT excludes an uncontrolled collection.

claim.early.bile-leak.minor-leak-ercp-st.statement: A persistent minor postoperative bile leak with preserved common-duct continuity can be referred for ERCP with transpapillary plastic-stent treatment.
claim.early.bile-leak.minor-leak-ercp-st.limitation: Excludes sepsis, peritonitis, uncontrolled collections, and complete common-bile-duct or common-hepatic-duct transection.
claim.early.bile-leak.minor-leak-ercp-st.applicablePopulation: Stable patients with a persistent minor post-cholecystectomy leak and preserved duct continuity.

claim.early.pseudocyst.contrast-ct-chara.statement: Contrast-enhanced CT can characterize a post-pancreatitis fluid collection before drainage planning; a mature encapsulated homogeneous fluid collection without solid debris after interstitial edematous pancreatitis is compatible with a pancreatic pseudocyst rather than walled-off necrosis.
claim.early.pseudocyst.contrast-ct-chara.limitation: The case must exclude necrotizing pancreatitis, pseudoaneurysm, and suspicious neoplastic features; no diameter alone establishes a drainage indication.
claim.early.pseudocyst.contrast-ct-chara.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent symptoms after resolved interstitial edematous acute pancreatitis.

claim.early.pseudocyst.symptomatic-endos.statement: A symptomatic mature pancreatic pseudocyst with suitable apposition to the stomach or duodenum can be referred for EUS-guided endoscopic drainage when appropriate expertise and backup are available.
claim.early.pseudocyst.symptomatic-endos.limitation: Symptoms, maturity, and suitable anatomy are required; this is an external specialist referral and size alone is not an indication.
claim.early.pseudocyst.symptomatic-endos.applicablePopulation: Stable patients with a characterized symptomatic pseudocyst and suitable anatomy.

claim.early.gerd.off-ppi-reflux-monitori.statement: When GERD is suspected but unproven and endoscopy provides no objective reflux evidence, ambulatory reflux monitoring off acid-suppressive therapy can establish or refute GERD before invasive treatment.
claim.early.gerd.off-ppi-reflux-monitori.limitation: Testing on therapy answers a different question in established GERD; the case excludes alarm symptoms and unequivocal erosive disease.
claim.early.gerd.off-ppi-reflux-monitori.applicablePopulation: Stable adults considering antireflux surgery with typical symptoms and normal endoscopy.

claim.early.gerd.hrm-before-operative-pl.statement: After objective reflux is documented and antireflux surgery remains under consideration, high-resolution manometry should be completed before operative planning to exclude achalasia and absent contractility; manometry does not establish GERD.
claim.early.gerd.hrm-before-operative-pl.limitation: A normal manometry result does not obligate surgery or choose a specific operation.
claim.early.gerd.hrm-before-operative-pl.applicablePopulation: Adults with objectively documented reflux being evaluated for an antireflux procedure.

claim.early.pbh.completed-whipple-triad.statement: Post-bariatric hypoglycemia can be recognized when typical symptoms coincide with biochemically confirmed glucose below 3.0 mmol/L (54 mg/dL), preferably by venous plasma measurement, and symptoms improve after correction, completing Whipple's triad after alternative causes are considered.
claim.early.pbh.completed-whipple-triad.limitation: The current Society for Endocrinology guideline advises against dynamic provocation testing; an older guideline differs on mixed-meal testing, so no provocative test appears as an answer choice.
claim.early.pbh.completed-whipple-triad.applicablePopulation: Stable adults remotely post-bariatric surgery with spontaneous postmeal symptoms and no atypical fasting pattern.

claim.early.pbh.initial-dietary-care.statement: Initial management of confirmed post-bariatric hypoglycemia should include specialist bariatric-dietitian assessment and an individualized pattern of smaller, more frequent meals with controlled carbohydrate portions and lower-glycemic carbohydrate choices.
claim.early.pbh.initial-dietary-care.limitation: Evidence is based largely on small or uncontrolled dietary studies; no exact gram target or interval is taught.
claim.early.pbh.initial-dietary-care.applicablePopulation: Cooperative stable adults with confirmed PBH after the acute episode has resolved.

claim.lynch-tumor.universal-mmr-screenin.statement: MMR IHC or MSI tumor testing can screen a newly diagnosed colorectal cancer for a possible Lynch-syndrome signal. Tumor screening is not germline testing and does not itself diagnose Lynch syndrome.
claim.lynch-tumor.universal-mmr-screenin.limitation: Institutional pathways vary, and a screening result requires interpretation rather than a hereditary diagnosis.
claim.lynch-tumor.universal-mmr-screenin.applicablePopulation: Adults with newly diagnosed colorectal cancer and no prior tumor MMR evaluation.

claim.lynch-tumor.genetics-counseling-af.statement: After a Lynch-suggestive tumor result, genetics counseling and germline-testing discussion are appropriate before assigning an inherited syndrome or family testing plan.
claim.lynch-tumor.genetics-counseling-af.limitation: MSH2/MSH6 loss can have germline, somatic, or EPCAM-related explanations; the case does not select a specific panel or result.
claim.lynch-tumor.genetics-counseling-af.applicablePopulation: Adults with colorectal-tumor IHC showing MSH2 and MSH6 loss with retained internal controls.

claim.chronic-anal-fissure.topical-ccb-f.statement: For a typical chronic anal fissure, topical calcium-channel-blocker treatment is an appropriate first-line pharmacologic option with comparable efficacy and fewer adverse effects than topical nitrates.
claim.chronic-anal-fissure.topical-ccb-f.limitation: No drug, concentration, schedule, duration, or individual contraindication is taught.
claim.chronic-anal-fissure.topical-ccb-f.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with clinician-characterized chronic midline anal fissure.

claim.chronic-anal-fissure.selected-lis-.statement: After failed appropriate medical treatment, lateral internal sphincterotomy can be discussed for selected chronic anal fissure when baseline fecal incontinence and stated continence-risk history are absent.
claim.chronic-anal-fissure.selected-lis-.limitation: LIS requires individualized continence counseling and is not suitable for every patient.
claim.chronic-anal-fissure.selected-lis-.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with chronic fissure persistent after documented medical treatment and no described continence risk.

claim.cutaneous-scc.biopsy-for-diagnosis.statement: A lesion suspected to be cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma should have biopsy adequate for diagnosis and risk assessment; the selected technique depends on lesion features and location.
claim.cutaneous-scc.biopsy-for-diagnosis.limitation: This does not require one biopsy technique for every lesion.
claim.cutaneous-scc.biopsy-for-diagnosis.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a suspicious keratotic skin lesion and no tissue diagnosis.

claim.cutaneous-scc.risk-directed-surger.statement: Standard excision with histologic margin assessment is appropriate for low-risk primary cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, whereas high-risk disease should be evaluated for Mohs micrographic surgery.
claim.cutaneous-scc.risk-directed-surger.limitation: Risk classification must be explicit; location alone is not a universal Mohs indication.
claim.cutaneous-scc.risk-directed-surger.applicablePopulation: Adults with pathology-confirmed localized cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.

claim.cutaneous-scc.pathology-risk-featu.statement: Poor differentiation and perineural invasion are high-risk pathological features in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; their absence in a shallow well-differentiated primary supports the constrained low-risk teaching case.
claim.cutaneous-scc.pathology-risk-featu.limitation: Formal risk assessment uses multiple clinical and pathological features; this claim does not create a complete staging system.
claim.cutaneous-scc.pathology-risk-featu.applicablePopulation: Localized pathology-confirmed cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma in the authored clinic cases.

claim.venous-leg-ulcer.arterial-assessme.statement: Arterial status should be assessed before selecting compression for a suspected venous leg ulcer because coexisting arterial disease changes compression safety and type.
claim.venous-leg-ulcer.arterial-assessme.limitation: ABI can be unreliable with noncompressible arteries and this teaching does not prescribe a numeric cutoff.
claim.venous-leg-ulcer.arterial-assessme.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a suspected venous leg ulcer and no acute limb ischemia.

claim.venous-leg-ulcer.compression-after.statement: Compression therapy improves healing of an active venous leg ulcer when assessment supports adequate arterial perfusion and compression use.
claim.venous-leg-ulcer.compression-after.limitation: This claim does not prescribe compression pressure, wrap type, or mixed arterial-venous management.
claim.venous-leg-ulcer.compression-after.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with active venous leg ulcer and returned adequate arterial assessment.

claim.elective-splenectomy.vaccine-revie.statement: Before elective splenectomy, indicated pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Hib vaccines should be reviewed and given at least 14 days before surgery when possible.
claim.elective-splenectomy.vaccine-revie.limitation: This does not reproduce product schedules or delay an urgent operation.
claim.elective-splenectomy.vaccine-revie.applicablePopulation: Stable adults preparing for elective splenectomy.

claim.asplenia.fever-immediate-emergency.statement: Fever in a person with impaired splenic function requires immediate emergency assessment; a patient-specific standby oral antibiotic plan does not replace emergency presentation or prompt parenteral treatment after evaluation.
claim.asplenia.fever-immediate-emergency.limitation: The case does not select a drug, dose, diagnosis, or outpatient test pathway.
claim.asplenia.fever-immediate-emergency.applicablePopulation: Known asplenic adults with new fever.

claim.sbo.ct-transition-pattern.statement: A completed CT showing proximal small-bowel dilation, a transition point, and distal decompression supports mechanical SBO.
claim.sbo.ct-transition-pattern.limitation: CT interpretation must be integrated with clinical assessment.
claim.sbo.ct-transition-pattern.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected mechanical SBO and completed CT imaging.

claim.sbo.ct-ischemia-limit.statement: A mechanical transition pattern does not by itself establish or exclude bowel ischemia; clinical and additional CT danger features determine concern.
claim.sbo.ct-ischemia-limit.limitation: No single omitted sign is used to declare bowel viability.
claim.sbo.ct-ischemia-limit.applicablePopulation: Adults with CT evidence of SBO.

claim.sbo.urgent-escalation-features.statement: Peritonitis or concern for strangulation or ischemia in SBO requires urgent surgical evaluation without a routine outpatient testing delay.
claim.sbo.urgent-escalation-features.limitation: Stable nonoperative inpatient algorithms are outside this clinic objective.
claim.sbo.urgent-escalation-features.applicablePopulation: Adults with SBO and clinical danger features.

claim.primary-midline-hernia.clinical-re.statement: Most umbilical and epigastric hernias are diagnosed clinically; targeted ultrasound or CT can clarify an inconclusive examination.
claim.primary-midline-hernia.clinical-re.limitation: No unsourced distinction from rectus diastasis is taught.
claim.primary-midline-hernia.clinical-re.applicablePopulation: Adults with a suspected primary umbilical or epigastric hernia.

claim.primary-midline-hernia.symptomatic.statement: A stable symptomatic umbilical or epigastric hernia supports individualized elective repair discussion.
claim.primary-midline-hernia.symptomatic.limitation: The guideline reports limited evidence for many technique details; no universal technique is claimed.
claim.primary-midline-hernia.symptomatic.applicablePopulation: Adults with reducible symptomatic primary midline hernias.

claim.primary-midline-hernia.urgent-boun.statement: Acute nonreducibility with severe pain, vomiting, obstruction, or skin compromise requires urgent surgical assessment rather than elective counseling.
claim.primary-midline-hernia.urgent-boun.limitation: The objective teaches disposition, not operative technique.

claim.varicose.reflux-duplex.statement: Duplex ultrasound with reflux assessment is the diagnostic test of choice for evaluating symptomatic lower-extremity chronic venous reflux.
claim.varicose.reflux-duplex.limitation: The existing service must be labeled for reflux assessment, not only acute DVT compression.
claim.varicose.reflux-duplex.applicablePopulation: Adults with symptomatic varicose veins being evaluated for treatment.

claim.varicose.intervention-referral.statement: For symptomatic axial superficial reflux in an intervention candidate who wants treatment, specialist superficial venous intervention assessment is preferred to mandatory long-term compression.
claim.varicose.intervention-referral.limitation: The exact procedure depends on specialist anatomy and assessment.
claim.varicose.intervention-referral.applicablePopulation: Adults with symptomatic axial superficial reflux who are intervention candidates.

claim.varicose.conservative-boundary.statement: Conservative care remains reasonable when preference, comorbidity, mobility, anatomy, or resources weigh against intervention.
claim.varicose.conservative-boundary.limitation: No universal garment or duration is prescribed.
claim.varicose.conservative-boundary.applicablePopulation: Adults with stable symptomatic varicose veins.

claim.dfi.clinical-recognition.statement: Diabetes-related foot soft-tissue infection is diagnosed clinically from local or systemic inflammatory findings; colonization alone does not establish infection.
claim.dfi.clinical-recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with diabetes and a foot wound.

claim.dfi.initial-escalation.statement: Severe infection or moderate infection with important morbidity warrants hospital consideration; gangrene, deep abscess, necrotizing infection, compartment syndrome, or severe ischemia warrants urgent surgical consultation.
claim.dfi.initial-escalation.limitation: The clinic objective stops at recognition and external escalation.
claim.dfi.initial-escalation.applicablePopulation: Adults with diabetes-related foot infection and danger features.

claim.dfu.no-antibiotics-uninfected.statement: Systemic or local antibiotics should not be used for a clinically uninfected diabetic foot ulcer solely to prevent infection or promote healing.
claim.dfu.no-antibiotics-uninfected.limitation: External multidisciplinary foot care remains required; no onsite wound service is implied.
claim.dfu.no-antibiotics-uninfected.applicablePopulation: Adults with a clinically uninfected diabetes-related foot ulcer.

claim.burn.superficial-partial-depth.statement: A superficial partial-thickness burn is typically moist, red, blanching, blistered, and very painful; depth can evolve and requires reassessment.
claim.burn.superficial-partial-depth.limitation: Individual findings are interpreted together rather than as absolute rules.

claim.burn.deeper-depth-contrast.statement: Deep partial-thickness burns tend to be paler or drier, less blanching, and less sensate; full-thickness burns are dry or leathery, nonblanching, and insensate.
claim.burn.deeper-depth-contrast.limitation: Burn depth can be mixed or evolve.

claim.burn.referral-boundary.statement: Burn-center consultation or transfer depends on depth, extent, special location, mechanism, inhalation concern, comorbidity, pain, local resources, and associated trauma; consultation does not make every small burn an automatic transfer.
claim.burn.referral-boundary.limitation: No unsourced numeric threshold or general treatment algorithm is taught.
claim.burn.referral-boundary.applicablePopulation: Adults with burns evaluated in a general clinic or emergency handoff.

claim.burn.deep-hand-consult.statement: A deep partial-thickness burn involving the hand warrants burn-center consultation for transfer planning.
claim.burn.deep-hand-consult.limitation: Consultation and transfer are distinct decisions shaped by the receiving center and local resources.
claim.burn.deep-hand-consult.applicablePopulation: Adults with deep partial-thickness hand burns.

claim.burn.inhalation-emergency.statement: Facial burns with soot, hoarseness, or increasing work of breathing require emergency stabilization and burn-center coordination for possible inhalation injury.
claim.burn.inhalation-emergency.limitation: Airway stabilization must not wait for routine outpatient care.
claim.burn.inhalation-emergency.applicablePopulation: Adults with burns and possible inhalation injury.

claim.hs.pattern-recognition.statement: HS is recognized clinically by typical recurrent nodules, abscesses, tunnels, or scars in characteristic intertriginous sites with a relapsing course.
claim.hs.pattern-recognition.limitation: No single lesion alone establishes the longitudinal diagnosis.
claim.hs.pattern-recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with recurrent lesions in intertriginous skin.

claim.hs.multimodal-planning.statement: Recurrent or tunnel-forming HS needs severity-based longitudinal multimodal medical and procedural planning.
claim.hs.multimodal-planning.limitation: No specific drug regimen or universal operation is prescribed.

claim.hs.drainage-limitation.statement: Incision and drainage may relieve an acute collection but is not definitive control of chronic tunnel-forming HS.
claim.hs.drainage-limitation.limitation: Acute abscess assessment remains necessary when present.
claim.hs.drainage-limitation.applicablePopulation: Adults with HS and recurrent abscesses or tunnels.

claim.parastomal-hernia.recognition.statement: A dynamic peristomal bulge compatible with a fascial defect supports parastomal-hernia recognition; uncertainty or obstructive symptoms require further assessment.
claim.parastomal-hernia.recognition.limitation: The EHS source is a limited cross-check; detailed boundaries rely on the open mapping review.
claim.parastomal-hernia.recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with an established stoma and new peristomal contour change.

claim.parastomal-hernia.individualized-n.statement: Stable nonobstructed parastomal hernia symptoms may receive individualized appliance, support, activity, education, and external referral measures.
claim.parastomal-hernia.individualized-n.limitation: Evidence is limited; no universal garment or routine operation is supported.
claim.parastomal-hernia.individualized-n.applicablePopulation: Adults with a stable reducible parastomal hernia.

claim.parastomal-hernia.urgent-boundary.statement: A painful nonreducible parastomal bulge with vomiting or reduced output requires urgent surgical evaluation for obstruction or ischemia.
claim.parastomal-hernia.urgent-boundary.limitation: No clinic maneuver should delay transfer.
claim.parastomal-hernia.urgent-boundary.applicablePopulation: Adults with a stoma and acute obstructive features.

claim.stoma-prolapse.assessment.statement: A prolapsed stoma requires prompt assessment of reducibility, bowel viability, output or obstruction, pain, and appliance function.
claim.stoma-prolapse.assessment.limitation: Evidence quality for many reduction techniques is low.
claim.stoma-prolapse.assessment.applicablePopulation: Adults with an established stoma and elongated protruding bowel.

claim.stoma-prolapse.nonurgent-boundary.statement: A viable reducible stoma prolapse can follow a nonemergency external colorectal and stoma-specialist pathway.
claim.stoma-prolapse.nonurgent-boundary.limitation: No specific reduction method or operation is prescribed.
claim.stoma-prolapse.nonurgent-boundary.applicablePopulation: Adults with a viable reducible productive stoma prolapse.

claim.stoma-prolapse.urgent-escalation.statement: Irreducible stoma prolapse with ischemia or obstruction requires urgent surgical evaluation.
claim.stoma-prolapse.urgent-escalation.limitation: Low-grade evidence is retained; reduction attempts must not delay escalation.
claim.stoma-prolapse.urgent-escalation.applicablePopulation: Adults with irreducible prolapse and viability or obstruction concerns.

claim.gcs.eye-mapping.statement: Eye response scores are E4 spontaneous, E3 to sound, E2 to pressure, and E1 none.
claim.gcs.eye-mapping.limitation: Official source family; independent corroboration limited.

claim.gcs.verbal-mapping.statement: Verbal response scores are V5 oriented, V4 confused, V3 words, V2 sounds, and V1 none when testable.
claim.gcs.verbal-mapping.limitation: Official source family; independent corroboration limited.
claim.gcs.verbal-mapping.applicablePopulation: Patients with a testable verbal response.

claim.gcs.motor-mapping.statement: Motor response scores are M6 obeys commands, M5 localizes, M4 normal flexion, M3 abnormal flexion, M2 extension, and M1 none.
claim.gcs.motor-mapping.limitation: Official source family; independent corroboration limited.

claim.gcs.complete-total.statement: A GCS total is the sum of eye, verbal, and motor scores only when all three components are testable; components should remain visible.
claim.gcs.complete-total.limitation: No severity band, prognosis, or treatment threshold is taught.
claim.gcs.complete-total.applicablePopulation: Patients with all three GCS components testable.

claim.gcs.verbal-nt.statement: When an interference genuinely prevents verbal testing, document V-NT with the reason and do not substitute 1 or 0 or report a misleading total.
claim.gcs.verbal-nt.limitation: A tracheostomy does not automatically make speech untestable.
claim.gcs.verbal-nt.applicablePopulation: Patients with an actual interference to verbal-response testing.

claim.lymphedema.secondary-recognition.statement: Chronic limb swelling after lymph-node or lymphatic-vessel treatment may represent secondary lymphedema when history and tissue findings are compatible.
claim.lymphedema.secondary-recognition.limitation: The diagnosis is not made solely from prior treatment history.
claim.lymphedema.secondary-recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with chronic limb swelling after lymphatic treatment.

claim.lymphedema.differential-safety.statement: Acute DVT, infection, recurrent malignancy, and systemic causes must be considered and investigated when the tempo or associated findings indicate them.
claim.lymphedema.differential-safety.limitation: Testing is driven by the differential rather than ordered routinely for every stable case.
claim.lymphedema.differential-safety.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established secondary lymphedema.

claim.lymphedema.early-pitting.statement: Early secondary lymphedema may remain soft and pitting before later tissue changes develop.
claim.lymphedema.early-pitting.limitation: Pitting is compatible but not diagnostic by itself.
claim.lymphedema.early-pitting.applicablePopulation: Adults with early secondary limb lymphedema.

claim.lymphedema.late-fibrosis.statement: Long-standing secondary lymphedema can develop firm tissue and skin thickening consistent with fibrotic change.
claim.lymphedema.late-fibrosis.limitation: Chronic firmness still requires assessment for other causes when the pattern changes.
claim.lymphedema.late-fibrosis.applicablePopulation: Adults with chronic secondary limb lymphedema.

claim.lymphedema.decongestive-referral.statement: Established lymphedema is managed with individualized decongestive care using fitted compression, exercise, skin care, and manual lymphatic drainage as appropriate.
claim.lymphedema.decongestive-referral.limitation: Evidence and response vary; no universal garment, pressure, modality, or guaranteed response is claimed.
claim.lymphedema.decongestive-referral.applicablePopulation: Adults with stable established secondary lymphedema.

claim.php.recognition.statement: Persistent pain after inguinal-hernia repair requires focused history and examination, pain mapping, and reassessment for recurrence and other causes; a compatible neuropathic distribution supports but does not alone prove a nerve mechanism.
claim.php.recognition.limitation: No single symptom proves a named nerve lesion.
claim.php.recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with persistent pain after inguinal-hernia repair.

claim.php.block-evaluation.statement: A specialist-performed local-anesthetic trigger-point or peripheral nerve block may add diagnostic information, but evidence is very low and no technique or response is guaranteed.
claim.php.block-evaluation.limitation: External specialist assessment only; no treatment ladder or guaranteed response.
claim.php.block-evaluation.applicablePopulation: Adults with persistent focal pain after recurrence and other causes are reassessed.

claim.spigelian.anatomy-recognition.statement: Spigelian hernia occurs through the Spigelian fascia along the lateral ventral abdominal wall; examination, ultrasonography, or CT may establish the diagnosis.
claim.spigelian.anatomy-recognition.limitation: Single-guideline evidence; no imaging test is mandatory when examination is clear.
claim.spigelian.anatomy-recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with a suspected lateral ventral abdominal-wall defect.

claim.spigelian.repair-referral.statement: A confirmed Spigelian hernia supports surgical repair discussion, but evidence is insufficient to prescribe one open or laparoscopic technique for every patient.
claim.spigelian.repair-referral.limitation: Urgent incarceration or obstruction requires emergency assessment.

claim.mesh.deep-pattern.statement: Prosthetic mesh infection may present as a chronic or indolent deep process with sinus drainage, collection, fistula, or systemic infection rather than superficial incisional erythema alone.
claim.mesh.deep-pattern.limitation: Single consensus source; findings require clinical correlation.
claim.mesh.deep-pattern.applicablePopulation: Adults after hernia repair with implanted mesh.

claim.mesh.source-control.statement: Suspected deep mesh infection needs prompt specialist source-control evaluation; treatment is individualized and failed conservative management may require removal, so removal is not automatic.
claim.mesh.source-control.limitation: Exact antibiotics and operative technique are outside scope.
claim.mesh.source-control.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected deep prosthetic mesh infection.

claim.cirrhosis.multifactor-risk.statement: Perioperative risk in cirrhosis depends on liver severity, portal hypertension and decompensation, procedure type, comorbidity, and center experience; no one score or laboratory value captures the whole decision.
claim.cirrhosis.multifactor-risk.limitation: Single expert-review source; no fixed mortality estimate is taught.
claim.cirrhosis.multifactor-risk.applicablePopulation: Adults with cirrhosis being considered for nonhepatic surgery.

claim.cirrhosis.optimize-decompensation.statement: Active decompensation supports multidisciplinary optimization before proceeding with a nonurgent elective plan; deferral is an inferred case-specific boundary rather than an automatic prohibition.
claim.cirrhosis.optimize-decompensation.limitation: Urgent surgical emergencies require immediate assessment despite elevated risk.
claim.cirrhosis.optimize-decompensation.applicablePopulation: Adults with cirrhosis and a proposed nonurgent elective operation.

claim.ptld.pattern.statement: PTLD is heterogeneous; in a solid-organ recipient, unexplained fever, lymphadenopathy, an extranodal mass, organ dysfunction, or rising EBV viremia should prompt evaluation while infection and rejection remain mimics.
claim.ptld.pattern.limitation: The list is nonexhaustive and no one feature establishes PTLD.
claim.ptld.pattern.applicablePopulation: Solid-organ transplant recipients with otherwise unexplained concerning findings.

claim.ptld.tissue.statement: Tissue pathology is required to diagnose and classify suspected PTLD; EBV DNA and imaging are supportive and do not replace histopathologic diagnosis.
claim.ptld.tissue.limitation: No biopsy technique, staging system, surveillance cutoff, or treatment regimen is taught.

claim.dtc.preop-ultrasound.statement: Malignant thyroid cytology or molecular findings warrant preoperative central and lateral neck ultrasonography to assess cervical nodes and gross local extension.
claim.dtc.preop-ultrasound.limitation: No unchecked numeric node threshold is taught.
claim.dtc.preop-ultrasound.applicablePopulation: Adults proceeding toward surgery for differentiated thyroid cancer confirmed by cytology or molecular findings.

claim.dtc.lobectomy-boundary.statement: For a patient who has chosen surgery for a differentiated thyroid cancer measuring 2 cm or less, confined to one lobe without gross extension or nodal disease, lobectomy is an eligible initial option.
claim.dtc.lobectomy-boundary.limitation: This exact boundary applies only to the stated low-risk unilateral profile and does not make lobectomy mandatory.
claim.dtc.lobectomy-boundary.applicablePopulation: Adults choosing surgery for unilateral intrathyroidal DTC measuring 2 cm or less without gross extension or nodal disease.

claim.dtc.extent.statement: Initial thyroid surgical extent is individualized from tumor extent and laterality, nodal or distant disease, recurrence considerations, future treatment needs, and patient preferences.
claim.dtc.extent.limitation: No operation is selected from age alone or mandated for every DTC.
claim.dtc.extent.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed differentiated thyroid cancer.

claim.discharge.pathologic-pattern.statement: Spontaneous unilateral single-duct serous or bloody discharge is concerning for a pathologic process, whereas bilateral multiduct discharge elicited with compression more often follows a physiologic pattern.
claim.discharge.pathologic-pattern.limitation: Pattern classification does not itself establish etiology.

claim.discharge.imaging.statement: Clearly physiologic discharge generally does not need diagnostic imaging; pathologic discharge warrants age- and context-appropriate diagnostic mammography or DBT with targeted ultrasonography as applicable.
claim.discharge.imaging.limitation: Only directly supported adult contexts are authored; rating tables are not reproduced.
claim.discharge.imaging.applicablePopulation: Adults with physiologic or pathologic nipple-discharge patterns.

claim.nact.response-mapping.statement: After neoadjuvant systemic therapy, operative planning integrates original disease distribution, current breast and axillary examination, post-treatment imaging, and localization of the residual lesion or original marker when needed.
claim.nact.response-mapping.limitation: Expert-informed society resource guides; no imaging modality is universal.
claim.nact.response-mapping.applicablePopulation: Adult women with known noninflammatory breast cancer after completed neoadjuvant therapy.

claim.nact.bcs-selection.statement: Selected noninflammatory breast cancer may remain eligible for breast-conserving surgery after adequate response when residual extent can be localized and acceptable conservation, margins, radiotherapy, and patient preference align.
claim.nact.bcs-selection.limitation: Response alone does not prove eligibility or permit omission of surgery; inflammatory breast cancer is excluded.
claim.nact.bcs-selection.applicablePopulation: Adult women with noninflammatory breast cancer after neoadjuvant therapy.

claim.nact.oncoplastic-selection.statement: An oncoplastic breast-conserving approach can remain an option for selected localized residual disease when a wider resection is needed and negative margins with acceptable cosmesis appear feasible.
claim.nact.oncoplastic-selection.limitation: Expert-informed society resource guide; this does not make oncoplastic conservation suitable for every response pattern.
claim.nact.oncoplastic-selection.applicablePopulation: Adult women with localized noninflammatory breast cancer after neoadjuvant therapy.

claim.bcc.pattern.statement: A slowly enlarging pearly or translucent papule or nodule, often with telangiectasia or ulceration, is concerning for BCC and warrants diagnostic confirmation; a scar-like plaque can represent morpheaform BCC.
claim.bcc.pattern.limitation: Clinical appearance raises concern but does not establish histology.
claim.bcc.pattern.applicablePopulation: Adults with a new or changing skin lesion.

claim.bcc.local-invasion.statement: BCC usually grows locally and can cause substantial destructive morbidity if neglected or recurrent.
claim.bcc.local-invasion.limitation: No rate or timeline is asserted.

claim.bcc.rare-metastasis.statement: Metastasis from BCC is rare, but this does not minimize locally advanced disease or remove the need for care.

claim.nutrition.screen.statement: Nutritional status should be assessed before major surgery with a structured clinical process; albumin alone is not treated as a nutrition diagnosis.
claim.nutrition.screen.limitation: Single older permitted guideline; no proprietary screening tool or exact cutoff is reproduced.

claim.nutrition.referral.statement: Identified preoperative nutritional risk supports dietitian and perioperative-team assessment with an individualized nutrition plan.
claim.nutrition.referral.limitation: No universal supplement, formula, or duration is prescribed.

claim.nutrition.oral-enteral.statement: When the gastrointestinal tract functions, oral intake and oral supplements are preferred first, with enteral nutrition used when oral intake is inadequate.
claim.nutrition.oral-enteral.applicablePopulation: Nutritionally at-risk adult surgical patients with a functional gastrointestinal tract.

claim.nutrition.pn-boundary.statement: Parenteral nutrition is reserved for situations in which oral and enteral routes are infeasible, contraindicated, or insufficient.
claim.nutrition.pn-boundary.limitation: No fixed timing, formulation, or dose is taught.
claim.nutrition.pn-boundary.applicablePopulation: Adult surgical patients needing nutrition support.

claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-two-mm.statement: A 2-mm negative margin is adequate for pure DCIS treated with breast-conserving surgery and whole-breast irradiation.
claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-two-mm.limitation: Scoped to pure DCIS with whole-breast irradiation.
claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-two-mm.applicablePopulation: Adults with pure DCIS treated with breast conservation and whole-breast irradiation.

claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-no-routine-wide.statement: Routine re-excision to obtain a margin wider than 2 mm does not improve the supported breast-conservation outcome for pure DCIS treated with whole-breast irradiation.
claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-no-routine-wide.limitation: Does not apply to tumor on ink or an unassessed residual imaging abnormality.
claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-no-routine-wide.applicablePopulation: Adults with pure DCIS and a negative margin of at least 2 mm.

claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-narrow-individu.statement: A negative DCIS margin below 2 mm requires individualized re-excision judgment rather than automatic mastectomy.
