claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-narrow-individu.limitation: Decision incorporates extent, location, residual imaging and cosmetic consequences.
claim.gs028c.dcis.margin-narrow-individu.applicablePopulation: Adults with pure DCIS, a negative margin below 2 mm, and planned whole-breast irradiation.

claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-mastectomy.statement: Sentinel-node biopsy is ordinarily performed with mastectomy for pure DCIS because later lymphatic mapping may be unreliable.
claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-mastectomy.limitation: Single current society source; standard setting without a planned delayed magnetic-tracer strategy.
claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-mastectomy.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing mastectomy for pure DCIS.

claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-omit-bcs.statement: Routine axillary surgery is generally omitted for pure DCIS treated with uncomplicated breast-conserving surgery when invasion is not suspected.
claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-omit-bcs.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing routine breast conservation for pure DCIS without concern for invasion.

claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-risk-setting.statement: Sentinel-node biopsy is appropriate when the planned DCIS operation will compromise later mapping or when occult invasion is meaningfully suspected.
claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-risk-setting.limitation: Single current society source; case-specific judgment remains required.
claim.gs028c.dcis.axilla-risk-setting.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing DCIS surgery with threatened future mapping or concern for occult invasion.

claim.gs028c.palpable.targeted-us.statement: A persistent palpable breast finding in an adult at least 40 years old warrants targeted ultrasonography of the exact clinical area when diagnostic mammography is negative.
claim.gs028c.palpable.targeted-us.limitation: Single current specialty guideline; this does not endorse blanket supplemental screening ultrasound for breast density alone.
claim.gs028c.palpable.targeted-us.applicablePopulation: Adults age 40 or older with a persistent palpable breast finding and negative diagnostic mammography.

claim.gs028c.palpable.biopsy.statement: A clinically suspicious persistent palpable breast mass requires tissue diagnosis even when diagnostic mammography and targeted ultrasonography are negative.
claim.gs028c.palpable.biopsy.limitation: Single current specialty guideline; biopsy technique depends on whether an imaging target exists and local specialist assessment.
claim.gs028c.palpable.biopsy.applicablePopulation: Adults with a persistently suspicious palpable breast mass despite negative mammography and targeted ultrasound.

claim.gs028c.polyp.low-risk.statement: Complete endoscopic excision can be definitive for a malignant colon polyp that is well or moderately differentiated, has no LVI or PNI, no or low budding, a clearly negative margin, and less than 1 mm of submucosal invasion.
claim.gs028c.polyp.low-risk.limitation: Single current society guideline; every favorable feature must be established in an adequate specimen.
claim.gs028c.polyp.low-risk.applicablePopulation: Adults with a completely excised malignant colon polyp.

claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-margin.statement: A malignant colon polyp with a positive or indeterminate margin warrants oncologic segmental-resection assessment when the patient is fit.
claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-margin.limitation: Single current society guideline; operative fitness and preferences remain individualized.
claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-margin.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with a malignant colon polyp and positive or indeterminate margin.

claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-grade.statement: Poor differentiation in a malignant colon polyp warrants oncologic segmental-resection assessment when the patient is fit.
claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-grade.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with a poorly differentiated malignant colon polyp.

claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-lvi.statement: Lymphovascular invasion in a malignant colon polyp warrants oncologic segmental-resection assessment when the patient is fit.
claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-lvi.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with LVI in a malignant colon polyp.

claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-budding.statement: High tumor budding in a malignant colon polyp is an adverse feature supporting oncologic segmental-resection assessment when the patient is fit.
claim.gs028c.polyp.adverse-budding.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with high tumor budding in a malignant colon polyp.

claim.gs028c.dialysis.protein.statement: A hospitalized adult without acute or critical illness who has kidney failure and receives conventional intermittent chronic KRT generally requires at least 1.2 g protein/kg/day using an appropriate reference weight.
claim.gs028c.dialysis.protein.limitation: Single current society guideline; not a blanket outpatient, critical-care, or predialysis target.
claim.gs028c.dialysis.protein.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults without acute or critical illness who receive conventional intermittent chronic KRT and require nutrition support.

claim.gs028c.dialysis.no-overfeeding.statement: Calories should not exceed assessed energy needs merely to force positive nitrogen balance in hospitalized kidney disease.
claim.gs028c.dialysis.no-overfeeding.limitation: Single current society guideline; energy needs and tolerance remain individualized.
claim.gs028c.dialysis.no-overfeeding.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults with kidney disease receiving nutrition support.

claim.gs028c.retained-antrum.recognition.statement: Retained antral mucosa after intended antrectomy with Billroth II reconstruction can sustain gastrin stimulation and recurrent marginal ulceration.
claim.gs028c.retained-antrum.recognition.limitation: Older narrative review plus an open surgical-atlas cross-check; recognition only, with no precise remnant localization or treatment recommendation authored.
claim.gs028c.retained-antrum.recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with recurrent ulceration after intended antrectomy and Billroth II reconstruction.

claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.ppi.statement: PPI therapy is the initial medical treatment for an uncomplicated marginal ulcer after gastric bypass.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.ppi.limitation: Single society literature review that is not a standard of care.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.ppi.applicablePopulation: Adults with an uncomplicated endoscopically confirmed marginal ulcer after gastric bypass.

claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.nsaid.statement: NSAID exposure should be stopped or replaced during treatment of a marginal ulcer after gastric bypass.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.nsaid.applicablePopulation: Adults with a marginal ulcer after gastric bypass who use NSAIDs.

claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.smoking.statement: Smoking-cessation support is part of initial management when a patient with a marginal ulcer after gastric bypass smokes.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.smoking.applicablePopulation: Adults who smoke and have a marginal ulcer after gastric bypass.

claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.h-pylori.statement: Identified H. pylori infection should be treated during medical management of a marginal ulcer after gastric bypass.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.h-pylori.limitation: This does not claim that H. pylori caused the ulcer.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.h-pylori.applicablePopulation: Adults with a marginal ulcer after gastric bypass and identified H. pylori infection.

claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.complication.statement: Bleeding, perforation, obstruction, and refractory marginal ulcers require pathways beyond routine initial medical management.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.complication.limitation: The authored cases explicitly exclude these complications.
claim.gs028c.marginal-ulcer.complication.applicablePopulation: Adults with a marginal ulcer after gastric bypass.

claim.gs028c.appendicitis.ct-after-nondi.statement: For a hemodynamically stable, nonpregnant adult with ongoing diagnostic uncertainty after a nondiagnostic ultrasound, CT is an appropriate definitive imaging study for suspected appendicitis when MRI is not readily available.
claim.gs028c.appendicitis.ct-after-nondi.limitation: Ultrasound is a reasonable first study, and MRI is also definitive; each authored scenario therefore specifies a nondiagnostic ultrasound and lack of timely MRI access.
claim.gs028c.appendicitis.ct-after-nondi.applicablePopulation: Hemodynamically stable, nonpregnant adults with suspected appendicitis, persistent uncertainty after nondiagnostic ultrasound, and no timely MRI access.

claim.gs028c.appendicitis.appendicolith-.statement: Among adults choosing antibiotics for imaging-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis, an appendicolith is associated with a greater chance of complications or later appendectomy than no appendicolith.
claim.gs028c.appendicitis.appendicolith-.limitation: This risk modifier informs shared decision-making and is not an absolute prohibition on nonoperative care.
claim.gs028c.appendicitis.appendicolith-.applicablePopulation: Adults with imaging-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis who are considering an antibiotics-first strategy.

claim.gs028c.appendicitis.appendicolith-.statement: For an otherwise fit adult with uncomplicated appendicitis and an appendicolith, hospital surgical evaluation for appendectomy is favored over a routine antibiotics-only pathway.
claim.gs028c.appendicitis.appendicolith-.limitation: The SAGES recommendation for operative management is conditional, and patient circumstances and preferences still require shared decision-making.
claim.gs028c.appendicitis.appendicolith-.applicablePopulation: Otherwise fit adults with imaging-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis containing an appendicolith.

claim.gs028c.cholecystitis.hida-after-eq.statement: When acute calculous cholecystitis remains clinically suspected after equivocal ultrasonography, hepatobiliary scintigraphy is an appropriate clarifying study in selected patients when local resources permit.
claim.gs028c.cholecystitis.hida-after-eq.limitation: The guideline notes that HIDA use is constrained by time and resource availability; the claim does not require HIDA for every suspected case.
claim.gs028c.cholecystitis.hida-after-eq.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent clinical suspicion for acute calculous cholecystitis after equivocal ultrasonography and access to hepatobiliary scintigraphy.

claim.gs028c.cholecystitis.index-admissi.statement: A fit adult with confirmed acute calculous cholecystitis should receive hospital surgical care with laparoscopic cholecystectomy during the index admission rather than routine delayed interval surgery.
claim.gs028c.cholecystitis.index-admissi.limitation: Critical illness, septic shock, anesthetic contraindication, and lack of appropriate expertise require individualized alternatives.
claim.gs028c.cholecystitis.index-admissi.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with confirmed acute calculous cholecystitis and access to appropriate hospital surgical expertise.

claim.gs028c.pancreatitis.selective-earl.statement: Routine early contrast-enhanced CT is unnecessary when acute pancreatitis is already established clinically and the patient is improving without diagnostic uncertainty, organ failure, or signs of a complication.
claim.gs028c.pancreatitis.selective-earl.limitation: CT remains appropriate when the diagnosis is uncertain or the clinical course fails to improve or suggests a complication.
claim.gs028c.pancreatitis.selective-earl.applicablePopulation: Adults with clinically established mild acute pancreatitis who are improving without diagnostic uncertainty or complication signs.

claim.gs028c.pancreatitis.index-admissio.statement: For mild acute gallstone pancreatitis, laparoscopic cholecystectomy should occur during the index admission, preferably before discharge, when the patient is clinically improving and no local complication requires delay.
claim.gs028c.pancreatitis.index-admissio.limitation: This timing does not apply to severe pancreatitis or cases with persistent fluid collections or other complications that change operative timing.
claim.gs028c.pancreatitis.index-admissio.applicablePopulation: Adults recovering from mild acute gallstone pancreatitis without necrosis, persistent organ failure, or operative contraindication.

claim.gs028c.ali.category-one.statement: An acutely ischemic limb with intact sensation and motor function plus audible arterial and venous Doppler signals is viable rather than immediately threatened.
claim.gs028c.ali.category-one.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected acute limb ischemia.

claim.gs028c.ali.category-two-a.statement: Acute limb ischemia with sensory loss limited to the toes, no motor weakness, an absent arterial Doppler signal, and an audible venous signal is marginally threatened and salvageable with prompt treatment.
claim.gs028c.ali.category-two-a.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected acute limb ischemia.

claim.gs028c.ali.category-two-b.statement: Acute limb ischemia with sensory loss extending beyond the toes, mild or moderate motor weakness, an absent arterial Doppler signal, and an audible venous signal is immediately threatened and requires immediate revascularization for salvage.
claim.gs028c.ali.category-two-b.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected acute limb ischemia.

claim.gs028c.ali.category-three.statement: An anesthetic, paralyzed acutely ischemic limb with absent arterial and venous Doppler signals is irreversibly damaged and should not undergo attempted revascularization.
claim.gs028c.ali.category-three.limitation: Irreversibility requires the complete neurologic and Doppler pattern; absent pulses alone do not establish it.
claim.gs028c.ali.category-three.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected category III acute limb ischemia.

claim.gs028c.ali.ufh-unless-contraindica.statement: Systemic unfractionated heparin should be administered when acute limb ischemia is diagnosed unless anticoagulation is contraindicated.
claim.gs028c.ali.ufh-unless-contraindica.limitation: Active bleeding, high bleeding risk, aortic dissection, major vascular trauma, or prior heparin-induced thrombocytopenia can require withholding heparin or choosing an alternative.
claim.gs028c.ali.ufh-unless-contraindica.applicablePopulation: Adults with diagnosed acute limb ischemia.

claim.gs028c.ali.emergency-vascular-care.statement: Acute limb ischemia requires emergency assessment by a clinician able to determine viability and provide revascularization, with immediate transfer when that expertise is unavailable locally.
claim.gs028c.ali.emergency-vascular-care.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected acute limb ischemia.

claim.gs028c.ami.cta-without-delay.statement: CT angiography should be performed without delay when acute mesenteric ischemia is suspected.
claim.gs028c.ami.cta-without-delay.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected acute mesenteric ischemia.

claim.gs028c.ami.aki-does-not-delay-cta.statement: Acute kidney injury alone should not delay CTA when acute mesenteric ischemia is suspected because a missed or delayed diagnosis is more dangerous than the contrast exposure.
claim.gs028c.ami.aki-does-not-delay-cta.limitation: The receiving acute-care team should still optimize resuscitation and contrast safety without postponing the diagnostic study.
claim.gs028c.ami.aki-does-not-delay-cta.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected acute mesenteric ischemia and concurrent acute kidney injury.

claim.gs028c.ami.peritonitis-exploration.statement: Overt peritonitis in suspected acute mesenteric ischemia indicates likely bowel infarction and requires prompt operative exploration without additional diagnostic delay.
claim.gs028c.ami.peritonitis-exploration.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or confirmed acute mesenteric ischemia and overt peritonitis.

claim.gs028d.ards.permeability-edema.statement: ARDS produces inflammatory pulmonary edema through increased permeability of the alveolar-capillary barrier rather than through isolated elevation of hydrostatic pressure.
claim.gs028d.ards.permeability-edema.limitation: The mechanism is taught as a defining principle; individual patients may have additional hydrostatic or other contributors to pulmonary edema.
claim.gs028d.ards.permeability-edema.applicablePopulation: Adults with acute respiratory distress syndrome.

claim.gs028d.ards.predicted-body-weight-.statement: When an adult with ARDS receives invasive ventilation, tidal-volume selection is based on predicted body weight rather than current actual body weight.
claim.gs028d.ards.predicted-body-weight-.limitation: The authored objective tests the weight basis only and does not prescribe a universal numeric tidal volume or reproduce a calculation formula.
claim.gs028d.ards.predicted-body-weight-.applicablePopulation: Adults with ARDS receiving invasive mechanical ventilation.

claim.gs028d.bci.ecg-troponin-evaluation.statement: Adults with a mechanism concerning for blunt cardiac injury should undergo an admission ECG, and adding cardiac troponin improves the initial evaluation compared with ECG alone.
claim.gs028d.bci.ecg-troponin-evaluation.limitation: The optimal timing and serial schedule for troponin testing remain uncertain, so no assay cutoff or testing interval is authored.
claim.gs028d.bci.ecg-troponin-evaluation.applicablePopulation: Adults with blunt chest trauma concerning for blunt cardiac injury.

claim.gs028d.bci.abnormal-result-monitor.statement: A new ECG abnormality after suspected blunt cardiac injury, or an elevated troponin despite a normal ECG, warrants admission to a monitored hospital setting.
claim.gs028d.bci.abnormal-result-monitor.limitation: The guideline is from 2012, does not establish an optimal troponin timing schedule, and does not make every ECG abnormality diagnostic of structural cardiac injury.
claim.gs028d.bci.abnormal-result-monitor.applicablePopulation: Adults evaluated after blunt chest trauma concerning for blunt cardiac injury.

claim.gs028d.bci.normal-results-boundary.statement: When both the admission ECG and troponin I are normal after suspected blunt cardiac injury, blunt cardiac injury is ruled out for disposition purposes in the EAST pathway.
claim.gs028d.bci.normal-results-boundary.limitation: This disposition principle does not override another injury, symptom, or clinical reason for hospital admission; exact diagnostic-performance percentages are not asserted.
claim.gs028d.bci.normal-results-boundary.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected blunt cardiac injury and normal admission ECG and troponin I results.

claim.gs028d.head-injury.anticoagulant-c.statement: For an adult with mild traumatic brain injury who takes an anticoagulant, a usual clinical decision rule should not be used to exclude the need for head CT, and emergency imaging should be strongly considered.
claim.gs028d.head-injury.anticoagulant-c.limitation: The authored cases use warfarin or direct oral anticoagulants and do not extend the teaching point to aspirin alone; the exact scan decision remains a clinical judgment in emergency care.
claim.gs028d.head-injury.anticoagulant-c.applicablePopulation: Adults with mild traumatic brain injury who take warfarin or a direct oral anticoagulant.

claim.gs028d.pelvic-binder.greater-troch.statement: A pelvic binder used for suspected unstable pelvic-ring injury should be centered across the greater trochanters, rather than placed high over the iliac crests.
claim.gs028d.pelvic-binder.greater-troch.limitation: This anatomical placement principle is supported here by an older single guideline and is taught through retrospective EMS or hospital record review, not clinic resuscitation.
claim.gs028d.pelvic-binder.greater-troch.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving temporary pelvic stabilization for suspected unstable pelvic-ring injury.

claim.gs028d.acidosis.blood-gas.statement: When reduced plasma bicarbonate suggests metabolic acidosis, blood-gas assessment confirms the acidemia and identifies respiratory or mixed acid-base contributions.
claim.gs028d.acidosis.blood-gas.limitation: R1.1 is expert opinion; arterial sampling is not claimed universally superior.
claim.gs028d.acidosis.blood-gas.applicablePopulation: Adults with reduced plasma bicarbonate and suspected metabolic acidosis.

claim.gs028d.acidosis.corrected-gap.statement: In metabolic acidosis with low albumin, an albumin-corrected anion gap better assesses unmeasured anion accumulation than the uncorrected gap.
claim.gs028d.acidosis.corrected-gap.limitation: No correction formula or arithmetic threshold is taught; units and equations would require separate exact verification.
claim.gs028d.acidosis.corrected-gap.applicablePopulation: Adults with metabolic acidosis and hypoalbuminaemia.

claim.gs028d.hyperkalaemia.severe-transf.statement: Under the current UKKA adult pathway, a confirmed community potassium concentration of at least 6.5 mmol/L warrants immediate hospital assessment and treatment.
claim.gs028d.hyperkalaemia.severe-transf.limitation: This is a UK guideline threshold, not a universal jurisdictional rule or an exact arrhythmia probability.
claim.gs028d.hyperkalaemia.severe-transf.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed severe hyperkalaemia detected in the community.

claim.gs028d.hyperkalaemia.mechanisms.statement: In acute hyperkalaemia, intravenous calcium protects cardiac membrane physiology but does not lower serum potassium, whereas insulin with glucose shifts potassium into cells.
claim.gs028d.hyperkalaemia.mechanisms.limitation: The July 2026 calcium recommendation is 2C after no evidence for or against outcome benefit; no dose, timing, or survival claim is taught.
claim.gs028d.hyperkalaemia.mechanisms.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving hospital treatment for acute hyperkalaemia.

claim.gs028d.access.maturation-assessmen.statement: Clinical AV-access maturation assessment uses inspection, palpation, and auscultation; specialist ultrasound can supplement an examination that cannot establish maturation.
claim.gs028d.access.maturation-assessmen.limitation: No universal time interval, numeric flow threshold, or onsite specialist capability is asserted.
claim.gs028d.access.maturation-assessmen.applicablePopulation: Adults after creation of haemodialysis AV access.

claim.gs028d.access.dysfunction-referral.statement: New clinical or dialysis-performance evidence of AV-access dysfunction warrants access-team evaluation rather than routine imaging based only on the access being present.
claim.gs028d.access.dysfunction-referral.limitation: Asymptomatic surveillance benefit is uncertain; emergency bleeding and pseudoaneurysm meanings are outside this objective.
claim.gs028d.access.dysfunction-referral.applicablePopulation: Adults with a haemodialysis AV access and signs of dysfunction.

claim.gs028d.osa.validated-screen.statement: Validated preoperative screening can identify adults at increased probability of obstructive sleep apnoea for perioperative communication, but screening does not establish the diagnosis.
claim.gs028d.osa.validated-screen.limitation: No proprietary questionnaire, item wording, score cutoff, or guaranteed outcome benefit is reproduced.

claim.gs028d.mh.trigger-free-plan.statement: A patient with known or credibly documented malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility requires advance planning for trigger-free anaesthesia in a facility prepared to manage malignant hyperthermia.
claim.gs028d.mh.trigger-free-plan.limitation: Evidence relies substantially on expert opinion and case reports; no clinic anaesthetic, crisis algorithm, or dantrolene dose is taught.
claim.gs028d.mh.trigger-free-plan.applicablePopulation: Patients with known or credibly documented malignant-hyperthermia susceptibility.

claim.gs028d.frailty.validated-assessmen.statement: For an older adult preparing for elective major abdominal surgery, frailty should be assessed with a structured multidimensional instrument rather than inferred from chronological age or comorbidity count alone.
claim.gs028d.frailty.validated-assessmen.limitation: Consensus good-practice evidence with an independent low-quality consensus cross-check; no universal tool, cutoff, cancellation rule, or automatic intensive-care disposition is supported.
claim.gs028d.frailty.validated-assessmen.applicablePopulation: Older adults preparing for elective major abdominal surgery.

claim.gs028d.delirium.multicomponent-pla.statement: Surgical patients at risk for postoperative delirium should receive a tailored multidisciplinary multicomponent nonpharmacologic prevention plan from the perioperative hospital team.
claim.gs028d.delirium.multicomponent-pla.limitation: Components are individualized; no identical bundle, clinic monitoring capability, or guaranteed prevention is claimed.
claim.gs028d.delirium.multicomponent-pla.applicablePopulation: Adults at increased risk for postoperative delirium.

claim.gs028d.lung-screening.eligibility.statement: The USPSTF recommends annual low-dose CT for adults aged 50 through 80 years with at least 20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years, stopping after 15 quit-years or when health limits life expectancy or willingness or ability for curative lung surgery.
claim.gs028d.lung-screening.eligibility.limitation: Exact values are specific to the USPSTF framework; plain CT service is not substituted for external LDCT, and shared decision-making remains necessary.
claim.gs028d.lung-screening.eligibility.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic adults considered for USPSTF lung-cancer screening.

claim.gs028d.psp.recurrence-referral.statement: After an initial primary spontaneous pneumothorax, early thoracic-surgery discussion may be offered when recurrence prevention is an important patient priority.
claim.gs028d.psp.recurrence-referral.limitation: Conditional low-certainty recommendation; not a mandate and not extended to an initial secondary spontaneous pneumothorax.
claim.gs028d.psp.recurrence-referral.applicablePopulation: Stable adults after recovery from an initial primary spontaneous pneumothorax.

claim.gs028d.pleural-infection.drain-ref.statement: In suspected pleural infection with nonpurulent aspirate, pleural-fluid pH at or below 7.2 indicates high risk and supports hospital intercostal drainage when ultrasound shows sufficient safely accessible fluid.
claim.gs028d.pleural-infection.drain-ref.limitation: The threshold requires the complete infection, sample, and ultrasound context; drainage is hospital care and evidence comes from one copyrighted guideline.
claim.gs028d.pleural-infection.drain-ref.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected pleural infection and a nonpurulent diagnostic aspirate.

claim.gs028d.pleural-effusion.image-guid.statement: When diagnostic thoracentesis is indicated for an undiagnosed unilateral pleural effusion, the procedure should be image guided rather than performed blindly.
claim.gs028d.pleural-effusion.image-guid.limitation: Strong recommendation by consensus from one guideline; the clinic refers externally and does not perform the procedure.
claim.gs028d.pleural-effusion.image-guid.applicablePopulation: Adults requiring diagnostic thoracentesis for an undiagnosed unilateral pleural effusion.

claim.gs028e.imaging.ct-ionizing-xrays.statement: CT produces images using ionizing X-rays; omitting injected contrast does not remove the X-ray exposure inherent to CT.
claim.gs028e.imaging.ct-ionizing-xrays.limitation: A physical modality distinction only; no patient-specific radiation dose, organ-imaging preference, or numeric risk estimate is supplied.
claim.gs028e.imaging.ct-ionizing-xrays.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing medically indicated CT imaging.

claim.gs028e.imaging.ultrasound-acoustic.statement: Diagnostic ultrasound produces images using sound waves rather than ionizing radiation.
claim.gs028e.imaging.ultrasound-acoustic.limitation: Nonionizing does not establish that ultrasound is the correct examination for every clinical question or that unlimited exposure is harmless.

claim.gs028e.imaging.mri-magnetic-rf-non.statement: MRI produces images using magnetic fields and radiofrequency energy without ionizing radiation; this distinction does not eliminate its separate magnetic, device, and heating hazards.
claim.gs028e.imaging.mri-magnetic-rf-non.limitation: No universal imaging preference or contrast-safety guarantee is inferred from absence of ionizing radiation.

claim.gs028e.mri.device-specific-conditi.statement: MRI screening requires positive identification of an implanted device and verification that the proposed examination satisfies the device's MR safety labeling; a prior uneventful scan alone does not establish clearance for different conditions.
claim.gs028e.mri.device-specific-conditi.limitation: The cross-check is another FDA document, not an independent organization. The clinic must not independently clear an unidentified implant or impose a permanent ban on every implant.
claim.gs028e.mri.device-specific-conditi.applicablePopulation: Adults with implanted devices referred for MRI.

claim.gs028e.mri.cochlear-specific-instr.statement: Cochlear-implant MRI restrictions depend on the identified implant and its manufacturer's instructions; instructions for another model cannot be substituted.
claim.gs028e.mri.cochlear-specific-instr.limitation: Single device-specific federal source; no invented field-strength, bandaging, or magnet-removal instruction is authored.
claim.gs028e.mri.cochlear-specific-instr.applicablePopulation: Adults with cochlear implants considering MRI.

claim.gs028e.contrast.transient-warmth-p.statement: Brief isolated flushing or warmth during intravascular iodinated contrast administration is categorized as a physiologic reaction rather than an allergic-like reaction.
claim.gs028e.contrast.transient-warmth-p.limitation: Single society classification source. Applies only to the supplied isolated, transient, fully resolved event; no inference is made about future reaction risk or premedication.
claim.gs028e.contrast.transient-warmth-p.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a documented iodinated contrast event.

claim.gs028e.contrast.urticaria-allergic.statement: Urticaria following intravascular iodinated contrast is categorized as an allergic-like reaction, which does not by itself establish an IgE mechanism.
claim.gs028e.contrast.urticaria-allergic.limitation: Single society classification source; no treatment algorithm, exposure challenge, severity inference, or allergy-testing recommendation is supplied.
claim.gs028e.contrast.urticaria-allergic.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing documented iodinated contrast-associated hives.

claim.gs028e.contrast.extravasation-loca.statement: Contrast extravasation is escape of intravascular contrast into adjacent tissue and can produce local injection-site pain or swelling rather than isolated generalized warmth.
claim.gs028e.contrast.extravasation-loca.limitation: Single society source used to distinguish the supplied documented events; no severity, observation interval, or treatment algorithm is authored.
claim.gs028e.contrast.extravasation-loca.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a documented intravascular contrast event.

claim.gs028e.contrast.delayed-cutaneous-.statement: Delayed cutaneous contrast reactions produce a later skin eruption, which is distinct from isolated warmth during injection or urticaria documented during the injection itself.
claim.gs028e.contrast.delayed-cutaneous-.limitation: Single society source; no precise timing cutoff or immunologic mechanism is assigned to an individual event.
claim.gs028e.contrast.delayed-cutaneous-.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing the documented timing and features of a contrast event.

claim.gs028e.sglt2.ketoacidosis-without-.statement: SGLT2-inhibitor exposure can be associated with diabetic ketoacidosis despite glucose that is not markedly elevated; supplied ketone excess and metabolic acidosis support recognition, whereas glucose alone cannot exclude it.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.ketoacidosis-without-.limitation: Medication exposure is a clinically important association, not proof that every acidosis is drug-caused. No glucose, ketone, pH or bicarbonate cutoff is invented.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.ketoacidosis-without-.applicablePopulation: Adults with diabetes taking an SGLT2 inhibitor and compatible ketone/acidosis findings.

claim.gs028e.sglt2.ketoacidosis-precipit.statement: Surgery, reduced caloric intake, acute illness, and inadequate insulin are recognized precipitating contexts for ketoacidosis during SGLT2-inhibitor therapy.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.ketoacidosis-precipit.limitation: Context raises concern but does not diagnose ketoacidosis without supporting clinical and laboratory evidence; no risk probability is authored.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.ketoacidosis-precipit.applicablePopulation: Adults taking an SGLT2 inhibitor around illness, fasting or surgery.

claim.gs028e.sglt2.suspected-ketoacidosi.statement: Suspected SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis warrants interruption of the implicated drug and immediate medical assessment; a reassuring glucose value must not delay urgent care when ketones and acidosis are present.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.suspected-ketoacidosi.limitation: The clinic escalates rather than administering a DKA treatment protocol; no insulin, fluid, electrolyte, restart dose, or monitoring schedule is authored.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.suspected-ketoacidosi.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected current SGLT2-associated ketoacidosis.

claim.gs028e.naloxone.competitive-opioid.statement: Naloxone reverses opioid effects by competing at opioid receptor sites as an antagonist rather than stimulating those receptors or chemically destroying the opioid.
claim.gs028e.naloxone.competitive-opioid.limitation: This is a receptor-mechanism objective; no dose, formulation superiority or response guarantee is supplied. The 2023 label is not asserted to be the latest product label.
claim.gs028e.naloxone.competitive-opioid.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing documented or planned opioid-overdose reversal.

claim.gs028e.naloxone.emergency-support-.statement: Naloxone is a temporary reversal intervention and does not replace emergency medical assistance, airway or respiratory support when needed; opioid-related depression can recur after initial improvement.
claim.gs028e.naloxone.emergency-support-.limitation: Two FDA documents from one authority corroborate the boundary; this clinic does not conduct an opioid challenge or simulate advanced airway care.
claim.gs028e.naloxone.emergency-support-.applicablePopulation: Adults with known or suspected opioid toxicity or counseling about naloxone.

claim.gs028e.sglt2.empagliflozin-preoper.statement: U.S. empagliflozin labeling advises withholding the drug for at least three days when possible before surgery or a procedure associated with prolonged fasting.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.empagliflozin-preoper.limitation: Exact interval is drug-specific and based on official U.S. labeling; the second source is a manufacturer-label cross-check, not an independent guideline. Emergency surgery and individualized specialist decisions are outside the scored scenario.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.empagliflozin-preoper.applicablePopulation: Adults taking empagliflozin before elective surgery with sufficient planning time.

claim.gs028e.sglt2.ertugliflozin-preoper.statement: U.S. ertugliflozin labeling advises withholding the drug for at least four days when possible before surgery or a procedure associated with prolonged fasting.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.ertugliflozin-preoper.limitation: Single current drug-specific FDA-approved label; the four-day interval is not generalized to every SGLT2 inhibitor. Emergency surgery decisions are outside this objective.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.ertugliflozin-preoper.applicablePopulation: Adults taking ertugliflozin before elective surgery with sufficient planning time.

claim.gs028e.sglt2.postoperative-restart.statement: Empagliflozin and ertugliflozin labels condition postoperative resumption on clinical stability and return of oral intake rather than a fixed postoperative clock alone.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.postoperative-restart.limitation: Resumption remains an individualized treating-team decision; these cases do not authorize restart during active ketoacidosis or prescribe a fixed restart time.
claim.gs028e.sglt2.postoperative-restart.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a perioperative empagliflozin or ertugliflozin plan.

claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.peritoneal-co2-.statement: CO2 used to create pneumoperitoneum can cross peritoneal tissue into blood; absorbed CO2 is carried to the lungs for exhalation.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.peritoneal-co2-.limitation: Physiology review plus current clinical observational cross-check. No absorption rate, pressure cutoff, or claim that every raised CO2 measurement has this sole cause is authored.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.peritoneal-co2-.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing completed outside laparoscopic surgery with documented CO2 insufflation.

claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.co2-load-respir.statement: Peritoneal CO2 absorption adds a CO2 load; when pulmonary elimination does not match that load, blood CO2 can rise and produce respiratory acidemia.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.co2-load-respir.limitation: Ventilation and respiratory mechanics also affect blood CO2. The current observational study cannot establish every mechanistic contribution; these cases supply completed-care records rather than asking the clinic to select ventilator settings or manage live hypercarbia.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.co2-load-respir.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a resolved CO2-associated event in an outside anesthesia record.

claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.caval-compressi.statement: Pneumoperitoneum pressure that compresses abdominal veins or the vena cava can reduce venous return and cardiac preload; this is a possible mechanism in the supplied compression context, not an inevitable effect of laparoscopy.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.caval-compressi.limitation: No numeric pressure threshold, automatic hypotension rule, or universal cardiac-output direction is inferred. Both pressure and other perioperative factors contribute to hemodynamic observations.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.caval-compressi.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a completed laparoscopic operation with documented pressure-associated venous compression.

claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.pressure-positi.statement: Pneumoperitoneum hemodynamics depend on pressure, circulating volume, and positioning; early compression of splanchnic veins may increase central filling, while head-up positioning can reduce venous return and head-down positioning can increase it.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.pressure-positi.limitation: The review directly supports phase/position distinctions, while the independent study corroborates pressure-associated effects rather than every position comparison. No universal preload outcome or operative management instruction is supplied.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.pressure-positi.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing the hemodynamic context in an outside laparoscopy record.

claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.diaphragm-phren.statement: After laparoscopy, residual gas and diaphragmatic irritation can stimulate the phrenic sensory pathway and contribute to pain perceived at the shoulder even without a shoulder injury.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.diaphragm-phren.limitation: Shoulder pain has multiple possible causes; the proposed phrenic/diaphragmatic mechanism is not proved for every episode. The trial is a gynecologic-population mechanism cross-check; no analgesic, gas-removal procedure or fixed pain duration is prescribed.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.diaphragm-phren.applicablePopulation: Adults with a completed outside laparoscopic cholecystectomy and a fully reassuring clinic assessment.

claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.shoulder-pain-r.statement: A mild improving shoulder symptom after laparoscopy may be discussed as referred pain only in a reassuring clinical context; breathing difficulty, severe or worsening abdominal pain, fever, persistent vomiting, jaundice, or concerning wound changes require renewed assessment rather than automatic gas-pain reassurance.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.shoulder-pain-r.limitation: Single current professional-society patient guidance supports these warning features. No exact fever threshold or complete triage algorithm is authored; the stem supplies current benign findings and does not exclude all disease through wording alone.
claim.gs028e.laparoscopy.shoulder-pain-r.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing shoulder pain after outside laparoscopic gallbladder removal.

claim.gs028e.wound.collagen-iii-to-i-rem.statement: Early healing tissue contains relatively more type III collagen; remodeling progressively replaces much of that matrix with type I collagen rather than reversing the sequence.
claim.gs028e.wound.collagen-iii-to-i-rem.limitation: One adequate peer-reviewed biological review supports this narrow mechanism. This describes a relative matrix change, not complete elimination of type III collagen, an exact timeline, restoration of normal skin strength, or a wound treatment recommendation.
claim.gs028e.wound.collagen-iii-to-i-rem.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing uncomplicated healing of a skin incision.

claim.gs028e.scar_extent.statement: A raised hypertrophic scar stays within the original wound boundary, whereas a keloid extends into skin beyond that boundary.
claim.gs028e.scar_extent.limitation: Morphologic distinction from one official patient-information source; neither timing, symptoms nor ancestry alone establishes the classification. No regression or treatment guarantee.
claim.gs028e.scar_extent.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a raised scar after a healed skin wound.

claim.gs028e.scar_shape_comparison.statement: An atrophic scar may be depressed below the surrounding skin, in contrast to the raised morphology supplied for hypertrophic scars and keloids.
claim.gs028e.scar_shape_comparison.limitation: One official patient-information source; used only for the morphological distractor distinction, without cause, treatment or timing claims.
claim.gs028e.scar_shape_comparison.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing a raised healed scar with a depressed scar pattern.

claim.gs028e.secondary_intention.statement: Secondary-intention healing describes an appropriately open wound allowed to heal without bringing its edges together with closure; planned later edge approximation is a different strategy.
claim.gs028e.secondary_intention.limitation: One current institutional source for the narrow definition. The question supplies the treating clinician's appropriate open-wound plan; it does not decide which wounds should be left open or prescribe care, duration or strength.
claim.gs028e.secondary_intention.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a clinician-selected open skin-wound healing plan.

claim.gs028e.type_i.statement: In a documented IgE-mediated type I reaction, antigen engagement of IgE on sensitized mast cells can trigger mediator release.
claim.gs028e.type_i.limitation: Stable immune mechanism, not a diagnosis from symptoms alone or an allergy-treatment protocol. Both federal sources are older; their mechanism is cross-checked without importing historical management instructions.
claim.gs028e.type_i.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing an outside-confirmed IgE-mediated reaction.

claim.gs028e.urticaria_not_always_ige.statement: Urticaria alone does not establish an IgE-mediated mechanism because contact urticaria may be IgE-mediated or non-IgE-mediated.
claim.gs028e.urticaria_not_always_ige.limitation: The authored cases explicitly supply specialist confirmation where an IgE mechanism is tested; they do not classify all hives, all food reactions or all drug reactions as type I.
claim.gs028e.urticaria_not_always_ige.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a resolved urticarial reaction.

claim.gs028e.type_iv.statement: Confirmed allergic contact dermatitis is a T-cell-mediated, type IV delayed hypersensitivity reaction rather than an IgE-mediated mast-cell reaction.
claim.gs028e.type_iv.limitation: This applies to allergic contact dermatitis, not every irritant contact rash. Exact onset intervals, patch-testing instructions and treatment are not taught.
claim.gs028e.type_iv.applicablePopulation: Adults with specialist-confirmed allergic contact dermatitis.

claim.gs028e.non_ige_antibody_comparison.statement: Type II and type III hypersensitivity involve non-IgE antibodies, including IgG or IgM, and complement; these broad antibody mechanisms differ from the IgE mast-cell and T-cell contact pathways.
claim.gs028e.non_ige_antibody_comparison.limitation: Narrow comparator from the FDA glossary, Hypersensitivity. No specific cytotoxic target, immune-complex disease, frequency or management claim is inferred from this older source.
claim.gs028e.non_ige_antibody_comparison.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing the established immune mechanism of a resolved reaction.

claim.gs028e.t_cell_graft_comparison.statement: Allograft rejection may involve T-cell-mediated or antibody-mediated pathways, and the pathways can coexist; a documented hyperacute preformed-antibody event should not be substituted with an unproven T-cell-only explanation.
claim.gs028e.t_cell_graft_comparison.limitation: Narrow comparator from the transplant review Abstract; does not classify all acute rejection as T-cell-only, infer a treatment or establish a new active diagnosis.
claim.gs028e.t_cell_graft_comparison.applicablePopulation: Stable adults reviewing a confirmed historical transplant rejection mechanism.

claim.gs028e.hyperacute_preformed.statement: Documented hyperacute allograft rejection can be driven by recipient antibodies that were present before transplantation and recognize donor antigens.
claim.gs028e.hyperacute_preformed.limitation: Narrow mechanism from a transplant review plus an independent commissioned background cross-check. Early graft dysfunction alone does not prove rejection or this mechanism; no transplant timing threshold or treatment is inferred.
claim.gs028e.hyperacute_preformed.applicablePopulation: Stable adults reviewing an outside-confirmed historical hyperacute allograft event.

claim.gs028e.hyperacute_vascular.statement: Preformed donor-specific antibodies can bind allograft endothelium and initiate complement-associated vascular injury and thrombosis in hyperacute rejection.
claim.gs028e.hyperacute_vascular.limitation: One adequately licensed review supplies this narrow vascular mechanism. No claim that all acute rejection is antibody-mediated or that T-cell and antibody mechanisms cannot coexist.
claim.gs028e.hyperacute_vascular.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a documented historical donor-specific antibody-mediated graft injury.

claim.gs028e.mixing_initial_workup.statement: For an unexplained isolated prolonged aPTT after specimen and anticoagulant interference have been assessed, a mixing study can initially help distinguish factor deficiency from an inhibitory substance when immediate FVIII activity testing is unavailable.
claim.gs028e.mixing_initial_workup.limitation: Conditional laboratory workup, not routine preoperative screening or a universal mandatory next test. The cases supply repeated unexplained findings, reviewed interferences and unavailable immediate FVIII:C. Specific factor assays are pursued in parallel by the specialist.
claim.gs028e.mixing_initial_workup.applicablePopulation: Stable adults already referred for an outside specialist evaluation of an unexplained isolated prolonged aPTT.

claim.gs028e.mixing_method.statement: An aPTT mixing study evaluates the aPTT response after combining patient plasma with normal plasma; immediate and incubated assessments can reveal different inhibitory patterns.
claim.gs028e.mixing_method.limitation: Qualitative method only. No mixing ratio, incubation duration, temperature or correction threshold is specified. Neither platelet testing nor a patient-only repeat is that plasma comparison.
claim.gs028e.mixing_method.applicablePopulation: Stable adults reviewing the purpose or method of an outside specialist mixing assessment.

claim.gs028e.mixing_correction.statement: Correction of a prolonged aPTT with normal plasma both immediately and after incubation favors factor deficiency as an initial interpretation.
claim.gs028e.mixing_correction.limitation: The independent society-journal review supports the laboratory principle, not importation of its ICU management algorithm. Correction is laboratory-defined and does not identify a particular factor or establish a final diagnosis.
claim.gs028e.mixing_correction.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a specialist laboratory's qualitative immediate and incubated mixing report.

claim.gs028e.mixing_noncorrection.statement: Failure of the aPTT mixture to correct immediately and after incubation favors an inhibitory substance as an initial interpretation.
claim.gs028e.mixing_noncorrection.limitation: This finding does not establish a particular inhibitor, acquired hemophilia A or a clinical bleeding phenotype. Drug and preanalytical effects must be considered; the authored report states these have been assessed.
claim.gs028e.mixing_noncorrection.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a valid specialist mixing study with persistent noncorrection.

claim.gs028e.mixing_time_dependent.statement: Initial correction followed by loss of correction after incubation can indicate a time-dependent inhibitor; immediate correction alone does not exclude that possibility.
claim.gs028e.mixing_time_dependent.limitation: No exact incubation period, temperature, ratio or laboratory cutoff is authored. A qualitative pattern suggests a mechanism and requires appropriate factor/inhibitor assessment; it is not a definitive diagnosis.
claim.gs028e.mixing_time_dependent.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing immediate versus incubated results from a specialist coagulation laboratory.

claim.gs028e.mixing_limits.statement: Mixing studies are incompletely standardized, cannot by themselves establish or exclude acquired hemophilia A, and should not replace appropriate parallel factor assays.
claim.gs028e.mixing_limits.limitation: No universal correction threshold or isolated-aPTT bleeding-risk estimate is inferred. Interpretation remains tied to the laboratory method and clinical context.
claim.gs028e.mixing_limits.applicablePopulation: Adults with an outside specialist workup of an unexplained prolonged aPTT.

claim.gs028e.stage_extent.statement: Cancer stage describes the extent of disease, including the primary tumor and its spread, using the system appropriate to that cancer.
claim.gs028e.stage_extent.limitation: General official definition from one government source; systems differ by cancer. No stage number, treatment or universal prognosis is assigned from incomplete details.

claim.gs028e.grade_morphology.statement: Tumor grade describes microscopic features such as differentiation and abnormal appearance, with criteria specific to the tumor type.
claim.gs028e.grade_morphology.limitation: General official definition from one government source. No universal numeric grading scheme or guaranteed clinical behavior is taught.
claim.gs028e.grade_morphology.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a pathologist's tumor-specific grading report.

claim.gs028e.grade_not_stage.statement: Tumor grade and cancer stage describe different properties; microscopic grade alone does not establish anatomic spread, and an extent-of-disease finding alone does not establish grade.
claim.gs028e.grade_not_stage.limitation: Two official NCI pages corroborate the distinction but are not independent organizations. The questions do not deny that both properties may matter in a cancer-specific system.
claim.gs028e.grade_not_stage.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing staging and pathology descriptions of cancer.

claim.gs028e.suppressor_loss.statement: Functional RB1 protein helps restrain cell division; loss of its function removes a tumor-suppressive restraint rather than creating an activated growth-promoting protein.
claim.gs028e.suppressor_loss.limitation: Stable molecular mechanism from a government gene summary; not a general statement that all cancer-causing mutations act through loss of function.
claim.gs028e.suppressor_loss.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing an outside tumor molecular report explicitly documenting RB1 loss.

claim.gs028e.rb1_biallelic.statement: The classic RB1 biallelic-loss model involves inactivation or loss of both functioning RB1 copies in a tumor cell.
claim.gs028e.rb1_biallelic.limitation: The authored report explicitly establishes loss of both alleles. A supplied adult tumor report is used for molecular discussion; retinoblastoma background sources are not used to create adult retinoblastoma care or inherited-syndrome diagnoses.
claim.gs028e.rb1_biallelic.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied tumor-cell report documenting biallelic RB1 loss.

claim.gs028e.two_hit_scoped.statement: A classic RB1 two-hit explanation is scoped to the documented biallelic-loss mechanism and is not a universal claim that every tumor suppressor or every tumor requires two such events.
claim.gs028e.two_hit_scoped.limitation: The current PDQ summary recognizes alternate molecular pathways. No inherited FAP/Lynch objective, germline inference or universal rule is taught.
claim.gs028e.two_hit_scoped.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving explanation of an explicitly supplied RB1 biallelic tumor finding.

claim.gs028e.clean_wound.statement: An uninfected operative wound without inflammation, relevant tract entry or a break in aseptic technique, and closed primarily, fits the clean class.
claim.gs028e.clean_wound.limitation: One official surveillance definition source. The case explicitly supplies the operative circumstances; current skin appearance alone does not determine the original class.
claim.gs028e.clean_wound.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing an outside operation's recorded contamination conditions.

claim.gs028e.clean_contaminated.statement: Controlled entry into an alimentary, respiratory, genital or urinary tract without unusual contamination, infection or a major aseptic breach fits the clean-contaminated class.
claim.gs028e.clean_contaminated.limitation: Single official surveillance source. No procedure name alone, infection risk percentage or antibiotic regimen is inferred.
claim.gs028e.clean_contaminated.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a documented controlled tract-entry operation.

claim.gs028e.contaminated.statement: Gross gastrointestinal spillage during an operation without established infection or a pre-existing perforated viscus fits the contaminated class.
claim.gs028e.contaminated.limitation: The authored scenario explicitly distinguishes an intraoperative spill from pre-existing perforation or purulent infection; this is not an antibiotic-selection rule.
claim.gs028e.contaminated.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing an operation with documented gross gastrointestinal spillage.
