claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.spina.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.statement: The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.limitation: One older review used for stable anatomy and localization only; no operative repair deadline or recovery probability is taught. A full postoperative neurologic assessment is still needed.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.statement: Axillary surgery can injure the long thoracic nerve.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.limitation: One older review used for stable anatomy and localization only; no operative repair deadline or recovery probability is taught. A full postoperative neurologic assessment is still needed.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.statement: Serratus weakness can produce medial scapular winging accentuated by forward pushing.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.limitation: One older review used for stable anatomy and localization only; no operative repair deadline or recovery probability is taught. A full postoperative neurologic assessment is still needed.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.statement: Trapezius, latissimus and deltoid deficits represent motor localizations different from serratus weakness.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.limitation: One older review used for stable anatomy and localization only; no operative repair deadline or recovery probability is taught. A full postoperative neurologic assessment is still needed.
claim.gs028g.postoperative-scapula.long-.applicablePopulation: Adult synthetic perioperative or postoperative clinic encounters; no onsite hospital operation is simulated.

claim.gs028f.pregnancy.hcg-testing.statement: Pregnancy testing for hCG is part of the assessment of reproductive-age pelvic or abdominal pain when pregnancy is possible; menstrual history or reported contraception does not substitute for testing when early-pregnancy complications are suspected.
claim.gs028f.pregnancy.hcg-testing.limitation: Guideline and independent government test information. The authored task selects testing as part of immediate assessment; it does not postpone urgent care, select a universal urine-versus-serum assay, or diagnose an ectopic pregnancy.
claim.gs028f.pregnancy.hcg-testing.applicablePopulation: Reproductive-age adults with pelvic/abdominal symptoms and possible pregnancy.

claim.gs028f.pregnancy.early-negative-li.statement: A home urine pregnancy test taken early can be negative despite pregnancy, so an early negative home result does not settle pregnancy status when compatible symptoms persist.
claim.gs028f.pregnancy.early-negative-li.limitation: Single federal test-information source; no exact repeat interval, detection threshold or assay sensitivity is specified.
claim.gs028f.pregnancy.early-negative-li.applicablePopulation: Adults with a possible early pregnancy and an early negative home test.

claim.gs028f.ectopic.symptoms-require-as.statement: A positive pregnancy test with compatible pelvic pain or abnormal vaginal bleeding raises concern for an ectopic pregnancy and requires prompt specialist-capable assessment even when the initial circulation is stable.
claim.gs028f.ectopic.symptoms-require-as.limitation: Current guideline corroborated by independent government symptom guidance. This is suspicion requiring urgent evaluation, not a definitive ectopic diagnosis or an onsite treatment recommendation. The NHS page's displayed review is overdue. Escalating pain, faintness or other deterioration requires emergency assessment without a routine testing wait.
claim.gs028f.ectopic.symptoms-require-as.applicablePopulation: Symptomatic adults with a positive pregnancy test and an unestablished pregnancy location.

claim.gs028f.ectopic.hcg-does-not-locate.statement: A positive hCG result establishes evidence of pregnancy but does not by itself establish its location; clinical assessment and appropriate ultrasonography are needed to evaluate a suspected ectopic pregnancy.
claim.gs028f.ectopic.hcg-does-not-locate.limitation: No hCG discriminatory value, definitive ultrasound rule, treatment regimen or mandatory test sequence is authored.
claim.gs028f.ectopic.hcg-does-not-locate.applicablePopulation: Adults being evaluated for a possible ectopic pregnancy.

claim.gs028f.nerve.median-carpal-localiz.statement: Carpal tunnel syndrome localizes compression of the median nerve to the carpal tunnel at the wrist.
claim.gs028f.nerve.median-carpal-localiz.limitation: Single federal educational source for foundational anatomy, updated 2018. Supplied clinical clues support localization; no automatic operation, electrodiagnostic test or universal cause of hand tingling is asserted.
claim.gs028f.nerve.median-carpal-localiz.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied carpal-tunnel pattern or an outside localization report.

claim.gs028f.nerve.median-wrist-symptoms.statement: Median-nerve compression at the wrist can produce hand numbness and tingling involving the thumb, index and middle fingers, with nocturnal or wrist-position-provoked symptoms.
claim.gs028f.nerve.median-wrist-symptoms.limitation: Only the sourced symptom distribution and wrist/nocturnal context are used. No exact sensory boundary, prevalence, occupational causation or diagnostic certainty from one symptom is claimed.
claim.gs028f.nerve.median-wrist-symptoms.applicablePopulation: Adults with characteristic supplied wrist-level median symptoms.

claim.gs028f.nerve.ulnar-cubital-localiz.statement: Cubital tunnel syndrome localizes ulnar-nerve compression to the inner elbow and can produce tingling or numbness in the little and ring fingers.
claim.gs028f.nerve.ulnar-cubital-localiz.limitation: Single current NHS hand-therapy source for the narrow localization. Ulnar symptoms alone do not distinguish every elbow, wrist or proximal lesion; the authored cases supply elbow-localizing findings.
claim.gs028f.nerve.ulnar-cubital-localiz.applicablePopulation: Adults with characteristic supplied elbow-level ulnar findings.

claim.gs028f.nerve.elbow-provocation.statement: Bending the elbow for prolonged periods or leaning on the inner elbow can provoke symptoms from ulnar compression at the cubital tunnel.
claim.gs028f.nerve.elbow-provocation.limitation: Current patient guidance supports provocation, not a guarantee of diagnosis from position alone or a treatment protocol.

claim.gs028f.neck.adult-lateral-malignan.statement: A persistent unexplained lateral neck mass in an adult requires evaluation for malignancy; a cystic appearance in an older adult does not establish a benign developmental cyst.
claim.gs028f.neck.adult-lateral-malignan.limitation: Single independent multidisciplinary guideline directly supports the malignancy/cystic boundary. The cases are adults older than40 with persistent unexplained nonthyroid masses, not a thyroid-nodule, thyroglossal-duct or known benign-cyst objective. No precise duration threshold or definitive cancer diagnosis is inferred.
claim.gs028f.neck.adult-lateral-malignan.applicablePopulation: Adults older than40 with a persistent unexplained lateral or cystic neck mass.

claim.gs028f.neck.selected-contrast-ct.statement: Contrast-enhanced neck CT can be an appropriate selected cross-sectional study to characterize a nonthyroid/nonparotid neck mass and its cervical anatomy during malignancy evaluation.
claim.gs028f.neck.selected-contrast-ct.limitation: Society-reviewed2022 patient summary supports CT among appropriate options, corroborated by UK2024 CT/anatomy guidance. Primary ACR2018 narrative/portal was inaccessible and is not used. MRI and ultrasound can also be appropriate; CT is not universally superior or mandatory before FNA. No felt/cannot-felt distinction is used.
claim.gs028f.neck.selected-contrast-ct.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a persistent nonpulsatile nonthyroid/nonparotid neck mass and a specialist-selected cross-sectional imaging plan.

claim.gs028f.neck.imaging-versus-tissue-.statement: Cross-sectional neck imaging characterizes anatomy, whereas cell or tissue sampling supplies the material for a cytological or histological diagnosis of an undiagnosed suspicious neck mass.
claim.gs028f.neck.imaging-versus-tissue-.limitation: Single guideline's independently synthesized distinction between imaging and needle-sampling roles. A supplied CT description does not substitute for a tissue specimen; no universal sequence or guaranteed sampling result is claimed.
claim.gs028f.neck.imaging-versus-tissue-.applicablePopulation: Adults with an imaged but still undiagnosed suspicious cervical mass.

claim.gs028f.neck.needle-before-open.statement: After appropriate assessment of an undiagnosed at-risk adult neck mass, fine-needle aspiration is an appropriate initial needle-sampling approach; open incisional or excisional biopsy should not replace the initial needle approach.
claim.gs028f.neck.needle-before-open.limitation: Single independent guideline. FNA is the best offered needle option, not universally preferable to core biopsy. The game action is specialist referral, not a fabricated local generic-FNA procedure or a complete cancer-workup sequence.
claim.gs028f.neck.needle-before-open.applicablePopulation: Adults with an assessed, undiagnosed suspicious cervical mass requiring an initial needle sample.

claim.gs028f.neck.core-biopsy-alternativ.statement: Core needle biopsy may be appropriate for selected neck masses when the tissue or ancillary testing needed is not adequately supplied by fine-needle aspiration.
claim.gs028f.neck.core-biopsy-alternativ.limitation: Single guideline; core is acknowledged in feedback and is never an incorrect alternative to FNA. The cases do not ask for lymphoma-specific sampling or prescribe open biopsy after a fixed number of attempts.
claim.gs028f.neck.core-biopsy-alternativ.applicablePopulation: Specialist-assessed neck masses with technique selection based on pathology requirements.

claim.gs028f.reconstruction.graft-withou.statement: A skin graft is transferred without its own connected blood supply and depends on the recipient bed for support and subsequent vascularization.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.graft-withou.limitation: Single current peer-reviewed review for the graft definition. No exact stages, timing of vascularization, selection rule or graft-survival guarantee is used.

claim.gs028f.reconstruction.pedicled-fla.statement: A pedicled flap moves tissue while retaining a vascular connection that supplies the transferred tissue.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.pedicled-fla.limitation: Current review and independent federal fact sheet support the vascular principle. No named flap design, operative instruction or outcome ranking is inferred.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.pedicled-fla.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a documented pedicled tissue transfer.

claim.gs028f.reconstruction.free-flap-re.statement: A free flap carries its vessels with the transferred tissue, with those vessels reconnected at the recipient site to establish perfusion.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.free-flap-re.limitation: Independent sources corroborate free-flap vascular transfer. Being detached during transfer does not make it a skin graft when the supplied record documents vessel reconnection; no onsite microsurgical capability is implied.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.free-flap-re.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a completed outside free-flap reconstruction.

claim.gs028f.reconstruction.perfusion-no.statement: The graft-versus-flap distinction concerns transfer of the tissue's blood supply, whereas donor-recipient relationship, tissue thickness and donor location describe separate aspects of reconstruction.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.perfusion-no.limitation: Original comparison of independently verified definitions, not a copied classification table. It does not claim that perfusion is the sole factor in choosing a reconstruction.

claim.gs028f.reconstruction.donor-retain.statement: After a split-thickness skin harvest, retained epithelial elements of deeper skin appendages at the donor site can regenerate the donor wound's epithelial surface.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.donor-retain.limitation: The historical narrative review is the sole direct donor-site source. Independent hair-follicle mechanistic evidence corroborates epithelial contribution but is not a donor-management guideline. No exact healing interval, harvest depth, guaranteed outcome or full-thickness donor closure rule is asserted.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.donor-retain.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a partial-thickness skin-graft donor wound with retained appendages.

claim.gs028f.reconstruction.appendage-ep.statement: Hair follicles contain epithelial cells that can contribute to skin-wound re-epithelialization.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.appendage-ep.limitation: Mechanistic review and donor-site narrative corroboration. Models do not establish an exact human healing time or imply every epithelial source is interchangeable; the authored donor cases explicitly retain appendages.
claim.gs028f.reconstruction.appendage-ep.applicablePopulation: Skin wounds with retained epithelial hair-follicle structures.

claim.gs028f.transplant.same-individual.statement: A graft using tissue obtained from the recipient's own body is an autograft.
claim.gs028f.transplant.same-individual.limitation: Donor-recipient terminology only; not a statement about blood supply, rejection, graft survival or the best reconstruction.

claim.gs028f.transplant.different-human.statement: A graft transferred between different people who are not genetically identical is an allograft, whether or not they are relatives.
claim.gs028f.transplant.different-human.limitation: Single government dictionary entry supports the relationship; no suitability or immunosuppression recommendation is made.
claim.gs028f.transplant.different-human.applicablePopulation: Human donor-recipient pairs who are not genetically identical.

claim.gs028f.transplant.genetically-iden.statement: A graft between genetically identical individuals, such as confirmed monozygotic twins, is an isograft or syngeneic graft.
claim.gs028f.transplant.genetically-iden.limitation: Single government controlled-vocabulary source; twin appearance or a matched blood type alone is not asserted to establish genetic identity.

claim.gs028f.transplant.different-specie.statement: A graft transferred from a donor of another species is a xenograft.
claim.gs028f.transplant.different-specie.limitation: Relationship only; the scenario supplies an outside-care product record and does not recommend routine animal-organ transplantation.
claim.gs028f.transplant.different-specie.applicablePopulation: Recipients of tissue with a supplied different-species origin.

claim.gs028f.local-anesthetic.sodium-cha.statement: Voltage-gated sodium channels are the principal molecular target responsible for the nerve-blocking action of conventional local anesthetics such as lidocaine.
claim.gs028f.local-anesthetic.sodium-cha.limitation: Principal mechanism, not a claim that these medicines interact with no other targets. Molecular review and independent government classification; no administration or dose rule.
claim.gs028f.local-anesthetic.sodium-cha.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing local-anesthetic action in sensory nerves.

claim.gs028f.local-anesthetic.nerve-cond.statement: Local-anesthetic inhibition of voltage-gated sodium-channel function reduces the sodium current needed for nerve excitation and action-potential conduction.
claim.gs028f.local-anesthetic.nerve-cond.limitation: Mechanistic review is the sole direct source for the conduction explanation. No specific concentration, onset, duration, sensory-fiber ranking or irreversible nerve effect is claimed.
claim.gs028f.local-anesthetic.nerve-cond.applicablePopulation: Sensory nerve membranes exposed to a conventional local anesthetic.

claim.gs028f.tacrolimus.fkbp12-complex.statement: Tacrolimus binds the intracellular immunophilin FKBP12; the resulting complex participates in inhibition of calcineurin.
claim.gs028f.tacrolimus.fkbp12-complex.limitation: Sole direct source is current PROGRAF prescribing information section 12.1. A qualitative mechanism only; no binding affinity, drug-comparison ranking, dose or medication-management rule.
claim.gs028f.tacrolimus.fkbp12-complex.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a documented tacrolimus prescription.

claim.gs028f.tacrolimus.calcineurin.statement: Calcineurin phosphatase is the key enzyme inhibited by the tacrolimus–FKBP12 complex in the drug's immunosuppressive mechanism.
claim.gs028f.tacrolimus.calcineurin.limitation: Exact label section 12.1 supports the principal pathway. This does not assert that tacrolimus has only one molecular interaction or prescribe any change in transplant medicines.

claim.gs028f.tacrolimus.t-cell-activatio.statement: The calcineurin-inhibiting action of tacrolimus suppresses T-lymphocyte activation and proliferation.
claim.gs028f.tacrolimus.t-cell-activatio.limitation: Sole verified mechanism source is the product label; qualitative immune effect only. No claim of guaranteed rejection prevention, selective depletion of every T cell or control of an individual patient's graft course.

claim.gs028f.nmb.skeletal-muscle-effect.statement: Rocuronium is a neuromuscular blocking drug that produces skeletal-muscle relaxation through blockade at the motor end plate.
claim.gs028f.nmb.skeletal-muscle-effect.limitation: Current label sections 1 and 12.1 are the sole direct source. A qualitative drug-effect classification, not a dose, administration technique, recovery interval or respiratory-management protocol.
claim.gs028f.nmb.skeletal-muscle-effect.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing documented rocuronium use in outside anesthesia care.

claim.gs028f.nmb.no-unconsciousness-anal.statement: Rocuronium's neuromuscular blockade does not itself provide unconsciousness or pain relief; adequate anesthesia or sedation is a separate requirement when it is used.
claim.gs028f.nmb.no-unconsciousness-anal.limitation: Label section 5.4 directly supports this boundary. Absence of movement cannot independently establish adequate anesthesia. Sole direct source; no ASA sedation definitions, awareness incidence or rescue/administration instructions are used.
claim.gs028f.nmb.no-unconsciousness-anal.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving patient counseling about neuromuscular blockade.

claim.gs028f.last.neurologic-pattern.statement: Systemic local-anesthetic toxicity can produce neurologic findings such as altered taste, tinnitus, perioral numbness, confusion and seizures in a compatible exposure context.
claim.gs028f.last.neurologic-pattern.limitation: ASRA educational discussion section 8 is the sole direct recognition source, published 2021. These findings are not individually diagnostic or a required sequence; the cases supply local-anesthetic exposure and a completed outside clinical course. No source vignette or rescue algorithm is reused.
claim.gs028f.last.neurologic-pattern.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a completed outside-care event after local-anesthetic exposure.

claim.gs028f.last.cardiac-pattern.statement: Systemic local-anesthetic toxicity can also involve cardiac conduction disturbances and serious ventricular arrhythmias.
claim.gs028f.last.cardiac-pattern.limitation: Targeted ASRA discussion sections 6 and 8 support cardiac involvement. Sole direct source; no ECG cutoffs, frequency, mandatory waveform or treatment protocol is claimed. A supplied compatible exposure is necessary for the case reasoning.
claim.gs028f.last.cardiac-pattern.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing documented cardiac findings after outside local-anesthetic administration.

claim.gs028f.last.variable-first-manifes.statement: Cardiovascular manifestations of systemic local-anesthetic toxicity can be the initial presentation, so a preceding neurologic warning sequence is not required.
claim.gs028f.last.variable-first-manifes.limitation: ASRA educational section 8 directly supports possible cardiac-first presentation. This is a recognition limit, not a claim that every perioperative arrhythmia is toxicity or that the supplied event's cause can be established without clinical evaluation.
claim.gs028f.last.variable-first-manifes.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing a completed outside event with documented local-anesthetic exposure.

claim.gs028f.refeeding.insulin-phosphate.statement: After substantial undernutrition, carbohydrate reintroduction can increase insulin and promote cellular uptake of phosphate, contributing to a fall in serum phosphate during refeeding.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.insulin-phosphate.limitation: The original 2023 cohort report's Introduction is the sole direct mechanism source in this packet. Stable physiology, not its neurocritical risk model or management algorithm. No exact intake, interval, phosphate threshold or claim that every postfeeding fall has this cause.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.insulin-phosphate.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied compatible outside refeeding course after substantial undernutrition.

claim.gs028f.refeeding.anabolic-transiti.statement: Reintroduction of nutrition after starvation shifts metabolism from a predominantly catabolic state toward an anabolic state.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.anabolic-transiti.limitation: Qualitative mechanism background in the observational report; no numerical energy requirement, timing or incidence adopted. The source population is neurocritical care, but only the stated background physiology is used.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.anabolic-transiti.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing an already evaluated refeeding-related electrolyte course.

claim.gs028f.refeeding.phosphate-not-spe.statement: A low serum phosphate concentration has causes other than refeeding, so that result alone does not establish refeeding syndrome.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.phosphate-not-spe.limitation: AuSPEN 2025 risk and diagnosis discussion supports this limit. No particular diagnostic definition, percentage fall, timing rule or alternative-cause algorithm is adopted. The mechanism cases supply the outside team's assessment and relevant course.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.phosphate-not-spe.applicablePopulation: Adults with low phosphate interpreted in a clinical context.

claim.gs028f.refeeding.thiamine-before-i.statement: For adults identified as at risk of refeeding syndrome, the AuSPEN consensus recommends planned thiamine supplementation before restarting nutrition.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.thiamine-before-i.limitation: Single adequate directly verified management source: AuSPEN 2025 section 3.4.1. Expert consensus explicitly reports no specific evidence evaluating thiamine's preventive role; benefit is not guaranteed. Original underlying-fact synthesis under conservative CC BY-NC-ND targeted-verification status. Dose, route, duration, feeding rate and NICE recommendations are excluded.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.thiamine-before-i.applicablePopulation: Adults already assessed by a specialist nutrition team as at risk during a monitored nutrition restart.

claim.gs028f.refeeding.monitoring-separa.statement: A high-risk nutrition-restart plan includes close clinical and electrolyte monitoring; planned thiamine supplementation does not replace that monitoring.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.monitoring-separa.limitation: AuSPEN 2025 summary and treatment discussion are the sole direct management source. A qualitative multidisciplinary-care principle, not a bedside feeding protocol or a guarantee of avoiding complications. No monitoring frequency, numeric target, prophylactic electrolyte dose or universal feeding rate.
claim.gs028f.refeeding.monitoring-separa.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving an expert-coordinated high-risk nutrition-restart plan.

claim.gs028f.safety.rca-retrospective.statement: Root cause analysis retrospectively reconstructs an adverse event or close call to identify contributing systems problems, rather than treating individual blame as its central purpose.
claim.gs028f.safety.rca-retrospective.limitation: Current AHRQ primer, reviewed June 15, 2024, directly supports the retrospective systems purpose. This is method classification, not a complete RCA protocol, proof of legal liability, mandated institutional policy or a guarantee of improvement.
claim.gs028f.safety.rca-retrospective.applicablePopulation: Patients discussing an already completed patient-specific safety event.

claim.gs028f.safety.fmea-prospective.statement: Healthcare failure mode and effects analysis is a proactive method for identifying potential process failures before those problems occur.
claim.gs028f.safety.fmea-prospective.limitation: Current VA NCPS proactive-risk overview, updated August 28, 2026, supports the healthcare FMEA variant. No claim that every prospective assessment is FMEA, no copied scoring matrix or decision tree, and no statement that the method eliminates risk.
claim.gs028f.safety.fmea-prospective.applicablePopulation: Patients discussing prospective safety review of a planned healthcare process.

claim.gs028f.oxygen.saturation-fraction.statement: Pulse-oximeter SpO2 estimates the proportion of hemoglobin oxygen-binding capacity occupied by oxygen, expressed as a percentage.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.saturation-fraction.limitation: FDA 2024 executive-summary Introduction supplies the hemoglobin-fraction explanation; FDA 2025 consumer page independently confirms the percentage estimate. SpO2 is an estimate with device limitations, not a direct measurement of blood oxygen content or tissue delivery. No formula or fixed normal threshold.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.saturation-fraction.applicablePopulation: Adults interpreting an ordinary supplied pulse-oximeter reading.

claim.gs028f.oxygen.hemoglobin-carriage.statement: Hemoglobin in red blood cells carries oxygen, and its blood concentration is a separate quantity from the percentage oxygen saturation.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.hemoglobin-carriage.limitation: NHLBI December 2025 CBC explanation verifies hemoglobin carriage; FDA background verifies saturation's proportional meaning. Original qualitative comparison, without a numeric anemia threshold, race-specific reference range, transfusion indication or claim about cardiac output.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.hemoglobin-carriage.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied outside hemoglobin result and saturation reading.

claim.gs028f.oxygen.anemia-content-limit.statement: Reduced hemoglobin can reduce blood oxygen-carrying content even when the remaining hemoglobin has a normal oxygen saturation, so a normal SpO2 alone does not exclude anemia or establish adequate oxygen content.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.anemia-content-limit.limitation: Qualitative physiological inference from independently verified hemoglobin-carriage and saturation-fraction facts; FDA device background also describes reduced oxygen-carrying ability in anemia. Other determinants of tissue oxygen delivery are not assessed. No numeric content equation, hemoglobin threshold or treatment decision.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.anemia-content-limit.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with established anemia discussing an outside blood-count result.

claim.gs028f.oxygen.clip-display-limit.statement: An ordinary pulse-oximeter display can report oxygen saturation and pulse rate, sometimes with signal strength; those displayed values do not provide a hemoglobin concentration.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.clip-display-limit.limitation: FDA 2025 consumer page is the sole direct source for ordinary clip display fields. Cases explicitly supply those fields only. This does not claim that every specialized multi-parameter device lacks additional functions, and it does not order a new blood test.
claim.gs028f.oxygen.clip-display-limit.applicablePopulation: Adults interpreting supplied ordinary pulse-oximeter display values.

claim.gs028f.melanoma.small-bowel-spread.statement: Cutaneous melanoma can metastasize to the small bowel.
claim.gs028f.melanoma.small-bowel-spread.limitation: The 2024 retrospective case series directly establishes occurrence, not a population frequency or ranking of primary cancers. No survival, treatment benefit, timing or diagnostic marker threshold is inferred from this selected surgical cohort.
claim.gs028f.melanoma.small-bowel-spread.applicablePopulation: Adults with an established cutaneous melanoma history and a supplied outside small-bowel pathology diagnosis.

claim.gs028f.melanoma.metastatic-primary.statement: A cancer metastasis retains the identity of its established primary cancer; its new anatomic location does not by itself make it a primary cancer of that organ.
claim.gs028f.melanoma.metastatic-primary.limitation: Current NCI explanation directly supports primary identity and naming after metastatic spread. The cases give a specialist pathology comparison confirming the relationship to a known cutaneous primary. No unknown-primary ranking, diagnosis from one stain, melanoma subtype inference or management decision.
claim.gs028f.melanoma.metastatic-primary.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a confirmed metastasis from a supplied known primary.

claim.gs028f.foreign-body.negative-bone-.statement: Some swallowed fish or chicken bones are not readily visible on plain radiographs, so a negative film does not exclude a retained bone.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.negative-bone-.limitation: Direct concordant WSES 2019 imaging guidance and official ESGE 2016 PDF page 3. The older guidelines remain on current official indexes; underlying diagnostic evidence has limitations. No exact sensitivity, false-negative proportion, blanket plain-film-first rule or claim that every bone is radiolucent.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.negative-bone-.applicablePopulation: Symptomatic adults reporting swallowed fish or chicken bone.

claim.gs028f.foreign-body.persistent-sym.statement: Persistent esophageal symptoms after a suspected swallowed foreign body warrant further specialist evaluation even when plain radiographs are negative.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.persistent-sym.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy section directly supports evaluation despite negative radiographs; ESGE independently cross-checks the radiographic bone limitation and therapeutic assessment. No complete imaging sequence or numeric removal deadline. Normal breathing does not resolve the supplied esophageal concern; urgent outside assessment is a case disposition rather than new clinic capability.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.persistent-sym.applicablePopulation: Adults with ongoing swallowing-related symptoms after suspected sharp-bone ingestion.

claim.gs028f.foreign-body.sharp-esophage.statement: A confirmed sharp-pointed foreign body retained in the esophagus is an indication for emergent therapeutic endoscopic removal.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.sharp-esophage.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy recommendation and ESGE 2016 official PDF page 4 agree. Strong guideline recommendations rely on largely low-quality evidence; age and current index status are recorded. The cases direct emergency hospital care outside the clinic, not a routine timed game EGD, a rescue protocol, extraction technique or a numeric deadline.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.sharp-esophage.applicablePopulation: Adults with supplied confirmation of a sharp esophageal foreign body.

claim.gs028f.foreign-body.sharp-perforat.statement: A sharp-pointed esophageal foreign body presents a risk of full-thickness esophageal injury, which underlies the need for emergent removal even without complete obstruction.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.sharp-perforat.limitation: Both guidelines support sharp-object urgency independent of the separate complete-obstruction indication. No exact perforation probability or claim that injury has already occurred. Cases have confirmed esophageal location, normal respiration and no supplied perforation; no onsite treatment or automatic surgery is inferred.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.sharp-perforat.applicablePopulation: Adults with a confirmed retained sharp esophageal object and preserved breathing.

claim.gs028f.foreign-body.initial-endosc.statement: For a persistent esophageal foreign body requiring removal, therapeutic endoscopy is the initial approach when the supplied assessment has not identified a complication or circumstance requiring an operation.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.initial-endosc.limitation: WSES 2019 endoscopy and surgical-indication sections directly support initial endoscopic care and separately identify operative indications. Sole direct source for this narrow comparator boundary. No extraction technique, universal avoidance of surgery, patient self-treatment or clinic procedure is taught.
claim.gs028f.foreign-body.initial-endosc.applicablePopulation: Adults with a confirmed retained esophageal foreign body and no supplied operative complication.

claim.gs028se.statistics.independent-t.statement: A two-sample t procedure compares means from two independent groups when the continuous observations, sampling, and distributional assumptions are reasonable.
claim.gs028se.statistics.independent-t.limitation: The fictional exercises state the relevant assumptions; they do not claim that every continuous two-group dataset requires a t test.
claim.gs028se.statistics.independent-t.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

claim.gs028se.statistics.independent-t.m.statement: McNemar testing is for paired binary responses, so it does not fit independent, continuous, ordinal, or multi-category observations in these exercises.
claim.gs028se.statistics.independent-t.m.limitation: This boundary distinguishes the data structure only; it does not teach extensions or continuity corrections.
claim.gs028se.statistics.independent-t.m.applicablePopulation: Fictional statistical-method exercises that include McNemar testing as a competing analysis.

claim.gs028se.statistics.paired-t.statement: A paired t procedure analyzes within-pair differences for continuous repeated or matched measurements when those differences are reasonably normal.
claim.gs028se.statistics.paired-t.limitation: The exercises explicitly describe reasonable paired-difference assumptions and do not make the test a default for every pre-post dataset.
claim.gs028se.statistics.paired-t.applicablePopulation: Fictional educational and quality-improvement datasets with the assumptions stated in each question.

claim.gs028se.statistics.one-way-anova.statement: One-way analysis of variance compares means across independent groups when the observations, residual distribution, and variance assumptions are reasonable.

claim.n2.5aa2710c7ac3.applicablePopulation: General human collagen biosynthesis and perioperative wound-healing education.

claim.n2.544a3a1d14f1.statement: The established biochemical requirement for vitamin C does not by itself justify routine high-dose supplementation as a universal treatment for every well-nourished postoperative patient.
claim.n2.544a3a1d14f1.limitation: Clinical supplementation evidence varies across populations and wound types; this concept teaches mechanism and does not prescribe a dose or treatment protocol. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N2. The exact clinical application, decision boundary and option ranking require review. Only one recorded source publication supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claim.n2.544a3a1d14f1.applicablePopulation: Postoperative patients without a separately established vitamin C deficiency or condition-specific supplementation indication.

claim.qq20261102.ultrasound-component-li.statement: Gallbladder wall thickening and surrounding fluid are individual ultrasound findings with limited sensitivity; their absence does not by itself exclude acute cholecystitis when the clinical concern persists.
claim.qq20261102.ultrasound-component-li.limitation: No exact wall cutoff or diagnostic rate is authored. Additional imaging depends on the clinical question and local practice; the fictional component findings do not prove a diagnosis.
claim.qq20261102.ultrasound-component-li.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected acute calculous cholecystitis.

claim.qq20261102.named-art-regimen.statement: Darunavir with ritonavir plus tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and emtricitabine is a recognized complete antiretroviral combination in selected clinical circumstances.
claim.qq20261102.named-art-regimen.limitation: A prescribed fictional regimen, not a recommendation to initiate it for everyone. Selection, food requirements, renal/bone considerations, resistance and interactions require individualized care. No dose or fasting schedule is taught; perioperative continuity uses the existing separate claims.
claim.qq20261102.named-art-regimen.applicablePopulation: Adults already prescribed the named combination in the fictional perioperative case.

claim.qq20261102.galactorrhea-pattern.statement: Galactorrhea describes milk-like breast secretion rather than a diagnosis established by reddish discharge.
claim.qq20261102.galactorrhea-pattern.limitation: Definition only from a government patient-information page. The item does not diagnose hyperprolactinemia or a pituitary lesion, and colour alone does not establish malignancy.

claim.qq20261102.motility-egjoo.statement: The Chicago v4.0 manometric category of esophagogastric junction outflow obstruction retains evidence of peristalsis; elevated relaxation pressure alone is insufficient for a clinically conclusive diagnosis.
claim.qq20261102.motility-egjoo.limitation: Only the neighboring-category distinction is used. Protocol positions, supportive testing and technical factors matter; no diagnostic numeric cutoff, subtype or treatment algorithm is reproduced.

claim.qq20261102.motility-absent-contrac.statement: Absent contractility in Chicago v4.0 requires failed esophageal contractions together with normal median integrated relaxation pressure; borderline relaxation values require further consideration.
claim.qq20261102.motility-absent-contrac.limitation: The items use clearly laboratory-abnormal relaxation measurements, not borderline values. This category is not a specific systemic-disease diagnosis; no device-dependent numerical threshold is invented.

claim.qq20261102.gastric-adjacent-organ-.statement: Combined pancreatic and splenic resection during gastrectomy is an extension considered for relevant direct invasion, not a default consequence of a proximal gastric primary.
claim.qq20261102.gastric-adjacent-organ-.limitation: The question concerns uninvolved organs and does not specify an operative technique. The 2025 English hilar-node recommendation contains contradictory wording, recorded separately and withheld from the item.
claim.qq20261102.gastric-adjacent-organ-.applicablePopulation: Operative planning for the supplied resectable proximal gastric adenocarcinoma.

claim.qq20261102.ulcer-initial-treatment.statement: A peptic ulcer with a nonbleeding visible vessel warrants endoscopic hemostasis followed by appropriate proton-pump inhibitor treatment.
claim.qq20261102.ulcer-initial-treatment.limitation: One current freely available society guideline is used for this added combined-plan claim; existing ACG evidence supports the hemostasis indication separately. No exact drug dose, duration or deadline is authored.
claim.qq20261102.ulcer-initial-treatment.applicablePopulation: Adults with peptic-ulcer bleeding and a nonbleeding visible vessel.

claim.qq20261102.ulcer-rescue-embolizati.statement: Transcatheter arterial embolization is generally considered after endoscopic hemostatic approaches fail rather than replacing an indicated initial endoscopic attempt.
claim.qq20261102.ulcer-rescue-embolizati.limitation: One current guideline supports this new escalation boundary. Selected prophylactic embolization after endoscopic control is a separate situation; no blanket prohibition or emergency delay is taught.
claim.qq20261102.ulcer-rescue-embolizati.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving management for bleeding peptic ulcers.

claim.qq20261102.gastric-hilar-language-.statement: The English 2025 JGCA CQ3-2 text contains opposed recommendations attached to the same stated greater-curvature condition, so that wording cannot independently resolve the hilar-dissection teaching point.
claim.qq20261102.gastric-hilar-language-.limitation: WITHHELD: review-only source discrepancy, not a patient teaching rule or answer rationale. Do not silently correct the text, average recommendations or infer the intended qualifier; named clinician/source clarification is required.
claim.qq20261102.gastric-hilar-language-.applicablePopulation: Editorial source review only; not used to key a question.

claim.qq20261102a.gallbladder-filling-ve.statement: Gallbladder-filling scintigraphy evaluates cystic-duct patency, whereas stimulated ejection fraction evaluates gallbladder emptying.
claim.qq20261102a.gallbladder-filling-ve.limitation: One technique-specific guideline plus an independent acute-disease guideline. Normal ultrasound wall/fluid components do not exclude acute disease; a universal HIDA-over-every-CT/MRI ranking is not asserted.
claim.qq20261102a.gallbladder-filling-ve.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.mixed-discharge-medica.statement: Metoclopramide can increase prolactin and produce galactorrhea.
claim.qq20261102a.mixed-discharge-medica.limitation: Primary regulatory label only for this drug fact; no dose, timing or causation of a focal breast lesion claimed. Separate existing discharge claims support assessment of spontaneous unilateral episodes.
claim.qq20261102a.mixed-discharge-medica.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.mixed-discharge-local-.statement: Spontaneous unilateral nipple discharge warrants breast-local assessment rather than being explained away by expressed bilateral secretion.
claim.qq20261102a.mixed-discharge-local-.limitation: Application synthesized from the separate pattern definitions in one open review, not a reported mixed-phenotype trial. Color alone is not a malignancy diagnosis; the medication-associated component can coexist.
claim.qq20261102a.mixed-discharge-local-.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.initial-breast-pathway.statement: In women over 40 with a pathologic discharge pattern, initial mammography is generally combined with ultrasound; MRI has a subsequent problem-solving role.
claim.qq20261102a.initial-breast-pathway.limitation: One current open imaging review, cross-checked against retained project discharge-imaging evidence. The exact age boundary is supported by the source; every supplied female profile is above it. Local imaging suitability remains clinician review.
claim.qq20261102a.initial-breast-pathway.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.boosted-midazolam-rout.statement: Oral midazolam is contraindicated with ritonavir-boosted protease-inhibitor therapy.
claim.qq20261102a.boosted-midazolam-rout.limitation: One adequately retrieved current guideline for this added interaction fact; NIH direct table returned 403 and is not counted as independent verification.
claim.qq20261102a.boosted-midazolam-rout.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.boosted-parenteral-tit.statement: Parenteral midazolam may be considered with boosted protease inhibitors in an appropriately monitored setting, with dose reduction considered particularly for repeated doses.
claim.qq20261102a.boosted-parenteral-tit.limitation: One verified current guideline. No exact dose, mandatory universal reduction, unsupervised administration or washout interval authored; anesthesia/HIV coordination required.
claim.qq20261102a.boosted-parenteral-tit.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.art-continuity.statement: Avoid uncoordinated perioperative ART interruption; consult the HIV team when interruption cannot be avoided.
claim.qq20261102a.art-continuity.limitation: One verified current guideline; administration feasibility and individual interactions still require clinical review. The existing named-regimen claim independently verifies the four-drug combination.
claim.qq20261102a.art-continuity.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.pressure-not-peristals.statement: Simultaneous panesophageal pressurization is not preserved propagated peristalsis when classifying achalasia.
claim.qq20261102a.pressure-not-peristals.limitation: Clinical application and the constructed phenotype require Melissa's review; no exact clinical probability, dose or timing is inferred.
claim.qq20261102a.pressure-not-peristals.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.primary-position-achal.statement: Abnormal median IRP in the primary test position with absent peristalsis can establish achalasia; abnormal IRP in both positions is not required as it is for an EGJOO pattern.
claim.qq20261102a.primary-position-achal.limitation: Single primary classification consensus for the exact positional distinction; ten primary-position swallows and protocol adequacy require clinical confirmation. No device-specific IRP threshold invented.
claim.qq20261102a.primary-position-achal.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.spastic-achalasia.statement: Premature or failed rather than normally peristaltic swallows with abnormal junction relaxation support a spastic achalasia pattern.
claim.qq20261102a.spastic-achalasia.limitation: The constructed case uses most premature swallows and remaining failed swallows; no subtype label is asked. Technical adequacy, latency reference and opioid effects require review.
claim.qq20261102a.spastic-achalasia.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.failed-contraction-thr.statement: Chicago v4.0 classifies DCI below 100 mmHg.s.cm as failed contraction.
claim.qq20261102a.failed-contraction-thr.limitation: The exact cutoff is explicitly supported by the consensus. B04's 30-80 readings are synthetic examples inside that range, not an invented normal threshold or measured patient dataset.
claim.qq20261102a.failed-contraction-thr.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.esophageal-physiology-.statement: High-resolution manometry supplies esophageal motor classification when persistent obstructive swallowing symptoms remain after structural evaluation.
claim.qq20261102a.esophageal-physiology-.limitation: FLIP can complement inconclusive studies or be used in selected circumstances; it is not declared useless. No later pressure result is used to justify the earlier task.
claim.qq20261102a.esophageal-physiology-.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.groin-initial-dynamic-.statement: Ultrasound is an initial imaging approach for suspected groin hernia when examination does not establish the diagnosis.
claim.qq20261102a.groin-initial-dynamic-.limitation: MRI can be appropriate after unresolved assessment; the case establishes first imaging and an intermittent lump, without an availability cue.
claim.qq20261102a.groin-initial-dynamic-.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.symptomatic-groin-plan.statement: Activity-limiting symptoms from an inguinal hernia favor discussion of elective repair rather than treating the patient as an asymptomatic watchful-waiting candidate.
claim.qq20261102a.symptomatic-groin-plan.limitation: Risk, preferences and surgical assessment remain necessary; no compulsory operation, emergency state or outcome probability asserted.
claim.qq20261102a.symptomatic-groin-plan.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.papillary-cytology-reg.statement: Malignant thyroid cytology warrants preoperative ultrasound assessment of central and lateral cervical nodal compartments.
claim.qq20261102a.papillary-cytology-reg.limitation: Current primary guideline supports the initial survey; additional CT/MRI or sampling can be appropriate for extensive/invasive or sonographically suspicious disease. No node-size threshold authored.
claim.qq20261102a.papillary-cytology-reg.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.papillary-cytology-pat.statement: Papillary groups with nuclear grooves and intranuclear cytoplasmic inclusions support a papillary thyroid carcinoma interpretation.
claim.qq20261102a.papillary-cytology-pat.limitation: A groove alone is insufficient; integrated architecture/nuclei and cytopathologist review are required. No histologic subtype or absolute specificity is taught.
claim.qq20261102a.papillary-cytology-pat.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.melanoma-integrated-no.statement: Clinically node-negative invasive melanoma in the supplied greater-than-1-mm range calls for sentinel-node staging consideration; reassuring ultrasound does not replace microscopic nodal staging.
claim.qq20261102a.melanoma-integrated-no.limitation: Existing synthetic thickness values are retained. No fixed metastatic probability or survival benefit asserted; subtype and patient suitability remain clinician review.
claim.qq20261102a.melanoma-integrated-no.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.melanoma-diagnostic-sa.statement: When feasible, complete diagnostic removal of a suspicious melanocytic lesion supports assessment of its architecture and invasion depth.
claim.qq20261102a.melanoma-diagnostic-sa.limitation: The offered tangential option is explicitly limited to papillary dermis; this does not condemn every shave or require excision in anatomically unsuitable lesions.
claim.qq20261102a.melanoma-diagnostic-sa.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.malignant-polyp-advers.statement: Adverse invasive-polyp histology or incomplete resection can warrant oncologic regional resection despite a clear-looking scar.
claim.qq20261102a.malignant-polyp-advers.limitation: One verified primary guideline for this added scope: lymphovascular invasion, poor differentiation, involved deep margin and fragmentation are separately constructed case findings. Individual pedunculated/sessile risk and operative fitness require review; normal CT nodes do not prove microscopic negativity.
claim.qq20261102a.malignant-polyp-advers.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.colon-systemic-staging.statement: Chest, abdominal and pelvic CT is a standard initial colon-cancer staging pathway; routine PET-CT is not its automatic replacement.
claim.qq20261102a.colon-systemic-staging.limitation: Single retrieved guideline. Chest CT plus abdominal MRI is also an accepted pathway and is deliberately not offered as wrong; chest radiography is not equivalent thoracic staging. Contrast suitability assumed, not guaranteed.
claim.qq20261102a.colon-systemic-staging.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.sarcoma-viable-biopsy-.statement: Image-guided core sampling of a heterogeneous soft-tissue tumor should target viable tumor identified with enhancement or vascularity.
claim.qq20261102a.sarcoma-viable-biopsy-.limitation: Exact targeting is directly supported by older primary technique guidance; current society guidance corroborates planned image-guided core biopsy. No diagnostic certainty from MRI alone, invented needle size or tract rule added.
claim.qq20261102a.sarcoma-viable-biopsy-.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.sarcoma-local-imaging.statement: MRI is the preferred local characterization/staging study for a deep or indeterminate limb soft-tissue mass before planned biopsy.
claim.qq20261102a.sarcoma-local-imaging.limitation: CT is useful in selected circumstances; ultrasound can triage accessible lesions. The supplied prior ultrasound establishes deep extent, rather than merely a lesion beneath skin.
claim.qq20261102a.sarcoma-local-imaging.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.subepithelial-integrat.statement: A homogeneous bright submucosal lesion with a yellow deformable endoscopic appearance supports lipoma characterization.
claim.qq20261102a.subepithelial-integrat.limitation: One primary guideline for the added raw EUS detail; existing lipoma evidence separately supports no directed follow-up when confidently characterized and asymptomatic. Not all SELs can be diagnosed from EUS alone.
claim.qq20261102a.subepithelial-integrat.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.gastric-depth-nodes-or.statement: A gastric primary extending into muscularis propria falls outside the early T1 nodal-dissection scope and supports a D2 framework in the represented operative plan.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-depth-nodes-or.limitation: The synthetic wall-layer observation must be checked by Melissa. No exact nodal station algorithm or disputed JGCA2025 hilar recommendation is used.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-depth-nodes-or.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.gastric-spleen-preserv.statement: Prophylactic splenectomy is not routine for the represented proximal gastric cancer without greater-curvature or splenic invasion.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-spleen-preserv.limitation: The separate contradictory English JGCA2025 hilar statement remains withheld. Direct invasion or therapeutic nodal indications can change scope; the case's fat plane is not proof against every microscopic extension.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-spleen-preserv.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.gastric-lineage-not-cl.statement: CD20 establishes B-cell lineage but is insufficient without representative morphology and ancillary assessment to classify gastric MALT lymphoma.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-lineage-not-cl.limitation: Repeat representative biopsies are warranted for the constructed crushed, architecture-poor sample. Clonality alone can occur in reactive inflammation and does not resolve every lymphoma subtype.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-lineage-not-cl.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.gastric-malt-response-.statement: Histologic gastric response assessment is needed after H. pylori-directed treatment of gastric MALT lymphoma; symptoms alone do not establish remission.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-malt-response-.limitation: No eradication regimen, exact follow-up interval, universal response probability or automatic salvage rule authored.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-malt-response-.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.gastric-small-b-cell-d.statement: Gastric small B-cell infiltration with gland involvement and a CD20/CD79a-positive, CD5/CD10/cyclin-D1-negative profile supports MALT lymphoma in integrated pathology review.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-small-b-cell-d.limitation: Markers have exceptions; this is not a unique single-stain rule, and lymphoma classification requires morphology, clinical context and expert review.
claim.qq20261102a.gastric-small-b-cell-d.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.null-test-versus-proto.statement: Testing against no effect and evaluating a prespecified meaningful effect or equivalence margin are different statistical questions.
claim.qq20261102a.null-test-versus-proto.limitation: B26/B27/B31/B39 numbers, targets and intervals are constructed protocol inputs, not clinical thresholds or observed treatment effects. TOST .05 uses a 90% CI, not a substituted 95% CI; arithmetic/rounding is separately validated.
claim.qq20261102a.null-test-versus-proto.applicablePopulation: Explicitly fictional study datasets; methodology only, not observed intervention effects.

claim.qq20261102a.odds-to-risk-conversio.statement: For a fixed covariate profile, multiply baseline odds by the conditional odds ratio, then convert resulting odds to risk as odds/(1+odds).
claim.qq20261102a.odds-to-risk-conversio.limitation: Algebraic derivation from definitions, not a causal/marginal prediction. With baseline .40 and OR .60 the risk is 2/7, approximately 29%; all values are fictional inputs.
claim.qq20261102a.odds-to-risk-conversio.applicablePopulation: Explicitly fictional study datasets; methodology only, not observed intervention effects.

claim.qq20261102a.relative-to-absolute-i.statement: With a fixed reference risk, a risk-ratio interval transforms to a risk-difference interval by multiplying each endpoint by that risk and subtracting it.
claim.qq20261102a.relative-to-absolute-i.limitation: Derived algebra on fictional inputs: .20*(.40-1)=-.12 and .20*(1.20-1)=.04. A reference-risk uncertainty distribution is not supplied or assumed; intervals are not hard bounds on truth.
claim.qq20261102a.relative-to-absolute-i.applicablePopulation: Explicitly fictional study datasets; methodology only, not observed intervention effects.

claim.qq20261102a.sedation-supported-dis.statement: After IV sedation, discharge planning includes assessed recovery and responsible adult support, not a driver-only transport booking.
claim.qq20261102a.sedation-supported-dis.limitation: One current specialist guideline plus retained existing local discharge advice. Local approved escort pathways may differ; no taxi-only shortcut, fixed recovery duration or blanket rule for unsedated/nitrous procedures taught.
claim.qq20261102a.sedation-supported-dis.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.sedation-after-reversa.statement: Re-sedation can follow flumazenil reversal of midazolam, so apparent immediate recovery does not remove the need for further monitoring.
claim.qq20261102a.sedation-after-reversa.limitation: One primary specialist guideline. No exact observation period or dose authored; prior benzodiazepine/opioid exposure and individual risk require review.
claim.qq20261102a.sedation-after-reversa.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.pancreatic-contrast-ch.statement: Pre-drainage cross-sectional imaging of a pancreatic fluid collection assesses wall, contents, adjacent organs and vessels.
claim.qq20261102a.pancreatic-contrast-ch.limitation: CT/MRCP and EUS play complementary roles. The item compares specified CT contrast protocols, not CT against a falsely invalid MRI pathway; actual vascular and contrast suitability remain review requirements.
claim.qq20261102a.pancreatic-contrast-ch.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.collection-symptom-att.statement: Persistent attributable symptoms or obstruction can warrant drainage assessment of a walled pancreatic fluid collection.
claim.qq20261102a.collection-symptom-att.limitation: One verified guideline for this added application. Referral is for access/expertise and symptom attribution assessment, not immediate puncture; no size-only cutoff, exact elapsed time or invented vessel clearance authored.
claim.qq20261102a.collection-symptom-att.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.pdsa-outcome-balancing.statement: Improvement-cycle decisions should consider whether process changes improve the intended outcome and add burden, then use the findings to plan the next test.
claim.qq20261102a.pdsa-outcome-balancing.limitation: B36 is a fictional process pilot, not patient trial evidence or question correctness analytics. The data favor adapting the form over rollout or training-only repetition; no universal abandon threshold taught.
claim.qq20261102a.pdsa-outcome-balancing.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.ibc-core-versus-adjunc.statement: Breast core tissue confirms invasive carcinoma in a suspected inflammatory breast cancer presentation; skin punch can add dermal information but does not replace that confirmation.
claim.qq20261102a.ibc-core-versus-adjunc.limitation: Existing primary-consensus claim retained; dermal emboli are not required. The poorly informative prior aspirate motivates a tissue core, and staging is conditional on confirmation, preserving the existing external-service bundle.
claim.qq20261102a.ibc-core-versus-adjunc.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.ibc-response-local-tre.statement: Clinical response to neoadjuvant treatment does not by itself remove the mastectomy and regional radiation components of the represented operable stage III inflammatory breast cancer pathway.
claim.qq20261102a.ibc-response-local-tre.limitation: Conditional future planning, not a claim that systemic therapy occurred during biopsy wait; individual operability and response require review. No modern non-IBC de-escalation rule is extrapolated.
claim.qq20261102a.ibc-response-local-tre.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102a.ulcer-local-modality-c.statement: A nonbleeding ulcer vessel can receive mechanical or contact-thermal hemostasis; epinephrine alone is inadequate, and topical agents are not routine sole initial therapy for that finding.
claim.qq20261102a.ulcer-local-modality-c.limitation: Current specific guideline only for the new modality comparison; retained ACG evidence independently supports hemostasis indication. Powder can be appropriate rescue/temporizing therapy; after the failed clip the selected contact treatment supplements epinephrine rather than repeating monotherapy. No dose or universal rescue sequence authored.
claim.qq20261102a.ulcer-local-modality-c.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

claim.qq20261102b.mixed-discharge-parall.statement: A plausible medication-associated prolactin rise warrants medication review and reassessment rather than automatic prioritization of pituitary imaging.
claim.qq20261102b.mixed-discharge-parall.limitation: One current open clinical review for this sequence; not a rule excluding pituitary disease. Existing independent metoclopramide and focal-discharge claims remain mapped.
claim.qq20261102b.mixed-discharge-parall.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

claim.qq20261102b.implant-mri-not-discha.statement: A noncontrast silicone-implant-integrity MRI does not replace the conventional diagnostic pathway for spontaneous focal nipple discharge.
claim.qq20261102b.implant-mri-not-discha.limitation: Synthesis of two distinct protocol facts, not a direct comparative trial; age-appropriate mammography/targeted ultrasound and later contrast MRI remain individualized.

claim.qq20261102b.route-specific-midazol.statement: Boosted-protease-inhibitor therapy requires individualized parenteral midazolam dosing and appropriate monitoring.
claim.qq20261102b.route-specific-midazol.limitation: Single adequate current guideline. Existing separate oral-contraindication/ART-continuity claims retained. Dose reduction is considered, especially with repeated dosing; no exact dose authored.
claim.qq20261102b.route-specific-midazol.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

claim.qq20261102b.oxygenation-not-ventil.statement: Pulse oximetry does not establish adequate ventilation during procedural sedation.
claim.qq20261102b.oxygenation-not-ventil.limitation: One primary specialist guideline. The fictional capnography/chest observations are not a numerical toxicity threshold.

claim.qq20261102b.sedation-ventilation-r.statement: Sedation-associated respiratory depression calls for assessment and support of ventilation, with reversal or additional anesthesia support as clinically needed.
claim.qq20261102b.sedation-ventilation-r.limitation: One primary specialist guideline. No reversal dose, saturation target, peak-effect time or universal rescue sequence authored.
claim.qq20261102b.sedation-ventilation-r.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

claim.qq20261102b.primary-position-class.statement: Universal failed peristalsis with an abnormal relaxation pressure in an adequate primary-position series can establish an achalasia pattern despite a normal secondary-position pressure.
claim.qq20261102b.primary-position-class.limitation: Primary classification consensus; technically adequate ten-swallow primary series supplied. It does not assert that manometry excludes every secondary cause.

claim.qq20261102b.opioid-spastic-pattern.statement: Opioid exposure can accompany an achalasia-like spastic pattern, and assessment off opioids is advised when feasible.
claim.qq20261102b.opioid-spastic-pattern.limitation: Conditional, low-grade consensus guidance. Withdrawal must be coordinated; no abrupt cessation, fixed washout or universal reversibility is claimed.

claim.qq20261102b.secondary-achalasia-as.statement: Older patients with achalasia-pattern physiology and substantial recent weight loss can require targeted assessment for a secondary junction lesion.
claim.qq20261102b.secondary-achalasia-as.limitation: Single adequate directly retrieved primary guideline for the added alarm-based application. EUS/cross-sectional choice is individualized; no exact weight/time threshold or probability is invented.

claim.qq20261102b.sentinel-before-recons.statement: Sentinel-node mapping/biopsy is preferably coordinated with wide excision before flap or graft reconstruction can disrupt later mapping.
claim.qq20261102b.sentinel-before-recons.limitation: Direct older primary technical guideline; current retained staging-indication evidence is independently mapped. No blanket contraindication after every excision or exact reliability effect is asserted.

claim.qq20261102e.transected-depth-lower.applicablePopulation: The named synthetic adult teaching cases; constructed observations are not empirical patient or gameplay data.

claim.qq20261102f.integrated-partial-dep.statement: A smaller invasive-depth measurement from a different partial specimen does not erase a greater valid demonstrated invasive extent; an incomplete whole-lesion maximum can still have a known lower bound relevant to a supported planning discussion.
claim.qq20261102f.integrated-partial-dep.limitation: Original cross-specimen application of previously verified full-thickness sampling and maximum-depth reporting guidance, not a separately retrieved specimen-integration rule. Dermatopathology must confirm validity and mapping. The 1.8-mm value is retained from this case's existing completed-primary record and 0.6 mm from its existing partial report; their new constructed placement is not a management cutoff. The actual greater-than-1-mm nodal-discussion boundary is separately mapped to existing claim.qq20261102a.melanoma-integrated-node-staging.
claim.qq20261102f.integrated-partial-dep.applicablePopulation: The identified named synthetic adult teaching cases; measurements and acquisition observations are constructed, not empirical patient/gameplay data.

claim.qq20261102f.mri-comparable-contras.statement: Assessment of contrast-related signal change in an intrinsically bright soft-tissue mass region requires accounting for acquisition settings; a pre/post comparison that also changes suppression cannot simply assign all signal differences to enhancement.
claim.qq20261102f.mri-comparable-contras.limitation: Technical application of previously verified primary MRI characterization/contrast-targeting guidance, reused offline. Only one adequate medical primary consensus source is mapped; no new direct verification of the exact constructed sequence pair occurred. MSK radiology must confirm this comparison and its priority. No universal sequence mandate, contrast dose, numerical enhancement criterion, tract or histologic diagnosis is inferred.
claim.qq20261102f.mri-comparable-contras.applicablePopulation: The identified named synthetic adult teaching cases; measurements and acquisition observations are constructed, not empirical patient/gameplay data.

claim.qq20261028.cholecystitis.comparati.statement: When additional imaging is needed for suspected acute calculous cholecystitis, WSES identifies hepatobiliary scintigraphy as having the strongest diagnostic sensitivity and specificity among the modalities compared, with use depending on resources and expertise.
claim.qq20261028.cholecystitis.comparati.limitation: One guideline supports the comparative ranking; this is not a universal next-test rule and does not address every competing abdominal or duct-imaging goal.
claim.qq20261028.cholecystitis.comparati.applicablePopulation: Selected patients with suspected acute calculous cholecystitis needing further imaging.

claim.qq20261028.merkel.panel-pattern.statement: A dermal small-cell malignancy with dot-pattern CK20 and neuroendocrine-marker expression can support Merkel cell carcinoma when integrated with the clinical and pathologic assessment.
claim.qq20261028.merkel.panel-pattern.limitation: The illustrative panel is not a stand-alone diagnostic algorithm; the exact differential and panel sufficiency require clinician review.
claim.qq20261028.merkel.panel-pattern.applicablePopulation: Patients undergoing evaluation of a dermal small-cell malignancy.

claim.qq20261028.merkel.panel-exceptions.statement: CK20 and TTF1 patterns help distinguish Merkel cell carcinoma from pulmonary small-cell carcinoma, but exceptions prevent a single marker from definitively separating them.
claim.qq20261028.merkel.panel-exceptions.limitation: The draft asks which diagnosis is best supported among the options, not which diagnosis a stain proves or excludes.
claim.qq20261028.merkel.panel-exceptions.applicablePopulation: Cutaneous small-cell malignancies with a pulmonary small-cell differential.

claim.qq20261028.capnography.rebreathing.statement: Rebreathing can raise the inspiratory carbon-dioxide baseline; a tracing returning to zero during inspiration weighs against that mechanism for a rising expired carbon-dioxide value.
claim.qq20261028.capnography.rebreathing.limitation: The source is a neonatal perspective. Only the general waveform mechanism is used; adult perioperative application and sampling limitations require clinician review. It does not rule out all equipment problems.
claim.qq20261028.capnography.rebreathing.applicablePopulation: Illustrative capnography interpretation; not a neonatal-to-adult management recommendation.

claim.qq20261028.peristomal.fit-exposure.statement: When a pouch opening leaves peristomal skin exposed to effluent, fit assessment and an opening fitted around the stoma base address continuing contact injury.
claim.qq20261028.peristomal.fit-exposure.limitation: Does not exclude coexisting infection or prescribe one product, wear interval or opening dimension. Exact skin-distribution interpretation requires clinician review.
claim.qq20261028.peristomal.fit-exposure.applicablePopulation: People with an ostomy and suspected effluent-related peristomal skin injury.

claim.qq20261028.statistics.odds-scale.statement: Odds compare a probability with its complement; the ratio of two such odds is an odds ratio, distinct from division or subtraction of the probabilities themselves.
claim.qq20261028.statistics.odds-scale.limitation: Algebraic educational expression, not an adjusted-model interpretation, causal conclusion or real clinical effect estimate. Existing source metadata remains at its recorded access date; analysis page rechecked 2026-10-28.

claim.qq20261029.discharge.mixed-pattern.statement: Bilateral secretion from several ducts elicited by compression can follow a physiologic pattern; it does not explain away a separate history of unprovoked unilateral reddish discharge.
claim.qq20261029.discharge.mixed-pattern.limitation: The mixed fictional observations require clinical interpretation. Pattern classification does not identify the lesion or establish malignancy.

claim.qq20261029.discharge.endocrine-alt.statement: Endocrine and medication-related causes can produce a bilateral secretory pattern; that explanation alone does not account for every focal discharge presentation.
claim.qq20261029.discharge.endocrine-alt.limitation: One open review supports the competing mechanism. The item supplies no endocrine laboratory diagnosis; clinicians must confirm distractor plausibility.

claim.qq20261029.thyroid.initial-lobecto.statement: ATA 2025 recommends lobectomy as the initial surgery for a thyroid cancer measuring 2 cm or less without gross extrathyroidal extension or nodal or distant metastases, unless bilateral cancer or another indication requires contralateral surgery.
claim.qq20261029.thyroid.initial-lobecto.limitation: Recommendation 15A and the official society summary corroborate one organization, not independent guidelines. This profile-specific recommendation must not become a blanket rule for all thyroid cancers.
claim.qq20261029.thyroid.initial-lobecto.applicablePopulation: Adults choosing surgery for the stated cT1N0M0 thyroid-cancer profile.

claim.qq20261029.hernia.spigelian.statement: A Spigelian hernia arises in the lateral abdominal wall in the region between the rectus muscle and semilunar line.
claim.qq20261029.hernia.spigelian.limitation: General anatomical distinction from an adult-focused review; no pediatric prevalence or treatment rule is inferred.

claim.qq20261029.hernia.incisional.statement: An incisional hernia is an abdominal-wall defect related to an operative scar; operative history must be matched to the defect's location.
claim.qq20261029.hernia.incisional.limitation: The synthetic scar location is an invented case observation, not a population statement. No surgical-risk rate is used.

claim.qq20261029.hernia.lumbar.statement: Lumbar hernias are lateral or posterior abdominal-wall defects rather than focal upper-midline defects.
claim.qq20261029.hernia.lumbar.limitation: General anatomical classification only; pediatric plausibility remains for clinician review.

claim.qq20261029.hernia.morgagni-categor.statement: Morgagni hernia is diaphragmatic, so it occupies a different anatomical category from the abdominal-wall hernias in A40.
claim.qq20261029.hernia.morgagni-categor.limitation: Review-packet category explanation only; no Morgagni option, patient phenotype, clinical management or source expression is imported.

claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-anatomic-lo.statement: A direct inguinal hernia protrudes through Hesselbach's triangle medial to the inferior epigastric vessels.
claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-anatomic-lo.limitation: The supporting source is a technical narrative review rather than a diagnostic-performance study.
claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-anatomic-lo.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing evaluation of direct inguinal operative anatomy.

claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-posterior-w.statement: A direct inguinal defect involves weakness of the transversalis fascia in the posterior inguinal wall.
claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-posterior-w.limitation: This bounded statement does not define every component or variation of the posterior inguinal wall.
claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-posterior-w.applicablePopulation: Adults with a direct inguinal defect encountered in operative anatomy.

claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-search-boun.statement: Failure to identify a cord-associated sac can prompt inspection for a direct defect, but does not by itself exclude every other occult groin lesion.
claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-search-boun.limitation: This is a bounded operative-search safeguard, not a validated diagnostic sequence or proof that a direct defect is present.
claim.inguinal-hernia.direct-search-boun.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing open inguinal exploration in which no cord-associated sac is initially identified.

claim.ventral-hernia.elective-pulmonary-.statement: For an adult with a stable, reducible, nonemergent midline incisional hernia being considered for elective repair, pulmonary fitness is a modifiable risk domain to address before finalizing repair planning.
claim.ventral-hernia.elective-pulmonary-.limitation: This does not establish a universal pulmonary target, treatment regimen, or mandatory delay interval.
claim.ventral-hernia.elective-pulmonary-.applicablePopulation: Adults being considered for elective midline incisional-hernia repair without an acute complication.

claim.ventral-hernia.urgent-feature-boun.statement: Acute irreducibility, bowel-obstruction features, escalating pain with peritoneal findings, or systemic deterioration moves an incisional-hernia presentation out of elective optimization and into urgent surgical-capable evaluation.
claim.ventral-hernia.urgent-feature-boun.limitation: The feature set is a safety boundary rather than a validated score; no single feature independently confirms strangulation.
