claim.ventral-hernia.urgent-feature-boun.applicablePopulation: Adults with a primary ventral or incisional hernia and possible acute complication.

claim.hcc.milan.standard-tumor-burden.statement: Standard Milan tumor-burden criteria for hepatocellular carcinoma comprise one lesion measuring 1 through 5 cm, or two to three lesions each measuring 1 through 3 cm.
claim.hcc.milan.standard-tumor-burden.limitation: This claim describes the standard tumor-number and size envelope; it is not a complete transplant-candidacy or organ-allocation rule.
claim.hcc.milan.standard-tumor-burden.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma being considered for specialist liver-transplant evaluation.

claim.hcc.milan.no-macrovascular-invasio.statement: Standard Milan classification requires no macrovascular invasion and no extrahepatic disease.
claim.hcc.milan.no-macrovascular-invasio.limitation: Microscopic pathology, transplant-center assessment, tumor biology, and other candidacy factors are outside this narrow recognition concept.
claim.hcc.milan.no-macrovascular-invasio.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma whose staging is being compared with standard Milan criteria.

claim.hcc.milan.guides-evaluation-not-au.statement: Meeting standard Milan criteria supports transplant-center evaluation but does not by itself guarantee listing or transplantation; disease outside Milan criteria may still warrant specialist evaluation of other pathways.
claim.hcc.milan.guides-evaluation-not-au.limitation: This concept intentionally excludes AFP policy, downstaging selection, organ allocation, liver function, comorbid contraindications, and individualized treatment choice.
claim.hcc.milan.guides-evaluation-not-au.applicablePopulation: Learners applying standard Milan criteria without equating a tumor-burden classification with automatic listing or permanent exclusion.

claim.breast-mass.under-30.initial-ultra.statement: For the scoped presentation of an adult woman younger than 30 years with a new palpable breast mass, breast ultrasound is the appropriate initial imaging study.
claim.breast-mass.under-30.initial-ultra.limitation: The approved variants exclude pregnancy, lactation, known high-risk status, overt inflammatory findings, and subsequent management of suspicious imaging.
claim.breast-mass.under-30.initial-ultra.applicablePopulation: Nonpregnant, nonlactating, average-risk adult women younger than 30 years presenting with a new palpable breast mass.

claim.breast-cyst.simple-ultrasound-phen.statement: A round or oval, circumscribed, anechoic breast lesion with posterior enhancement is concordant with the sonographic phenotype of a simple cyst.
claim.breast-cyst.simple-ultrasound-phen.limitation: Complicated cysts, complex cystic-and-solid masses, dermal lesions, and discordant clinical findings are outside this teaching phenotype.
claim.breast-cyst.simple-ultrasound-phen.applicablePopulation: Patients whose targeted breast ultrasound demonstrates the complete simple-cyst feature set.

claim.breast-cyst.simple-asymptomatic.ob.statement: An unequivocally simple breast cyst that is not painful or otherwise bothersome does not require routine drainage or surgical excision.
claim.breast-cyst.simple-asymptomatic.ob.limitation: This does not govern concerning, complex, recurrent, clinically discordant, or otherwise symptomatic lesions.
claim.breast-cyst.simple-asymptomatic.ob.applicablePopulation: Patients with an imaging-concordant simple breast cyst that is not painful or bothersome.

claim.breast-cyst.simple-symptomatic.asp.statement: Needle aspiration may be offered as the initial procedural treatment for symptom relief from an unequivocally simple breast cyst that is persistently painful or bothersome.
claim.breast-cyst.simple-symptomatic.asp.limitation: This does not define management of bloody aspirate, residual mass, recurrence, imaging discordance, or complex or solid lesions.
claim.breast-cyst.simple-symptomatic.asp.applicablePopulation: Patients with an imaging-concordant simple breast cyst causing persistent focal discomfort who want symptom relief.

claim.ebv.associated-malignancies.classi.statement: Epstein-Barr virus has recognized associations with Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
claim.ebv.associated-malignancies.classi.limitation: The strength and prevalence of the association vary by malignancy subtype, geography, age, and immune context.
claim.ebv.associated-malignancies.classi.applicablePopulation: Learners distinguishing canonical virus-malignancy associations; this is not an individual cancer-risk prediction.

claim.ebv.gastric-adenocarcinoma.subtype.statement: A subset of gastric adenocarcinomas is associated with Epstein-Barr virus.
claim.ebv.gastric-adenocarcinoma.subtype.limitation: The association applies to a subset and must not be phrased as though every gastric adenocarcinoma is EBV-positive.
claim.ebv.gastric-adenocarcinoma.subtype.applicablePopulation: Learners recognizing EBV-associated gastric adenocarcinoma as a molecularly defined subset.

claim.ebv.association-not-universal.statement: An established EBV-malignancy association does not mean that every case of that malignancy is EBV-positive.
claim.ebv.association-not-universal.limitation: This boundary does not quantify the prevalence of EBV positivity for any individual malignancy or predict risk for an individual with prior EBV infection.
claim.ebv.association-not-universal.applicablePopulation: Learners interpreting a recognized virus-malignancy association without converting it into a universal or patient-specific claim.

claim.colonic-lipoma.characteristic-endo.statement: A smooth, yellowish, soft gastrointestinal subepithelial lesion that indents with gentle probing has an endoscopic phenotype strongly supportive of lipoma; absence of the cushion or pillow sign alone does not exclude lipoma.
claim.colonic-lipoma.characteristic-endo.limitation: The positive phenotype is supportive, while the maneuver has limited sensitivity. Atypical or indeterminate lesions require a separate diagnostic pathway.
claim.colonic-lipoma.characteristic-endo.applicablePopulation: Adults with a colonic subepithelial lesion encountered during endoscopy.

claim.colonic-lipoma.clear-asymptomatic..statement: A clearly characterized asymptomatic gastrointestinal lipoma does not require lipoma-directed treatment or dedicated surveillance.
claim.colonic-lipoma.clear-asymptomatic..limitation: This applies only when the diagnosis is clear and the lesion is asymptomatic; ordinary colorectal screening or surveillance remains governed by the remainder of the examination and the patient's usual indications.
claim.colonic-lipoma.clear-asymptomatic..applicablePopulation: Adults with a clearly characterized, incidental, asymptomatic colonic lipoma.

claim.colonic-lipoma.symptoms-or-uncerta.statement: Bleeding, ulceration, clinically significant symptoms, obstruction, or diagnostic uncertainty makes the asymptomatic observation-only lipoma pathway inapplicable and requires further individualized evaluation.
claim.colonic-lipoma.symptoms-or-uncerta.limitation: This boundary does not select a particular endoscopic or surgical resection technique; that decision depends on lesion features, patient factors, and available expertise.
claim.colonic-lipoma.symptoms-or-uncerta.applicablePopulation: Adults with a suspected or confirmed colonic lipoma whose symptoms, surface features, or diagnostic certainty differ from the approved incidental asymptomatic phenotype.

claim.breast-imaging.mass.suspicious-mor.statement: An irregular mammographic mass with a spiculated margin is a concerning morphologic combination that warrants suspicious assessment rather than benign reassurance.
claim.breast-imaging.mass.suspicious-mor.limitation: Imaging morphology raises or lowers concern but is not itself a tissue diagnosis.
claim.breast-imaging.mass.suspicious-mor.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing diagnostic mammographic assessment of a breast mass.

claim.breast-imaging.mass.density-not-di.statement: Mammographic mass density is one descriptor and must be interpreted with shape, margin, associated features, comparison imaging, and the final radiologist assessment rather than being used alone to diagnose or exclude malignancy.
claim.breast-imaging.mass.density-not-di.limitation: The approved questions do not assign a final BI-RADS category from density alone.
claim.breast-imaging.mass.density-not-di.applicablePopulation: Adults whose diagnostic mammogram includes a described breast mass.

claim.breast-imaging.calcification.suspi.statement: Fine pleomorphic or fine linear or fine linear-branching calcifications are suspicious morphologies, and a linear or segmental distribution can add concern when interpreted with morphology and the complete examination.
claim.breast-imaging.calcification.suspi.limitation: No morphology or distribution descriptor independently establishes cancer.
claim.breast-imaging.calcification.suspi.applicablePopulation: Adults whose mammographic assessment includes breast calcifications.

claim.breast-imaging.calcification.typic.statement: Vascular, large rod-like, rim, layering, and coarse densely calcified patterns are among calcification appearances categorized as typically benign in the current mammography lexicon.
claim.breast-imaging.calcification.typic.limitation: The classification belongs within the complete radiologist assessment and cannot override other suspicious findings.
claim.breast-imaging.calcification.typic.applicablePopulation: Adults whose mammographic assessment includes breast calcifications.

claim.breast-imaging.suspicion-is-not-ti.statement: Suspicious breast imaging warrants the indicated diagnostic pathway and does not by itself establish a cancer diagnosis or authorize cancer-directed surgery without tissue diagnosis.
claim.breast-imaging.suspicion-is-not-ti.limitation: This package teaches imaging-feature recognition only; biopsy technique and cancer treatment are separate concepts.
claim.breast-imaging.suspicion-is-not-ti.applicablePopulation: Adults with breast imaging assessed as suspicious or highly suggestive of malignancy.

claim.breast-mass.age-30-to-39.initial-d.statement: For a woman age 30 to 39 with a new palpable breast mass, diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis and targeted breast ultrasound are appropriate components of the initial diagnostic imaging evaluation.
claim.breast-mass.age-30-to-39.initial-d.limitation: Only one adequate authoritative source is mapped. The exact combined-order question wording and distractors remain pending named-clinician review.
claim.breast-mass.age-30-to-39.initial-d.applicablePopulation: Nonpregnant, nonlactating, average-risk adult women age 30 to 39 with a new persistent palpable breast mass and no overt inflammatory findings.

claim.mondor-disease.classic-clinical-ph.statement: A newly developed, tender, cord-like superficial structure along the anterolateral breast or chest wall with little surrounding inflammation is characteristic of Mondor disease, a superficial thrombophlebitis.
claim.mondor-disease.classic-clinical-ph.limitation: Atypical, progressive, recurrent, systemic, or mass-associated findings require evaluation for alternative or secondary causes rather than pattern recognition alone.
claim.mondor-disease.classic-clinical-ph.applicablePopulation: Stable adults presenting with a new superficial breast or anterior chest-wall cord and no systemic illness.

claim.mondor-disease.selective-imaging-e.statement: When the diagnosis is uncertain, targeted high-frequency ultrasound with color Doppler can evaluate a suspected thrombosed superficial vein; age-appropriate diagnostic breast imaging is also appropriate when focal symptoms warrant evaluation for underlying breast pathology.
claim.mondor-disease.selective-imaging-e.limitation: This is a selective imaging pathway, not a claim that every classic uncomplicated presentation requires the same mammography-plus-ultrasound package.
claim.mondor-disease.selective-imaging-e.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a suspected superficial breast or chest-wall venous cord when the diagnosis is uncertain or a clinician must evaluate clinically significant focal breast symptoms or possible underlying pathology.

claim.mondor-disease.ultrasound-phenotyp.statement: A noncompressible subcutaneous tubular structure with absent internal color-Doppler flow supports thrombosis of a superficial vein in the appropriate clinical setting.
claim.mondor-disease.ultrasound-phenotyp.limitation: The finding must be interpreted with the examination and does not substitute for evaluation of a suspicious solid mass, abscess, or progressive inflammatory breast changes.
claim.mondor-disease.ultrasound-phenotyp.applicablePopulation: Stable adults undergoing targeted ultrasound for a suspected superficial breast or chest-wall venous thrombosis.

claim.mondor-disease.supportive-manageme.statement: Uncomplicated Mondor disease is generally self-limited and may be managed with supportive measures such as warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate, avoidance of local irritation, and follow-up; antibiotics, venous excision, and routine therapeutic anticoagulation are not standard without another indication.
claim.mondor-disease.supportive-manageme.limitation: Progressive diffuse breast change, adenopathy, a suspicious mass, infection, recurrent or migratory thrombophlebitis, or a known hypercoagulable condition falls outside this uncomplicated supportive-care pathway.
claim.mondor-disease.supportive-manageme.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a concordant uncomplicated superficial breast or chest-wall thrombophlebitis after appropriate clinical evaluation.

claim.postoperative-abdominal-symptoms.c.statement: For a hemodynamically stable patient with progressive nonlocalized abdominal symptoms after extensive abdominal surgery, contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis is an appropriate initial cross-sectional study to evaluate the extent of fluid and look for other postoperative complications.
claim.postoperative-abdominal-symptoms.c.limitation: This is a scoped initial-imaging choice for the approved stable presentation. Hemodynamic instability, peritonitis, a dominant organ-specific syndrome, or a contraindication to contrast requires a different pathway.
claim.postoperative-abdominal-symptoms.c.applicablePopulation: Hemodynamically stable adults with progressive abdominal swelling and discomfort after extensive abdominal surgery.

claim.chylous-ascites.imaging-does-not-c.statement: Cross-sectional imaging can demonstrate and localize ascites but cannot by appearance alone establish that the fluid is chylous.
claim.chylous-ascites.imaging-does-not-c.limitation: Imaging remains useful for extent, associated pathology, and procedural planning; this claim addresses fluid composition rather than overall imaging utility.
claim.chylous-ascites.imaging-does-not-c.applicablePopulation: Adults with postoperative intraperitoneal fluid under evaluation for possible chylous ascites.

claim.chylous-ascites.fluid-analysis-con.statement: Suspected postoperative chylous ascites requires diagnostic fluid sampling with triglyceride measurement and studies directed at infection and other plausible postoperative leaks rather than diagnosis from imaging appearance alone.
claim.chylous-ascites.fluid-analysis-con.limitation: The exact ancillary fluid studies depend on the operation and differential diagnosis. This approved concept does not teach an unsourced universal numeric triglyceride cutoff.
claim.chylous-ascites.fluid-analysis-con.applicablePopulation: Stable postoperative adults with newly identified ascites and suspected lymphatic leakage.

claim.postoperative-chylous-ascites.init.statement: Initial hospital management of large, symptomatic, reaccumulating postoperative chylous ascites can include symptom-directed peritoneal drainage, restriction of long-chain triglycerides with medium-chain triglyceride enrichment, and monitoring of nutrition, fluid, and electrolytes.
claim.postoperative-chylous-ascites.init.limitation: Evidence is heterogeneous, drainage is symptom- and accumulation-dependent, and persistent or severe refractory leakage may require individualized lymphatic localization, intervention, or surgery. This claim does not impose a rigid escalation timeline.
claim.postoperative-chylous-ascites.init.applicablePopulation: Hemodynamically stable postoperative adults with confirmed large, symptomatic, reaccumulating chylous ascites.

claim.vitamin-c.collagen-proline-lysine-.statement: Vitamin C, or ascorbate, is a required cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase activity during collagen biosynthesis.
claim.vitamin-c.collagen-proline-lysine-.limitation: The biochemical role applies to collagen biosynthesis broadly and should not be taught as unique to type III collagen.
claim.vitamin-c.collagen-proline-lysine-.applicablePopulation: General human collagen biosynthesis and perioperative wound-healing education.

claim.vitamin-c.collagen-stability-and-w.statement: Inadequate vitamin C impairs proline and lysine hydroxylation, compromising normal collagen maturation and stability and contributing to impaired wound healing.
claim.vitamin-c.collagen-stability-and-w.limitation: This mechanism does not establish that vitamin C deficiency is the cause of every impaired wound or that supplementation improves healing in every patient.
claim.vitamin-c.collagen-stability-and-w.applicablePopulation: General human collagen biosynthesis and perioperative wound-healing education.

claim.vitamin-c.supplementation-not-univ.statement: The established biochemical requirement for vitamin C does not by itself justify routine high-dose supplementation as a universal treatment for every well-nourished postoperative patient.
claim.vitamin-c.supplementation-not-univ.limitation: Clinical supplementation evidence varies across populations and wound types; this concept teaches mechanism and does not prescribe a dose or treatment protocol.
claim.vitamin-c.supplementation-not-univ.applicablePopulation: Postoperative patients without a separately established vitamin C deficiency or condition-specific supplementation indication.

claim.gastric-malt.integrated-pathologic.statement: Gastric MALT lymphoma is recognized by an integrated pathologic pattern that includes a small B-cell infiltrate with gland-infiltrating lymphoepithelial lesions and a compatible immunophenotype, commonly CD20 positive with CD5, CD10, and cyclin D1 absent.
claim.gastric-malt.integrated-pathologic.limitation: CD20 establishes B-cell lineage but is not specific for MALT lymphoma. Diagnosis requires integrated morphology and immunophenotyping, with additional evaluation when a limited biopsy is equivocal.
claim.gastric-malt.integrated-pathologic.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing pathologic evaluation of a gastric lymphoid infiltrate obtained by endoscopic biopsy.

claim.gastric-malt.hpylori-eradication-i.statement: For confirmed localized low-grade gastric MALT lymphoma associated with H. pylori and without large-cell transformation or another adverse presentation, H. pylori eradication is appropriate initial lymphoma-directed treatment without concurrent gastrectomy, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy.
claim.gastric-malt.hpylori-eradication-i.limitation: The exact eradication regimen depends on current local resistance patterns, allergies, prior antibiotic exposure, and applicable H. pylori guidance; this concept does not prescribe a regimen.
claim.gastric-malt.hpylori-eradication-i.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed localized low-grade H. pylori-positive gastric MALT lymphoma without transformation or immediately threatening disease.

claim.gastric-malt.eradication-confirmat.statement: Initial eradication treatment must be followed by confirmation that H. pylori was eradicated and by endoscopic biopsy reassessment of lymphoma response rather than being treated as a one-time antibiotic prescription with no follow-up.
claim.gastric-malt.eradication-confirmat.limitation: Lymphoma regression can be delayed. Exact follow-up intervals and subsequent management depend on eradication status, pathology, symptoms, stage, and adverse features.
claim.gastric-malt.eradication-confirmat.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving H. pylori eradication as initial treatment for gastric MALT lymphoma.

claim.gastric-malt.progression-and-trans.statement: Large-cell transformation, clinically significant progression, threatening organ effects, or failure after an adequate eradication pathway requires reassessment and may require radiotherapy or systemic lymphoma treatment rather than repetition of an eradication-only strategy.
claim.gastric-malt.progression-and-trans.limitation: This boundary does not assign one universal second-line treatment; subsequent therapy is individualized to stage, pathology, symptoms, prior response, and specialist assessment.
claim.gastric-malt.progression-and-trans.applicablePopulation: Adults with gastric MALT lymphoma outside the classic localized low-grade eradication-first presentation or with an inadequate response.

claim.gastroparesis.diagnostic-framework.statement: Gastroparesis is diagnosed in a patient with compatible upper gastrointestinal symptoms by documenting objectively delayed gastric emptying after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claim.gastroparesis.diagnostic-framework.limitation: Compatible symptoms alone are not diagnostic, and this concept assumes that an appropriate prior evaluation has already excluded mechanical obstruction.
claim.gastroparesis.diagnostic-framework.applicablePopulation: Adults with chronic nausea, vomiting, early satiety, or postprandial fullness and no demonstrated mechanical gastric-outlet obstruction.

claim.gastroparesis.four-hour-solid-meal.statement: Four-hour solid-meal gastric emptying scintigraphy is the preferred objective study in this concept for suspected gastroparesis after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claim.gastroparesis.four-hour-solid-meal.limitation: The 2022 ACG guideline recommends solid-meal scintigraphy for at least three hours, while the 2025 AGA guideline specifically favors four-hour testing over studies lasting two hours or less. This concept does not teach an exact abnormal-retention cutoff.
claim.gastroparesis.four-hour-solid-meal.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing objective evaluation for suspected gastroparesis after mechanical obstruction has been excluded.

claim.gastroparesis.nonemptying-test-bou.statement: Upper endoscopy can help exclude mechanical obstruction but does not replace objective gastric emptying measurement; esophageal manometry and ambulatory pH monitoring evaluate different physiologic questions.
claim.gastroparesis.nonemptying-test-bou.limitation: Other validated gastric-emptying modalities may have selected roles. They are not taught or used as false distractors in this narrowly approved scintigraphic-testing concept.
claim.gastroparesis.nonemptying-test-bou.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing outpatient evaluation for suspected gastroparesis.

claim.postoperative-ileus.persistent-ent.statement: The approved prolonged postoperative-ileus presentation requires persistent severe gastrointestinal dysfunction beyond seven postoperative days, exclusion of mechanical obstruction or another precipitating diagnosis, and inability to tolerate adequate oral or enteral nutrition.
claim.postoperative-ileus.persistent-ent.limitation: A postoperative-day number or high nasogastric output alone is insufficient. Nutritional status, likely duration, reversible contributors, and oral or enteral feasibility remain clinically important.
claim.postoperative-ileus.persistent-ent.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults with prolonged severe postoperative ileus after major abdominal surgery.

claim.postoperative-ileus.parenteral-nut.statement: Parenteral nutrition is appropriate nutritional support in the approved presentation when prolonged postoperative ileus prevents adequate oral or enteral nutrition beyond seven days and mechanical obstruction has been excluded.
claim.postoperative-ileus.parenteral-nut.limitation: This scope does not establish a universal instruction to delay nutrition until day seven. Malnutrition, high metabolic risk, critical illness, expected duration, and partial enteral tolerance can change timing and whether supplemental or total parenteral nutrition is used.
claim.postoperative-ileus.parenteral-nut.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults with persistent severe postoperative ileus who cannot use the gastrointestinal route for adequate nutrition.

claim.postoperative-ileus.nutrition-not-.statement: Parenteral nutrition supplies nutrients while oral and enteral feeding are infeasible; it does not directly restore bowel motility, replace evaluation for obstruction, or prevent resumption of enteral feeding when gastrointestinal function returns.
claim.postoperative-ileus.nutrition-not-.limitation: Ongoing ileus management and reassessment are outside this single nutritional-support concept.
claim.postoperative-ileus.nutrition-not-.applicablePopulation: Hospitalized adults receiving parenteral nutrition because prolonged postoperative ileus prevents adequate oral or enteral feeding.

claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.prophylacti.statement: Routine prophylactic splenectomy does not improve survival during curative gastrectomy for resectable proximal gastric adenocarcinoma without greater-curvature invasion, direct splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.
claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.prophylacti.limitation: This claim applies to prophylactic splenectomy in the defined proximal-gastric-cancer population and must not be generalized to every gastric tumor or to a therapeutic splenectomy indication.
claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.prophylacti.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing curative resection for proximal gastric adenocarcinoma without greater-curvature invasion, splenic invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease.

claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.prophylacti.statement: In the approved population, adding prophylactic splenectomy increases operative morbidity while spleen preservation maintains oncologic survival.
claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.prophylacti.limitation: The package does not teach exact complication rates or substitute this population-level result for individualized operative planning.
claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.prophylacti.applicablePopulation: Adults in the approved proximal-gastric-cancer operative population.

claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.spleen-pres.statement: The spleen-preservation teaching point is not a rule that splenectomy is never appropriate; direct splenic invasion, greater-curvature invasion, or suspected splenic-hilar disease falls outside the approved routine-prophylaxis scenario.
claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.spleen-pres.limitation: Falling outside this scope does not by itself prescribe splenectomy; the specific operative decision remains separately authored clinical content.
claim.gastric-adenocarcinoma.spleen-pres.applicablePopulation: Adults being evaluated for curative proximal gastric-cancer surgery.

claim.severe-burn.early-enteral-nutritio.statement: For an extensively burned patient who has been adequately resuscitated and has no enteral contraindication, enteral nutrition should begin as soon as feasible within the first 24 hours after injury.
claim.severe-burn.early-enteral-nutritio.limitation: The evidence supports early feeding but does not establish eight hours as a universal cutoff. The exact start depends on resuscitation, hemodynamic status, access, contraindications, and clinical feasibility.
claim.severe-burn.early-enteral-nutritio.applicablePopulation: Patients with extensive burns who are adequately resuscitated, hemodynamically stable, unable to meet nutritional needs orally, and without a contraindication to enteral nutrition.

claim.severe-burn.enteral-route-preferre.statement: When the gastrointestinal tract is usable, enteral nutrition is the preferred initial route for nutritional support after an extensive burn rather than routine first-line parenteral nutrition.
claim.severe-burn.enteral-route-preferre.limitation: This claim does not prescribe a feeding-access site, formula, advancement protocol, or management plan when adequate enteral nutrition is infeasible or contraindicated.
claim.severe-burn.enteral-route-preferre.applicablePopulation: Patients with extensive burns who require nutritional support and have a usable gastrointestinal tract.

claim.severe-burn.early-enteral-nutritio.statement: The approved early-enteral-nutrition rule requires adequate resuscitation and no enteral contraindication; ongoing shock, incomplete resuscitation, suspected intestinal ischemia, or mechanical obstruction falls outside this teaching scenario.
claim.severe-burn.early-enteral-nutritio.limitation: Falling outside the approved scenario does not itself specify parenteral nutrition or another intervention; those decisions require separately authored clinical content.
claim.severe-burn.early-enteral-nutritio.applicablePopulation: Patients with extensive burns being assessed for initiation of enteral nutritional support.

claim.ventral-hernia.controlled-enteroto.statement: In a stable adult undergoing ventral or incisional hernia repair, a recognized small-bowel enterotomy that has been securely repaired with adequate source control, minimal controlled contamination, and no ongoing gross spillage does not automatically preclude a selected single-stage mesh repair.
claim.ventral-hernia.controlled-enteroto.limitation: Direct evidence for an inadvertent enterotomy during elective repair remains limited. Whether to continue, convert, or defer repair requires individualized judgment; this approved concept begins only after the team has determined that single-stage repair is appropriate.
claim.ventral-hernia.controlled-enteroto.applicablePopulation: Stable adults undergoing ventral or incisional hernia repair after immediate recognition and secure repair of a small-bowel enterotomy with controlled contamination and no gross spillage.

claim.ventral-hernia.controlled-contamin.statement: When a selected single-stage ventral or incisional hernia repair proceeds after controlled enterotomy, permanent macroporous monofilament synthetic mesh is preferred over defaulting to biologic, microporous multifilament, or rapidly absorbable mesh solely because the field is clean-contaminated.
claim.ventral-hernia.controlled-contamin.limitation: The randomized trial addresses elective clean-contaminated and contaminated repairs rather than the exact inadvertent-enterotomy scenario, and the current EHS recommendation is conditional with low to very-low evidence certainty. Mesh plane, fixation, and direct bowel contact are not addressed by this concept.
claim.ventral-hernia.controlled-contamin.applicablePopulation: Selected stable adults proceeding with single-stage ventral or incisional hernia repair after adequate source control in a minimally contaminated field.

claim.ventral-hernia.enterotomy-mesh-sel.statement: Unstable physiology, uncertain bowel viability, an unrecognized or delayed enterotomy, incomplete source control, or persistent gross enteric or feculent spillage falls outside the approved macroporous-synthetic-mesh selection rule.
claim.ventral-hernia.enterotomy-mesh-sel.limitation: Falling outside this scope does not by itself prescribe tissue repair, biologic mesh, staged reconstruction, or abandonment; those operative decisions require separately authored content.
claim.ventral-hernia.enterotomy-mesh-sel.applicablePopulation: Adults with an enterotomy or gastrointestinal contamination encountered during ventral or incisional hernia repair.

claim.thoracic-trauma.right-thoracotomy-.statement: A right thoracotomy directly exposes the proximal or middle intrathoracic esophagus, intrathoracic trachea, and azygos vein and can therefore address selected combinations of localized injuries to those structures.
claim.thoracic-trauma.right-thoracotomy-.limitation: Exposure is not equivalent to a universal operative recommendation. Hemodynamic state, exact injury level, trajectory, associated injuries, pleural contamination, and need for vascular or cardiac control may require a different or extended incision.
claim.thoracic-trauma.right-thoracotomy-.applicablePopulation: Trauma patients with localized intrathoracic injuries undergoing operative exposure selection after initial assessment.

claim.thoracic-trauma.planned-right-post.statement: For a sufficiently stable trauma patient undergoing planned open repair of a localized upper or middle thoracic esophageal injury, a right posterolateral thoracotomy is an appropriate exposure; selected associated azygos or intrathoracic tracheal injuries can reinforce the right-sided choice.
claim.thoracic-trauma.planned-right-post.limitation: This claim assumes that the injury is localized and the patient can undergo a planned definitive exposure. Distal esophageal injuries are generally approached from the left, and the side of major pleural contamination or a competing cardiac or great-vessel injury can change the incision.
claim.thoracic-trauma.planned-right-post.applicablePopulation: Hemodynamically stable or stabilized trauma patients with a localized upper or middle thoracic esophageal injury selected for planned open repair.

claim.thoracic-trauma.resuscitative-inci.statement: A planned right posterolateral thoracotomy is not the default incision for a patient in traumatic arrest or extremis who requires immediate resuscitative chest access; resuscitative access is generally anterior and may require left anterolateral or clamshell exposure according to the suspected injury and local protocol.
claim.thoracic-trauma.resuscitative-inci.limitation: This boundary does not define eligibility for resuscitative thoracotomy or prescribe one incision for every arrest scenario. Those indications and technique choices require separate content.
claim.thoracic-trauma.resuscitative-inci.applicablePopulation: Trauma patients being assessed for immediate resuscitative versus planned definitive thoracic exposure.

claim.meckel-diverticulum.resection-exte.statement: For a symptomatic Meckel diverticulum, inflammation or disruption involving the diverticular base and adjacent ileum favors bowel-inclusive resection over simple diverticulectomy; segmental ileal resection is appropriate when adjacent ileum is involved.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.resection-exte.limitation: Wedge and segmental resection can both be reasonable in selected base-involved cases. The approved segmental-resection variants therefore specify adjacent ileal involvement rather than using base width alone.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.resection-exte.applicablePopulation: Adolescent or adult patients with a symptomatic Meckel diverticulum identified during abdominal exploration.

claim.meckel-diverticulum.long-narrow-ti.statement: Simple diverticulectomy is an appropriate resection for a long, narrow Meckel diverticulum when uncomplicated inflammation is confined to the distal tip and the base and adjacent ileum are healthy.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.long-narrow-ti.limitation: Macroscopic morphology does not perfectly predict heterotopic tissue. This claim does not extend to bleeding, tumor, obstruction, base perforation, or adjacent ileal disease.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.long-narrow-ti.applicablePopulation: Adolescent or adult patients with a symptomatic long, narrow Meckel diverticulum and inflammation confined to the distal tip.

claim.meckel-diverticulum.two-centimeter.statement: One retrospective series of 15 adults with perforated Meckel diverticula operationally classified a base width of 2 cm or greater as broad and less than 2 cm as narrow.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.two-centimeter.limitation: This is a source-specific operational definition from a small perforation series, not a validated universal cutoff and not an independent indication for segmental resection.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.two-centimeter.applicablePopulation: Adults with perforated Meckel diverticulum in the cited retrospective series.

claim.meckel-diverticulum.size-alone-not.statement: No exact base-width measurement should be treated as a universal stand-alone rule for Meckel resection extent; disease location and the integrity of the base and adjacent ileum remain necessary operative context.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.size-alone-not.limitation: Morphology studies are retrospective and partly conflicting. Diverticulum length greater than 2 cm is a separate observation about symptomatic risk and must not be confused with a 2 cm base-width definition.
claim.meckel-diverticulum.size-alone-not.applicablePopulation: Patients with a Meckel diverticulum undergoing operative assessment.

claim.aaa.female-sex-associated-perioper.statement: Contemporary pooled and national-registry evidence reports higher observed perioperative mortality among women than men after elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.
claim.aaa.female-sex-associated-perioper.limitation: The evidence is derived primarily from observational cohorts and pooled observational estimates; it supports an association rather than a causal or patient-specific prediction.
claim.aaa.female-sex-associated-perioper.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm; the approved concept is limited to counseling about population-level perioperative outcomes.

claim.aaa.sex-disparity-reported-after-e.statement: Higher observed perioperative mortality among women has been reported after both endovascular and open elective repair of intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.
claim.aaa.sex-disparity-reported-after-e.limitation: Effect estimates and contributing mechanisms vary across cohorts, anatomy, repair approach, era, and adjustment methods; the claim does not compare an individual patient's suitability for EVAR versus open repair.
claim.aaa.sex-disparity-reported-after-e.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving elective EVAR or open repair for intact abdominal aortic aneurysm.

claim.aaa.sex-association-is-not-individ.statement: A sex-associated difference in population-level operative outcomes informs counseling and risk assessment but does not determine an individual patient's outcome or make female sex a contraindication to repair.
claim.aaa.sex-association-is-not-individ.limitation: Individual risk still depends on anatomy, comorbidity, repair approach, center experience, and other patient-specific factors not taught by this concept.
claim.aaa.sex-association-is-not-individ.applicablePopulation: Learners interpreting observed sex-associated AAA repair outcomes during counseling without converting the association into deterministic treatment advice.

claim.aaa.repair-threshold-and-early-rep.statement: The 2022 ACC/AHA guideline recommends elective repair of an unruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm at a maximum diameter of at least 5.5 cm in men or at least 5.0 cm in women, and trials of routine repair for smaller asymptomatic aneurysms did not demonstrate a survival benefit.
claim.aaa.repair-threshold-and-early-rep.limitation: Diameter is not the only management consideration; symptoms, growth, anatomy, operative risk, patient preference, and specialist assessment remain relevant. This claim is used only to bound distractors in the approved concept.
claim.aaa.repair-threshold-and-early-rep.applicablePopulation: Adults with unruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm being evaluated for surveillance or elective repair.

claim.desmoid.initial-active-surveillanc.statement: Active surveillance through an experienced multidisciplinary team is an appropriate initial strategy for many newly diagnosed desmoid tumors that are stable, minimally symptomatic, and not threatening a critical structure or meaningful function.
claim.desmoid.initial-active-surveillanc.limitation: Surveillance is an active specialist-management strategy, not absence of follow-up; this concept does not specify a universal imaging interval or apply to persistent progression, critical-site threat, obstruction, or meaningful functional decline.
claim.desmoid.initial-active-surveillanc.applicablePopulation: Patients with biopsy-confirmed, newly diagnosed desmoid tumor without persistent progression, critical-site threat, obstruction, or meaningful functional deterioration.

claim.desmoid.active-treatment-after-per.statement: Active treatment may be considered after persistent radiologic or clinical progression or when desmoid disease threatens a critical structure or meaningful function.
claim.desmoid.active-treatment-after-per.limitation: The choice of active treatment is individualized by location, tempo, symptoms, expected morbidity, patient goals, and specialist review; progression does not make one treatment universal.
claim.desmoid.active-treatment-after-per.applicablePopulation: Patients with desmoid tumor demonstrating persistent progression, critical-site threat, pain, obstruction, or meaningful functional deterioration.

claim.desmoid.progressing-abdominal-wall.statement: After multidisciplinary review, surgery can be proposed for a progressing, symptomatic, resectable abdominal-wall desmoid when expected morbidity is acceptably low.
claim.desmoid.progressing-abdominal-wall.limitation: This location-specific option does not make surgery mandatory and should not be generalized to mesenteric, head-and-neck, chest-wall, extremity, or other disease where medical or other local treatment may better preserve function.
claim.desmoid.progressing-abdominal-wall.applicablePopulation: Patients with persistently progressing abdominal-wall desmoid tumor causing meaningful pain or functional limitation and an acceptably low expected morbidity from resection.

claim.desmoid.function-preserving-margin.statement: When surgery is selected for desmoid tumor, preservation of function and cosmesis may justify accepting a microscopically positive margin rather than pursuing a wider resection with avoidable morbidity.
claim.desmoid.function-preserving-margin.limitation: This is not permission to perform an unplanned incomplete operation; operative goals and acceptable morbidity require specialist multidisciplinary planning.
claim.desmoid.function-preserving-margin.applicablePopulation: Patients selected for desmoid resection when a wider microscopic margin would cause avoidable functional or cosmetic harm.

claim.desmoid.nonmetastatic-locally-aggr.statement: Desmoid tumors may grow infiltratively and recur locally but do not metastasize; symptoms or progression do not convert them into metastatic malignancies.
claim.desmoid.nonmetastatic-locally-aggr.limitation: Lack of metastatic potential does not make locally progressive or critical-site disease harmless.
claim.desmoid.nonmetastatic-locally-aggr.applicablePopulation: Patients with pathologically confirmed desmoid-type fibromatosis.

claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.high-risk-st.statement: Peptic ulcers with active spurting, active oozing, or a nonbleeding visible vessel are high-risk endoscopic findings for which endoscopic hemostasis is indicated.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.high-risk-st.limitation: This claim assumes the patient has been appropriately assessed and stabilized for endoscopy; it does not define pre-endoscopy resuscitation, transfusion, medication, or disposition decisions.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.high-risk-st.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing upper endoscopy for suspected or confirmed nonvariceal peptic-ulcer bleeding.

claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.clean-base-f.statement: A clean-based peptic ulcer or a flat pigmented spot does not require endoscopic hemostatic treatment solely for that stigma.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.clean-base-f.limitation: The absence of an endoscopic hemostasis indication does not determine the complete medical treatment, cause-specific therapy, observation need, or discharge plan.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.clean-base-f.applicablePopulation: Adults whose upper endoscopy shows a peptic ulcer with a clean base or flat pigmented spot and no separate high-risk bleeding stigma.

claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.nonbleeding-.statement: A nonbleeding visible vessel may be treated with an accepted thermal or mechanical hemostatic modality as monotherapy, or with such a definitive modality combined with epinephrine injection.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.nonbleeding-.limitation: The concept does not claim that every available modality is equivalent in every lesion, that two definitive modalities are routinely required, or that device selection is independent of anatomy, expertise, and equipment.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.nonbleeding-.applicablePopulation: Adults with a peptic ulcer containing a nonbleeding visible vessel during upper endoscopy.

claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.epinephrine-.statement: Epinephrine injection should not be used as the sole definitive endoscopic treatment for a high-risk bleeding peptic ulcer; when epinephrine is selected, it must be paired with a definitive hemostatic modality.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.epinephrine-.limitation: This claim does not require epinephrine in every hemostatic plan and does not make an accepted thermal, mechanical, or selected advanced modality inadequate merely because injection was omitted.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.epinephrine-.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving endoscopic hemostasis for a peptic ulcer with active bleeding or a nonbleeding visible vessel when epinephrine injection is under consideration.

claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.active-bleed.statement: A conventional combination pathway for an actively bleeding peptic ulcer uses dilute epinephrine injection for temporary control followed by contact thermal or mechanical hemostasis.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.active-bleed.limitation: This is a conventional pathway, not a claim that every actively bleeding ulcer must receive epinephrine or that selected contemporary OTS-clip or hemostatic-forceps monotherapy is never appropriate.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.active-bleed.applicablePopulation: Appropriately stabilized adults undergoing hospital endoscopy for an actively bleeding peptic ulcer when the conventional epinephrine-combination pathway is selected.

claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.selected-adv.statement: Current guidance recognizes selected advanced monotherapy options, including over-the-scope clipping for certain high-risk actively bleeding ulcers and hemostatic forceps with soft coagulation, so generic clip or cautery monotherapy cannot be labeled universally wrong.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.selected-adv.limitation: The exact choice depends on lesion characteristics, device type, technical competence, local resources, and recommendation strength; these advanced options are boundaries for distractor authoring rather than scored content in this package.
claim.peptic-ulcer-bleeding.selected-adv.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing expert endoscopic hemostasis for high-risk peptic-ulcer bleeding.

claim.quality-improvement.pdsa-linked-it.statement: PDSA is an iterative learning method: teams test a change on a limited scale, study what happened, refine the change, and use linked cycles to build toward broader implementation when results support it.
claim.quality-improvement.pdsa-linked-it.limitation: This claim does not establish the appropriate aim, measures, sample size, duration, or implementation threshold for a particular project.
claim.quality-improvement.pdsa-linked-it.applicablePopulation: Healthcare teams conducting structured quality-improvement tests, including ambulatory-surgery teams.

claim.quality-improvement.act-adopt-adap.statement: After studying a test's results, the Act step uses those findings to adopt, adapt, or abandon the tested change and to prepare the next test as appropriate.
claim.quality-improvement.act-adopt-adap.limitation: The three labels summarize a decision framework; the specific decision still depends on the project's prespecified aim, results, balancing measures, and operational context.
claim.quality-improvement.act-adopt-adap.applicablePopulation: Healthcare teams that have completed and studied a limited quality-improvement test.

claim.quality-improvement.next-step-foll.statement: The next quality-improvement action should follow the observed results: expand a successful change cautiously, revise and retest a partially successful change, or stop or redesign an unsuccessful change rather than switching methods or continuing unchanged automatically.
claim.quality-improvement.next-step-foll.limitation: Root-cause analysis or another improvement framework may be useful for a separately defined problem; this claim only rejects their automatic use solely because a PDSA test has reached the Act step.
claim.quality-improvement.next-step-foll.applicablePopulation: Healthcare quality-improvement teams choosing a next action after reviewing a completed test of change.

claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.body-tai.statement: When operative resection is selected for resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the body or tail, the anatomic pancreatic resection is a distal pancreatectomy rather than a pancreaticoduodenectomy.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.body-tai.limitation: This location-based operation does not determine treatment sequencing or establish resectability by itself.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.body-tai.applicablePopulation: Adults with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the pancreatic body or tail who are selected to proceed with operative resection.

claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.distal-r.statement: Standard oncologic distal resection for pancreatic body or tail adenocarcinoma includes splenectomy as part of distal pancreatectomy and regional oncologic clearance.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.distal-r.limitation: This approved teaching point is specific to confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma and does not define the operation for benign distal lesions, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, trauma, or other non-adenocarcinoma indications.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.distal-r.applicablePopulation: Adults with resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in the body or tail who are selected for oncologic resection.

claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.surgical.statement: Absence of distant metastases is necessary but not sufficient to select pancreatic-cancer surgery; anatomic resectability, operative fitness, disease biology, and multidisciplinary treatment planning also matter.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.surgical.limitation: The approved variants state that the tumor has already been judged resectable and ask which operation or referral follows if surgery proceeds; they do not choose neoadjuvant versus upfront treatment.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.surgical.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary evaluation for potentially resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.operatio.statement: Pancreaticoduodenectomy is used for pancreatic head or uncinate cancer, while distal pancreatectomy is used for pancreatic body or tail cancer; total pancreatectomy is not required solely because a resectable cancer is in the tail.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.operatio.limitation: Multifocal or locally extensive disease can create separate indications for total pancreatectomy, but those scenarios are outside this concept.
claim.pancreatic-adenocarcinoma.operatio.applicablePopulation: Adults with localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma being considered for resection.

claim.felty-syndrome.ra-neutropenia-sple.statement: Felty syndrome is suggested by long-standing, usually seropositive rheumatoid arthritis with persistent neutropenia; splenomegaly is a characteristic supporting feature and recurrent infections may be the presenting problem.
claim.felty-syndrome.ra-neutropenia-sple.limitation: The pattern is not pathognomonic. The approved diagnostic vignette explicitly excludes medication, infection, and clonal large-granular-lymphocyte causes before asking for the syndrome.
claim.felty-syndrome.ra-neutropenia-sple.applicablePopulation: Adults with established rheumatoid arthritis and persistent otherwise-unexplained neutropenia.

claim.felty-syndrome.splenomegaly-not-re.statement: Splenomegaly is common in Felty syndrome but is not an absolute prerequisite; persistent neutropenia in the appropriate rheumatoid-arthritis context remains the essential hematologic feature.
claim.felty-syndrome.splenomegaly-not-re.limitation: A normal-sized spleen does not establish Felty syndrome and does not remove the need to investigate alternative causes of neutropenia.
claim.felty-syndrome.splenomegaly-not-re.applicablePopulation: Adults with rheumatoid arthritis and persistent neutropenia after alternative causes have been evaluated.

claim.felty-syndrome.exclude-clonal-lgl-.statement: T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia and other hematologic, infectious, autoimmune, and medication-related causes can resemble Felty syndrome and require explicit exclusion rather than diagnosis from the triad alone.
claim.felty-syndrome.exclude-clonal-lgl-.limitation: This package does not teach the complete hematologic workup or a separate T-LGL diagnosis concept.
claim.felty-syndrome.exclude-clonal-lgl-.applicablePopulation: Adults with rheumatoid arthritis, neutropenia, and possible splenomegaly undergoing diagnostic evaluation.

claim.felty-syndrome.methotrexate-first-.statement: Methotrexate is the usual first-line disease-modifying treatment for confirmed Felty syndrome when treatment is indicated, with specialist monitoring of blood counts and clinical response.
claim.felty-syndrome.methotrexate-first-.limitation: Felty syndrome is rare and treatment evidence is based mainly on case reports and small case series rather than randomized trials; this concept does not prescribe a dose or monitoring interval.
claim.felty-syndrome.methotrexate-first-.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with confirmed Felty syndrome who do not have an active infection and have not yet received syndrome-directed disease-modifying treatment.

claim.felty-syndrome.glucocorticoid-gcsf.statement: Glucocorticoids or G-CSF may be used as temporary bridging or supportive therapy while disease-modifying treatment takes effect; glucocorticoids are not universally contraindicated but should be avoided in active infection and are not the preferred sole long-term strategy.
claim.felty-syndrome.glucocorticoid-gcsf.limitation: The approved questions do not prescribe a dose, duration, laboratory target, or universal bridging regimen.
claim.felty-syndrome.glucocorticoid-gcsf.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed Felty syndrome receiving specialist-directed treatment.

claim.felty-syndrome.splenectomy-refract.statement: Splenectomy is generally reserved for Felty syndrome with recurrent infections despite adequate medical treatment rather than used as routine initial therapy.
claim.felty-syndrome.splenectomy-refract.limitation: The exact likelihood and durability of hematologic response are not taught because the evidence is old, heterogeneous, and confounded by historical overlap with T-LGL leukemia.
claim.felty-syndrome.splenectomy-refract.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed Felty syndrome and recurrent infections despite adequate specialist-directed medical therapy.

claim.phyllodes.benign-complete-excision.statement: For benign phyllodes tumors, complete excision is the counseling target without a prescribed fixed-width margin.
claim.phyllodes.benign-complete-excision.limitation: Management wording is evidence-sensitive consensus guidance and does not establish a universal biological cutoff.
claim.phyllodes.benign-complete-excision.applicablePopulation: Patients with pathology-confirmed benign phyllodes tumors considering local treatment.

claim.phyllodes.benign-positive-margin-m.statement: A positive margin after benign phyllodes excision does not by itself require re-excision; residual or transected-tumor concern changes the discussion.
claim.phyllodes.benign-positive-margin-m.limitation: This is counseling guidance, not a substitute for individualized pathology and multidisciplinary review.
claim.phyllodes.benign-positive-margin-m.applicablePopulation: Patients with benign phyllodes tumors after complete excision and a positive margin.

claim.phyllodes.borderline-margin-target.statement: Borderline phyllodes counseling uses a 5-mm margin aim for complete excision planning.
claim.phyllodes.borderline-margin-target.limitation: The margin aim is consensus management guidance with evidence limitations, not a biological cliff.
claim.phyllodes.borderline-margin-target.applicablePopulation: Patients with borderline phyllodes tumors undergoing local treatment planning.

claim.phyllodes.borderline-close-margin-.statement: For borderline phyllodes, a margin below 3 mm supports re-excision and a 3-to-under-5-mm margin supports individualized re-excision discussion.
claim.phyllodes.borderline-close-margin-.limitation: Intervals are evidence-sensitive consensus management boundaries rather than universal biological cutoffs.
claim.phyllodes.borderline-close-margin-.applicablePopulation: Patients with borderline phyllodes tumors after excision with a close margin.

claim.phyllodes.malignant-margin-target.statement: Malignant phyllodes counseling uses a 10-mm margin aim for complete excision planning.
claim.phyllodes.malignant-margin-target.limitation: The margin aim is consensus management guidance with evidence limitations, not a biological cliff.
claim.phyllodes.malignant-margin-target.applicablePopulation: Patients with malignant phyllodes tumors undergoing local treatment planning.

claim.phyllodes.malignant-close-margin-m.statement: For malignant phyllodes, a margin below 5 mm supports re-excision; at 5 to under 10 mm, re-excision is recommended while surveillance may be considered only after explicit risk-benefit discussion.
claim.phyllodes.malignant-close-margin-m.limitation: Intervals are evidence-sensitive consensus management boundaries rather than universal biological cutoffs.
claim.phyllodes.malignant-close-margin-m.applicablePopulation: Patients with malignant phyllodes tumors after excision with a close margin.

claim.phyllodes.hematogenous-spread-patt.statement: Phyllodes tumors have a predominantly hematogenous metastatic pattern, with nodal spread uncommon relative to hematogenous spread.
claim.phyllodes.hematogenous-spread-patt.limitation: This describes a usual pattern and does not predict the course for an individual patient.
claim.phyllodes.hematogenous-spread-patt.applicablePopulation: Patients receiving counseling about malignant phyllodes tumor spread patterns.

claim.phyllodes.no-routine-axillary-stag.statement: Routine sentinel-node or axillary staging is not indicated for phyllodes tumors when axillary nodes are nonsuspicious.
claim.phyllodes.no-routine-axillary-stag.limitation: This boundary applies to nonsuspicious nodes and does not replace evaluation of a concerning axillary finding.
claim.phyllodes.no-routine-axillary-stag.applicablePopulation: Patients with benign, borderline, or malignant phyllodes tumors and nonsuspicious axillary nodes.

claim.phyllodes.suspicious-node-biopsy-e.statement: A suspicious axillary node in a patient with phyllodes history warrants image-guided histopathologic needle biopsy; biopsy-proven involvement may prompt axillary-dissection consideration after MDT discussion.
claim.phyllodes.suspicious-node-biopsy-e.limitation: This exception is driven by the suspicious-node evaluation and requires individualized multidisciplinary review.
claim.phyllodes.suspicious-node-biopsy-e.applicablePopulation: Patients with a phyllodes tumor history and a suspicious axillary node during follow-up.

claim.trauma-vka.scope.statement: Emergency VKA reversal teaching is limited to documented VKA/warfarin exposure with major or critical-site traumatic bleeding or an urgent intervention; an elevated INR alone does not establish that medication-specific pathway.
claim.trauma-vka.scope.limitation: Does not define all causes or management of INR elevation.
claim.trauma-vka.scope.applicablePopulation: Patients with documented VKA/warfarin exposure and traumatic major or critical-site bleeding, or an urgent intervention.

claim.trauma-vka.pcc-selection.statement: In the approved VKA emergency-reversal scope, 4F-PCC is the rapid clotting-factor replacement product; plasma is a fallback when 4F-PCC is unavailable.
claim.trauma-vka.pcc-selection.limitation: Does not provide dose, inventory, or patient-specific prescribing instructions.
claim.trauma-vka.pcc-selection.applicablePopulation: Patients within the approved VKA emergency-reversal teaching scope.

claim.trauma-vka.iv-vitamin-k.statement: IV vitamin K is paired with PCC in the approved VKA emergency-reversal teaching because vitamin K does not supply the immediate factor replacement provided by PCC.
claim.trauma-vka.iv-vitamin-k.limitation: No timing or dosing instruction is encoded.
claim.trauma-vka.iv-vitamin-k.applicablePopulation: Patients within the approved VKA emergency-reversal teaching scope.

claim.trauma-vka.pcc-vs-plasma.statement: Available 4F-PCC provides concentrated factor replacement with less infusion volume and more rapid preparation or administration than plasma in the approved VKA-reversal comparison.
claim.trauma-vka.pcc-vs-plasma.limitation: Does not replace hemorrhage control, resuscitation, or local protocol.
claim.trauma-vka.pcc-vs-plasma.applicablePopulation: Patients within the approved VKA emergency-reversal teaching scope when 4F-PCC and plasma are available.

claim.trauma-vka.composition.statement: The named procoagulant factors in the approved 4F-PCC teaching set are II, VII, IX, and X.
claim.trauma-vka.composition.limitation: Formulation details beyond the named teaching set are out of scope.
claim.trauma-vka.composition.applicablePopulation: Patients within the approved VKA emergency-reversal teaching scope.

claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.postsplen.statement: For the approved presentation of persistent anemia with biochemical hemolysis after documented total splenectomy, reassessment and evaluation for accessory splenic tissue is the selected next step.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.postsplen.limitation: MCV or RDW alone does not establish persistent hemolysis, and this narrow teaching path does not diagnose every cause of anemia after splenectomy.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.postsplen.applicablePopulation: Patients matching the approved hereditary-spherocytosis post-splenectomy presentations.

claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.absent-ho.statement: Absent Howell-Jolly bodies after splenectomy can support suspicion of residual functioning splenic tissue.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.absent-ho.limitation: Absence is supportive only; it is not independently diagnostic and is not sufficient to select surgery.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.absent-ho.applicablePopulation: Approved post-splenectomy hereditary-spherocytosis presentation with continued hemolysis.

claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.heat-dama.statement: Tc-99m heat-damaged RBC scintigraphy is the approved functional-tissue study for the constrained presentation after hereditary spherocytosis remains supported.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.heat-dama.limitation: The configured facility time is editorial game tuning rather than a clinical turnaround claim; this does not define a universal imaging sequence.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.heat-dama.applicablePopulation: Patients in the approved persistent-hemolysis functional-tissue evaluation presentation.

claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.confirmed.statement: For the approved profile with confirmed functioning accessory splenic tissue causing persistent symptomatic hereditary-spherocytosis hemolysis, referral to hospital surgery for removal is the selected management disposition.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.confirmed.limitation: Incidental tissue alone is not an indication, and this package does not simulate hospital surgery or endorse immediate reoperation before confirmation.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.confirmed.applicablePopulation: Patients matching the confirmed, symptomatic, persistent-hemolysis profile in the approved management variants.

claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.postsplen.statement: The approved pathway does not use steroids, IVIG, or embolization for persistent hereditary-spherocytosis hemolysis after splenectomy.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.postsplen.limitation: This is a scope boundary for the exact approved teaching pathway, not a broad claim about all indications for those interventions.
claim.hereditary-spherocytosis.postsplen.applicablePopulation: The seven approved row-57 variants only.

claim.accessory-spleen.splenic-hilum-com.statement: The splenic hilum is the most common location represented for an accessory spleen in this approved anatomy concept.
claim.accessory-spleen.splenic-hilum-com.limitation: The package intentionally omits an exact prevalence estimate and does not turn this common-location teaching point into a complete operative search rule.
claim.accessory-spleen.splenic-hilum-com.applicablePopulation: Patients represented by the approved clinic discussions surrounding referral for hospital splenectomy.

claim.accessory-spleen.location-teaching.statement: A common accessory-spleen location does not establish that inspection of that one location alone is sufficient during splenectomy.
claim.accessory-spleen.location-teaching.limitation: This concept does not address retained accessory tissue, recurrent hemolysis, completion splenectomy, reoperation, or any operative-management sequence.
claim.accessory-spleen.location-teaching.applicablePopulation: Learners applying the narrow location-recognition concept rather than an operative-management protocol.

claim.fhh.lifelong-mild-hypercalcemia-re.statement: FHH commonly presents as lifelong, nonprogressive mild hypercalcemia with normal or mildly increased PTH, typically low urinary calcium excretion, and often a family history of hypercalcemia.
claim.fhh.lifelong-mild-hypercalcemia-re.limitation: No individual feature is sufficient to distinguish FHH from primary hyperparathyroidism, and serum magnesium is not a reliable discriminator.
claim.fhh.lifelong-mild-hypercalcemia-re.applicablePopulation: Stable patients undergoing outpatient evaluation of persistent PTH-dependent hypercalcemia.

claim.fhh.paired-urine-serum-calcium-cre.statement: When FHH is suspected, urinary calcium excretion should be evaluated with a calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio calculated from concurrent serum measurements and a 24-hour urine calcium and creatinine collection.
claim.fhh.paired-urine-serum-calcium-cre.limitation: Collection quality, renal function, vitamin-D status, pregnancy, and thiazides can affect interpretation; the game does not treat the collection as localization imaging.
claim.fhh.paired-urine-serum-calcium-cre.applicablePopulation: Stable patients with persistent hypercalcemia and nonsuppressed PTH when FHH and primary hyperparathyroidism are being differentiated.

claim.fhh.low-cccr-supports-but-does-not.statement: A calcium-to-creatinine clearance ratio below 0.01 supports suspicion for FHH but cannot confirm the diagnosis by itself because values overlap with primary hyperparathyroidism.
claim.fhh.low-cccr-supports-but-does-not.limitation: The exact 0.01 threshold is used only as a source-supported screening clue, not as a standalone diagnostic cutoff.
claim.fhh.low-cccr-supports-but-does-not.applicablePopulation: Patients with interpretable paired serum and 24-hour urine calcium and creatinine measurements.

claim.fhh.genetic-and-family-confirmatio.statement: Suggestive biochemistry and family history should prompt family evaluation and genetic testing; a pathogenic FHH-associated variant can confirm the diagnosis, while negative testing does not exclude every clinically suspected case.
claim.fhh.genetic-and-family-confirmatio.limitation: Variants of uncertain significance and mutation-negative clinically suspected FHH require specialist interpretation; the approved questions use a pathogenic CASR result when confirmation is stated.
claim.fhh.genetic-and-family-confirmatio.applicablePopulation: Patients with a biochemical and family pattern that raises suspicion for FHH.

claim.fhh.reassurance-observation-avoid-.statement: Confirmed uncomplicated FHH is generally managed with reassurance and observation rather than parathyroid surgery, which usually does not correct the inherited calcium-sensing disorder.
claim.fhh.reassurance-observation-avoid-.limitation: Rare symptomatic or atypical FHH and coexisting primary hyperparathyroidism require specialist individualized management and are excluded from these variants.
claim.fhh.reassurance-observation-avoid-.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic patients with confirmed FHH, stable mild hypercalcemia, and no authored complication or coexisting primary hyperparathyroidism.

claim.men2a.manifestation-pattern.statement: MEN2A includes medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism in the approved recognition scope.
claim.men2a.manifestation-pattern.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata remains needs_clinician_review; exact question wording is separately approved.
claim.men2a.manifestation-pattern.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved MEN2A clinic variants.

claim.men2a.pheochromocytoma-priority.statement: A functioning pheochromocytoma must be excluded or addressed before thyroid intervention in the approved MEN2A scope.
claim.men2a.pheochromocytoma-priority.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata remains needs_clinician_review; exact question wording is separately approved.
claim.men2a.pheochromocytoma-priority.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved MEN2A clinic variants.

claim.pheochromocytoma.alpha-before-beta.statement: When both drug classes are used for a functioning pheochromocytoma, alpha blockade is established before beta blockade is added if indicated.
claim.pheochromocytoma.alpha-before-beta.limitation: Independently authored source/claim metadata remains needs_clinician_review; exact question wording is separately approved.
claim.pheochromocytoma.alpha-before-beta.applicablePopulation: Only patients represented by the exact approved MEN2A clinic variants.

claim.hcc.resection.favorable-compensate.statement: For the approved profile of a solitary HCC with preserved liver function, no clinically significant portal hypertension, adequate future liver remnant, and no macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic disease, hospital HPB-surgery referral for hepatic resection evaluation is the selected disposition.
claim.hcc.resection.favorable-compensate.limitation: This is a deliberately favorable multiparametric profile, not a universal treatment rule for every solitary HCC or every person with Child-Pugh A cirrhosis. EASL 2025 metadata was not locally verifiable, so this package records the single-source limitation rather than inventing a second citation.
claim.hcc.resection.favorable-compensate.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the owner-approved compensated-cirrhosis profiles in this package.

claim.hcc.resection.portal-hypertension-.statement: Clinically significant portal hypertension is one selection consideration in the approved favorable resection profile.
claim.hcc.resection.portal-hypertension-.limitation: This package does not teach clinically significant portal hypertension as an absolute contraindication to every limited hepatic resection, nor does it make preserved liver function alone sufficient for selection.
claim.hcc.resection.portal-hypertension-.applicablePopulation: Learners applying only the clear favorable-profile boundary in the approved cases.

claim.lymphangitis.distal-entry-proximal.statement: Acute lymphangitis can be recognized clinically when a distal skin entry site is accompanied by a tender erythematous streak extending proximally toward tender regional lymph nodes.
claim.lymphangitis.distal-entry-proximal.limitation: This narrow claim supports pattern recognition only; it does not establish an organism, severity, testing plan, treatment, prognosis, or disposition. MSD Manual Professional is the sole adequate targeted-verification source retained for this claim; an independent source has not yet been recorded.
claim.lymphangitis.distal-entry-proximal.applicablePopulation: Patients represented in the approved outpatient clinic vignettes with a distal skin entry site, proximal tender streak, and regional nodal tenderness.

claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.operable.statement: For the constrained approved profile of jaundice with completed cross-sectional imaging showing an operable distal malignant biliary obstruction, combined EUS-guided sampling and ERCP brushings is the selected tissue-evaluation plan.
claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.operable.limitation: This is a constrained BSG pathway after completed CT and MRI/MRCP, not a universal inference for every biliary stricture. CA 19-9 is not diagnostic confirmation, and the eight-hour result requirement is editorial simulation rather than clinical evidence.
claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.operable.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the approved completed-imaging distal-obstruction profiles without metastatic disease.

claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.distal-w.statement: For the approved fit patient with biopsy-confirmed resectable lower common-bile-duct cholangiocarcinoma and no distant disease, referral to hospital HPB surgery for pancreaticoduodenectomy is the selected operation pathway.
claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.distal-w.limitation: Distal pancreaticoduodenectomy referral is hospital-only and specialist-directed; this does not establish a universal operation for all cholangiocarcinoma locations or biliary strictures.
claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.distal-w.applicablePopulation: Fit adults with biopsy-confirmed resectable distal common-bile-duct cholangiocarcinoma and no distant disease in the approved variants.

claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.constrai.statement: Distal common-bile-duct disease near the pancreatic head is the location represented by the approved Whipple-referral variant.
claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.constrai.limitation: The package does not extend this location-to-operation relationship to perihilar or intrahepatic disease.
claim.distal-cholangiocarcinoma.constrai.applicablePopulation: The completed, biopsy-confirmed distal-location profile used only in the approved reverse-location variant.

claim.obstructive-jaundice.reduced-vitam.statement: Reduced bile delivery in obstructive jaundice can impair intestinal vitamin K absorption.
claim.obstructive-jaundice.reduced-vitam.limitation: This does not mean every patient with obstruction develops vitamin K deficiency or bleeding.
claim.obstructive-jaundice.reduced-vitam.applicablePopulation: Patients in the approved obstructive-jaundice teaching presentations.

claim.vitamin-k-deficiency.coagulopathy-.statement: Vitamin K deficiency can produce coagulation abnormalities including prolonged PT/INR and bleeding manifestations.
claim.vitamin-k-deficiency.coagulopathy-.limitation: This narrow concept does not establish a dose, treatment plan, timeline, or every possible cause of abnormal coagulation testing.
claim.vitamin-k-deficiency.coagulopathy-.applicablePopulation: Patients in the approved vitamin K-related coagulopathy presentations.

claim.gallbladder-polyp.european-sru-car.statement: The 2022 European guideline recommends cholecystectomy for gallbladder polyps measuring at least 10 mm and for 6-9 mm polyps with its specified risk factors, whereas the SRU and CAR framework uses morphology and generally places surgical consultation at 15 mm or lower when adjacent focal wall thickening is indeterminate.
claim.gallbladder-polyp.european-sru-car.limitation: The frameworks disagree on selected thresholds and surveillance details. This package does not teach a hybrid rule, an exact surveillance interval, or a disputed borderline profile.
claim.gallbladder-polyp.european-sru-car.applicablePopulation: Patients with incidentally detected gallbladder polyps whose completed ultrasound reports match the explicitly approved profiles.

claim.gallbladder-polyp.approved-concord.statement: For the owner-approved profiles, the teaching categories are referral for cholecystectomy evaluation for a 16 mm polyp or a 12 mm polyp with adjacent focal wall thickening, ultrasound surveillance for an 8 mm thick-stalk polyp without focal wall thickening or PSC, and no further follow-up for a 4 mm thin-stalk polyp without suspicious features or PSC.
claim.gallbladder-polyp.approved-concord.limitation: This is a constrained profile-level teaching set, not a complete management algorithm; it excludes invasion, attributable symptoms, PSC where specified, and all unapproved risk modifiers or schedules.
claim.gallbladder-polyp.approved-concord.applicablePopulation: Patients represented by the six owner-approved completed-ultrasound profiles only.

claim.thyroid-nodule.fna-after-selected-.statement: For a stable patient whose ultrasound identifies suspicious thyroid-nodule features meeting biopsy criteria, ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration is an appropriate next diagnostic step after TSH and ultrasound evaluation.
claim.thyroid-nodule.fna-after-selected-.limitation: This does not define ultrasound score cutoffs, size thresholds, or the workup of every thyroid nodule.
claim.thyroid-nodule.fna-after-selected-.applicablePopulation: Stable outpatients with a selected suspicious thyroid nodule, normal TSH, and ultrasound features meeting biopsy criteria.

claim.thyroid-nodule.follicular-invasion.statement: Follicular cytology cannot itself establish capsular or vascular invasion; that distinction between follicular adenoma and carcinoma requires histologic evaluation of the lesion.
claim.thyroid-nodule.follicular-invasion.limitation: This bounded distinction does not prescribe an operation, molecular-testing strategy, or management for every indeterminate cytology result.
claim.thyroid-nodule.follicular-invasion.applicablePopulation: Patients whose thyroid FNA is reported as a follicular neoplasm in this authored diagnostic pathway.

claim.primary-hyperparathyroidism.bioche.statement: In the scoped stable outpatient evaluation, repeat serum calcium together with intact PTH establishes the biochemical pattern of primary hyperparathyroidism before localization planning.
claim.primary-hyperparathyroidism.bioche.limitation: This single-source claim does not define every cause of hypercalcemia or make localization imaging diagnostic.
claim.primary-hyperparathyroidism.bioche.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with prior hypercalcemia whose renal, vitamin-D, medication, and inherited-mimic context has already been reviewed.

claim.primary-hyperparathyroidism.renal-.statement: For a patient with biochemically confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism and documented kidney-stone or fragility-fracture involvement, parathyroid surgical assessment is an appropriate planning step.
