claim.primary-hyperparathyroidism.renal-.limitation: The accepted cross-check is undated AAES patient education rather than a newly verified formal guideline. This claim excludes asymptomatic cutoffs, surveillance intervals, drug regimens, and individualized operative-suitability decisions.
claim.primary-hyperparathyroidism.renal-.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism and an authored kidney stone or fragility fracture.

claim.inguinal-hernia.equivocal-exam-ult.statement: For a stable patient with intermittent groin symptoms and an equivocal examination, targeted dynamic groin ultrasound is a selected next study to clarify possible inguinal hernia anatomy.
claim.inguinal-hernia.equivocal-exam-ult.limitation: Obvious hernias do not require routine imaging; ultrasound is operator-dependent, and a nondiagnostic study can require context-specific further imaging. NIDDK cites HerniaSurge, so it is not independent underlying trial evidence.
claim.inguinal-hernia.equivocal-exam-ult.applicablePopulation: Stable outpatients with activity-related groin symptoms, equivocal examination, and no incarceration, obstruction, or strangulation features.

claim.inguinal-hernia.symptomatic-electi.statement: For a patient with a confirmed reducible inguinal hernia and meaningful activity-limiting symptoms, elective repair discussion and planning are appropriate.
claim.inguinal-hernia.symptomatic-electi.limitation: This does not select a repair technique, mesh, or timing protocol, and does not treat watchful waiting as the default for the symptomatic profiles used here. NIDDK cites HerniaSurge as underlying evidence.
claim.inguinal-hernia.symptomatic-electi.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with confirmed reducible inguinal hernia and authored symptomatic activity limitation.

claim.anal-fissure.acute-midline-recogni.statement: Recent severe pain with defecation, scant bright-red bleeding, and a superficial midline anal tear on gentle inspection support acute anal fissure.
claim.anal-fissure.acute-midline-recogni.limitation: Persistent, lateral, multiple, painless, or otherwise atypical lesions require reassessment; the finding does not explain every cause of rectal bleeding.
claim.anal-fissure.acute-midline-recogni.applicablePopulation: Stable outpatients with a recent painful superficial midline tear and no abscess, systemic illness, or chronic fissure features.

claim.anal-fissure.initial-conservative-.statement: Initial care for an uncomplicated acute anal fissure includes stool-regulating fiber, sufficient fluid intake, and warm sitz baths to support comfortable soft formed stools.
claim.anal-fissure.initial-conservative-.limitation: No exact dose, schedule, duration, medication concentration, or healing probability is specified; persistent symptoms warrant reassessment.
claim.anal-fissure.initial-conservative-.applicablePopulation: Stable outpatients with a typical uncomplicated acute midline anal fissure.

claim.internal-hemorrhoids.anoscopy-eval.statement: After history, external inspection, and digital examination, anoscopy directly evaluates suspected internal hemorrhoidal tissue when local canal anatomy remains unconfirmed.
claim.internal-hemorrhoids.anoscopy-eval.limitation: Rectal bleeding must not automatically be attributed to hemorrhoids; upstream evaluation and screening remain individualized. The source is undated society patient guidance rather than a verified current formal guideline.
claim.internal-hemorrhoids.anoscopy-eval.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent painless bleeding or prolapse whose upstream colorectal evaluation is already appropriate and who have no alarm symptoms or iron-deficiency anemia.

claim.internal-hemorrhoids.office-bandin.statement: Office rubber-band ligation is an appropriate treatment option for selected bleeding or prolapsing internal hemorrhoids that persist after dietary and bowel-habit care.
claim.internal-hemorrhoids.office-bandin.limitation: Other office treatments can also be appropriate. This claim is limited to uncomplicated internal disease without a bleeding disorder, antithrombotic complication, active infection, or substantial external component.
claim.internal-hemorrhoids.office-bandin.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with confirmed spontaneously reducing internal hemorrhoids and persistent bleeding or prolapse after conservative care.

claim.esophageal-dysphagia.upper-endosco.statement: Upper-GI endoscopy with appropriate esophageal biopsies evaluates persistent esophageal dysphagia by examining mucosa and structural narrowing and obtaining tissue when indicated.
claim.esophageal-dysphagia.upper-endosco.limitation: This does not prescribe an emergency pathway, universal dilation, screening criteria, or a test sequence for every dysphagia presentation.
claim.esophageal-dysphagia.upper-endosco.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent esophageal dysphagia who can tolerate liquids and have no acute food impaction.

claim.barrett-esophagus.intestinal-metap.statement: A visible esophageal columnar segment with biopsy-confirmed specialized intestinal metaplasia supports the diagnosis of Barrett esophagus.
claim.barrett-esophagus.intestinal-metap.limitation: Barrett metaplasia is not treated as the cause of obstructive dysphagia here, and this claim does not specify screening groups, cancer risk, surveillance intervals, acid-suppression protocols, or dysplasia treatment.
claim.barrett-esophagus.intestinal-metap.applicablePopulation: Adults with an adequately examined esophageal columnar segment and specialized intestinal metaplasia on biopsy without dysplasia or carcinoma.

claim.achalasia.high-resolution-manometr.statement: High-resolution esophageal manometry is the confirmatory physiologic test when achalasia is suspected after structural obstruction and concerning pseudoachalasia have been appropriately excluded.
claim.achalasia.high-resolution-manometr.limitation: The accepted guideline rates diagnostic evidence as low despite strong consensus. This claim does not prescribe subtype thresholds or a treatment algorithm.
claim.achalasia.high-resolution-manometr.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with persistent solids-and-liquids dysphagia and regurgitation after an adequate EGD excludes mechanical obstruction and concerning pseudoachalasia.

claim.achalasia.manometric-recognition.statement: Absent esophageal peristalsis together with impaired esophagogastric-junction relaxation on high-resolution manometry supports achalasia.
claim.achalasia.manometric-recognition.limitation: No exact pressure cutoff, subtype assignment, or universal requirement for raised basal lower-esophageal-sphincter pressure is asserted; the accepted precise source is a single society guideline.
claim.achalasia.manometric-recognition.applicablePopulation: Adults with an adequate structural evaluation and the authored manometric pattern.

claim.pigmented-skin-lesion.complete-dia.statement: A small accessible pigmented lesion concerning for melanoma should usually undergo complete diagnostic excision with narrow clinical margins and sufficient depth for histologic microstaging.
claim.pigmented-skin-lesion.complete-dia.limitation: Partial biopsy can be appropriate for selected large or anatomically difficult lesions, and this claim does not prohibit every properly performed deep saucerization technique or define an exact diagnostic margin.
claim.pigmented-skin-lesion.complete-dia.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a small accessible evolving superficial pigmented lesion and no prior tissue diagnosis.

claim.melanoma.sentinel-node-staging.statement: For clinically node-negative melanoma of intermediate thickness, sentinel lymph-node biopsy should be discussed for pathological regional staging alongside definitive wide-excision planning.
claim.melanoma.sentinel-node-staging.limitation: Sentinel-node biopsy is not complete nodal dissection, does not itself prove metastatic disease, and is not presented as guaranteeing survival benefit. Exact margin rules and systemic treatment are outside this claim.
claim.melanoma.sentinel-node-staging.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with biopsy-confirmed intermediate-thickness invasive melanoma and no clinically palpable regional nodes.

claim.postoperative-seroma.ultrasound-ch.statement: Targeted ultrasound can characterize an uncertain superficial postoperative breast collection and distinguish simple fluid features from a solid or suspiciously vascular finding.
claim.postoperative-seroma.ultrasound-ch.limitation: This imaging detail is supported by a single institutional teaching source rather than a society guideline, and ultrasound is not presented as universally definitive outside the complete clinical context.
claim.postoperative-seroma.ultrasound-ch.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with uncertain superficial fullness after benign breast excision and no emergency or infectious features.

claim.postoperative-seroma.uncomplicated.statement: A small simple postoperative seroma without infection, wound tension, an implant, meaningful pain, or functional limitation can be observed with clinical follow-up rather than routinely aspirated.
claim.postoperative-seroma.uncomplicated.limitation: The management detail is chiefly supported by one institutional source; symptoms, wound compromise, infection concern, diagnostic uncertainty, or other patient factors can justify intervention.
claim.postoperative-seroma.uncomplicated.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a small simple collection after benign breast excision and no infection, wound tension, implant, meaningful pain, or functional limitation.

claim.pilonidal-disease.chronic-sinus-re.statement: Recurrent drainage through characteristic midline pits in the natal cleft, without a current abscess, supports chronic pilonidal sinus disease on clinical examination.
claim.pilonidal-disease.chronic-sinus-re.limitation: The examination should consider other causes, including an anal fistula when the location or history raises concern; routine imaging is not required for the classic presentation used here.
claim.pilonidal-disease.chronic-sinus-re.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with recurrent natal-cleft drainage and midline pits but no fluctuant abscess, cellulitis, or systemic illness.

claim.pilonidal-disease.off-midline-clos.statement: When excision with primary closure has already been selected for chronic pilonidal disease, the closure should be placed away from the natal midline.
claim.pilonidal-disease.off-midline-clos.limitation: Open healing and minimally invasive approaches remain valid individualized alternatives, and no single named flap is asserted to be best for every patient.
claim.pilonidal-disease.off-midline-clos.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with chronic pilonidal disease who, after individualized discussion, have selected excision with primary closure.

claim.graves-pattern-recognition.classic.statement:
Thyroid-hormone-excess symptoms with diffuse thyroid enlargement and bilateral
proptosis form a clinical pattern that supports Graves disease.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.classic.limitation:
a supporting pattern, not a stand-alone diagnostic
  rule; Graves disease may occur without proptosis.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.classic.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing clinic evaluation for a clinical pattern compatible with Graves disease.

claim.graves-pattern-recognition.thyroto.statement:
Palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, sweating, unintentional weight loss,
and muscle weakness can occur with thyroid-hormone excess but do not alone
establish its cause.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.thyroto.limitation:
the variants use a fuller clinical pattern and do not
  teach diagnosis from symptoms alone.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.thyroto.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing clinic evaluation for a clinical pattern compatible with Graves disease.

claim.graves-pattern-recognition.pretibi.statement:
Pretibial dermopathy, such as thickened raised plaques over the anterior shins,
is an associated Graves finding that can add support to an otherwise compatible
clinical pattern.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.pretibi.limitation:
an associated finding, not a required feature or
  independent diagnostic rule.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.pretibi.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing clinic evaluation for a clinical pattern compatible with Graves disease.

claim.graves-pattern-recognition.nodular.statement:
Overactive thyroid nodules can cause thyroid-hormone excess, so hormone-excess
symptoms do not by themselves distinguish Graves disease from nodular disease.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.nodular.limitation:
a competing cause of thyroid-hormone excess; this
  draft does not teach imaging, laboratory testing, or management.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.nodular.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing clinic evaluation for a clinical pattern compatible with Graves disease.

claim.graves-pattern-recognition.painful.statement:
Subacute thyroiditis can present with a painful enlarged thyroid and is a
competing clinical presentation when thyroid-hormone excess is documented.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.painful.limitation:
this draft identifies a competing presentation only;
  it does not teach thyroiditis testing or treatment.
claim.graves-pattern-recognition.painful.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing clinic evaluation for a clinical pattern compatible with Graves disease.

claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.pos.statement:
In a patient with compatible clinical findings and biochemical thyrotoxicosis,
a positive TRAb result supports Graves disease as the etiology.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.pos.limitation:
supportive in clinical context, not a stand-alone
  replacement for the complete evaluation.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.pos.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible clinical findings and biochemical thyrotoxicosis undergoing etiologic evaluation.

claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.neg.statement:
A negative TRAb result does not fully exclude Graves disease when the clinical
and biochemical context remains compatible.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.neg.limitation:
the result changes diagnostic support but does not
  independently resolve the cause or prescribe a next imaging step.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.neg.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible clinical findings and biochemical thyrotoxicosis undergoing etiologic evaluation.

claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.fun.statement:
TSH, T4, and T3 results describe thyroid function, whereas TRAb supplies
etiologic antibody evidence relevant to Graves disease.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.fun.limitation:
this draft uses qualitative result labels only and does
  not teach thresholds, assay selection beyond TRAb, or broad antibody panels.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.fun.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible clinical findings and biochemical thyrotoxicosis undergoing etiologic evaluation.

claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.bio.statement:
A low TSH result with a high free T4 result is a biochemical pattern of thyroid
hormone excess; those functional results do not by themselves identify Graves
disease as the cause.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.bio.limitation:
qualitative functional context only; this draft does
  not teach thresholds, severity classification, or a treatment decision.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.bio.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible clinical findings and biochemical thyrotoxicosis undergoing etiologic evaluation.

claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.sym.statement:
Palpitations, heat intolerance, unintentional weight loss, and diffuse thyroid
enlargement can accompany Graves disease; these findings alone do not establish
the cause of thyrotoxicosis.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.sym.limitation:
supporting presentation context only; a full clinical
  evaluation remains necessary.
claim.graves-trab-diagnostic-support.sym.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible clinical findings and biochemical thyrotoxicosis undergoing etiologic evaluation.

claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.r.statement:
For Graves disease, recurrent hyperthyroidism after antithyroid-drug withdrawal
is a setting in which RAI therapy may be considered.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.r.limitation:
a guideline-supported indication for consideration, not
  a mandate or a universal preferred treatment for every recurrence.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.r.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding adults with established Graves disease and no active thyroid eye disease who are considering treatment options.

claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.p.statement:
Antithyroid drugs, RAI, and surgery are treatment options for Graves disease;
their selection should incorporate the patient’s circumstances and preferences.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.p.limitation:
this draft presents a bounded counseling choice and
  does not establish a universal treatment hierarchy.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.p.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding adults with established Graves disease and no active thyroid eye disease who are considering treatment options.

claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.r.statement:
RAI is a nonsurgical, disease-directed treatment that destroys overactive
thyroid cells. Antithyroid drugs reduce thyroid-hormone production, while
beta-blocking medicines can control symptoms without reducing hormone
production.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.r.limitation:
distinguishes the broad roles of these options for the
  counseling question; it does not specify a dose, preparation regimen,
  treatment timeline, or universal treatment preference.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.r.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding adults with established Graves disease and no active thyroid eye disease who are considering treatment options.

claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.g.limitation:
these features support the established diagnosis in
  the patient presentations but do not independently select RAI treatment.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.g.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding adults with established Graves disease and no active thyroid eye disease who are considering treatment options.

claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.e.statement:
RAI evaluation requires individualized selection. Pregnancy and current
breastfeeding are contraindications to RAI treatment, while active thyroid eye
disease requires individualized assessment.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.e.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding adults with established Graves disease and no active thyroid eye disease who are considering treatment options.

claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.s.statement:
RAI evaluation includes specialist counseling, informed consent, and practical
precaution instructions before treatment.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.s.limitation:
a clinical counseling claim only; it does not determine
  where RAI is delivered or teach jurisdiction-specific requirements. The
  game's clinic-only counseling and referral boundary is release metadata, not
  a medical claim.
claim.graves-rai-appropriate-candidate.s.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant, nonbreastfeeding adults with established Graves disease and no active thyroid eye disease who are considering treatment options.

claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.statement:
RAI treatment is contraindicated throughout pregnancy for a patient with Graves
disease.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.limitation:
applies to RAI treatment; it does not prohibit clinical
  counseling, referral, or other individualized pregnancy care.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Pregnant adults with Graves disease being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.statement:
Radioiodine can cross the placenta, be taken up by the fetal thyroid, and harm
or destroy fetal thyroid tissue, causing permanent hypothyroidism.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.limitation:
explains the treatment exclusion; this draft does not
  teach timing, dose, fetal testing, or pregnancy-loss counseling.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Pregnant adults with Graves disease being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.statement:
Avoiding RAI during pregnancy does not end care: endocrine and obstetric
assessment and individually tailored monitoring can continue.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.limitation:
no regimen, dose, surgery timing, or assertion that all
  pregnant patients require medication is taught.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Pregnant adults with Graves disease being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.statement:
Palpitations, tremor, diffuse thyroid enlargement, and a positive TRAb result
can provide clinical and diagnostic context supporting Graves disease.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.limitation:
background context only; it is not a separate scored
  recognition or antibody-interpretation concept in this packet.
claim.graves-rai-pregnancy-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Pregnant adults with Graves disease being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.statement:
Current breastfeeding contraindicates therapeutic iodine-131 treatment for a
patient with Graves disease.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.limitation:
applies to therapeutic iodine-131; it does not prohibit
  counseling, referral, or individualized endocrine and pediatric guidance.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Adults currently breastfeeding who have Graves disease and are being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.statement:
Therapeutic iodine-131 can enter breast milk and expose the nursing infant's
thyroid to radioiodine.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.limitation:
explains the lactation exclusion without teaching an
  infant dose, radiation measurement, emergency response, or exposure protocol.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Adults currently breastfeeding who have Graves disease and are being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.statement:
For therapeutic iodine-131, breastfeeding cessation must be planned before
treatment.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.limitation:
this is pre-treatment counseling, not an exposure
  emergency. It supplies no interval, dose, or weaning protocol.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Adults currently breastfeeding who have Graves disease and are being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.statement:
After therapeutic iodine-131, standard guidance advises against resuming
breastfeeding the current child.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.limitation:
this recommendation does not claim a lifelong anatomic
  inability to breastfeed, address a future child after a future pregnancy, or
  supply a resumption interval, dose, or protocol.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Adults currently breastfeeding who have Graves disease and are being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.statement:
Palpitations, tremor, diffuse thyroid enlargement, and a positive TRAb result
can provide clinical and diagnostic context supporting Graves disease.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.limitation:
background context only; it is not a separate scored
  recognition or antibody-interpretation concept in this packet.
claim.graves-rai-lactation-contraindicat.applicablePopulation: Adults currently breastfeeding who have Graves disease and are being counseled about therapeutic iodine-131.

claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.ge.statement:
In ordinary Graves treatment selection, therapeutic iodine-131 is generally
avoided when thyroid eye disease is active and moderate-to-severe.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.ge.limitation:
not an absolute lifetime prohibition; specialist
  exceptions may be considered when alternatives are not feasible.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.ge.applicablePopulation: Adults with Graves disease and specialist-documented active moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.

claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.wo.statement: Therapeutic iodine-131 may worsen existing thyroid eye disease.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.wo.limitation:
supports counseling avoidance in the documented active
  moderate-to-severe setting; it does not create an emergency-treatment rule.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.wo.applicablePopulation: Adults with Graves disease and specialist-documented active moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.

claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.ey.statement: Improvement in thyroid symptoms alone does not establish that thyroid eye disease has become inactive.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.ey.limitation:
this is a synthetic application: ATA and NIDDK document
  that TED can coexist with normal thyroid function, while the case independently
  states specialist-confirmed active disease. It does not establish a timeline or cause.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.ey.applicablePopulation: Adults with Graves disease and specialist-documented active moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.

claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.gr.statement: Palpitations, fine tremor, heat intolerance, diffuse goiter, and diffuse scan uptake can provide clinical context for Graves disease.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.gr.limitation: background context only, not an extra scored concept; these findings do not grade TED or independently select treatment.
claim.graves-rai-active-ted-avoidance.gr.applicablePopulation: Adults with Graves disease and specialist-documented active moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease.

claim.gallstones.ultrasound-first.statement: Abdominal ultrasound is an appropriate initial imaging test for a stable outpatient with suspected gallstones.
claim.gallstones.ultrasound-first.limitation: This scoped claim does not cover unstable patients or every alternative biliary presentation.
claim.gallstones.ultrasound-first.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with symptoms compatible with uncomplicated gallstones.

claim.gallstones.symptomatic-referral.statement: Recurrent compatible symptoms with ultrasound-confirmed gallstones support elective surgical assessment and cholecystectomy counseling.
claim.gallstones.symptomatic-referral.limitation: Individual operative suitability and competing diagnoses still require assessment.
claim.gallstones.symptomatic-referral.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with symptomatic gallstones and no acute complication in this encounter.

claim.gallstones.incidental-observation.statement: Incidentally found gallstones without symptoms or suspicious features usually do not require prophylactic surgery.
claim.gallstones.incidental-observation.limitation: Higher-risk gallbladder features and later biliary symptoms are outside this pathway.
claim.gallstones.incidental-observation.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic adults with uncomplicated incidental gallstones.

claim.gallstones.ercp-common-bile-duct-s.statement: ERCP can remove a stone lodged in the common bile duct; that indication is distinct from treating uncomplicated stones confined to the gallbladder.
claim.gallstones.ercp-common-bile-duct-s.limitation: This supporting boundary does not define every indication for ERCP.
claim.gallstones.ercp-common-bile-duct-s.applicablePopulation: Adults being evaluated for gallstone disease where duct intervention is considered.

claim.nephrolithiasis.noncontrast-ct.statement: Noncontrast CT can clarify stone presence, location, and obstruction when a stable nonpregnant adult has unresolved diagnostic uncertainty after indeterminate ultrasound.
claim.nephrolithiasis.noncontrast-ct.limitation: This is not a universal first-line imaging rule and does not apply to pregnancy, children, or unstable presentations.
claim.nephrolithiasis.noncontrast-ct.applicablePopulation: Stable nonpregnant adults with suspected stone disease and unresolved diagnostic uncertainty.

claim.nephrolithiasis.recurrent-metaboli.statement: Recurrent stone disease supports stone-composition analysis when material is available and urine and blood metabolic evaluation, including a 24-hour urine assessment of volume and mineral measures, to inform prevention planning.
claim.nephrolithiasis.recurrent-metaboli.limitation: Sources are older single-agency guidance; this claim does not prescribe a preventive drug or exact collection protocol.
claim.nephrolithiasis.recurrent-metaboli.applicablePopulation: Adults with recurrent confirmed kidney stone disease after the acute episode is addressed.

claim.nephrolithiasis.infection-evidence.statement: Clinical and urine findings relevant to urinary infection are distinct from CT characterization of stone location and obstruction.
claim.nephrolithiasis.infection-evidence.limitation: An available urinalysis without documented infection is not treated as an absolute exclusion of infection.
claim.nephrolithiasis.infection-evidence.applicablePopulation: Stable adults undergoing evaluation for suspected kidney stones.

claim.celiac.initial-serology.statement: While a patient is eating gluten, tTG-IgA together with total-IgA context is a usual initial serologic assessment for suspected celiac disease.
claim.celiac.initial-serology.limitation: IgA deficiency changes test selection; serology is not presented as universally definitive.
claim.celiac.initial-serology.applicablePopulation: Adults with compatible symptoms who remain on gluten during diagnostic evaluation.

claim.celiac.adult-biopsy.statement: In a usual adult pathway, positive compatible serology leads to upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies for diagnostic confirmation.
claim.celiac.adult-biopsy.limitation: This does not assert that every adult in every setting must undergo biopsy.
claim.celiac.adult-biopsy.applicablePopulation: Adults with positive celiac serology and adequate total IgA in a routine diagnostic pathway.

claim.celiac.gluten-free-treatment.statement: Confirmed celiac disease is treated with a gluten-free diet, supported by a dietitian with relevant expertise.
claim.celiac.gluten-free-treatment.limitation: No exact response interval, supplement regimen, or gluten-challenge protocol is taught.
claim.celiac.gluten-free-treatment.applicablePopulation: Adults with celiac disease confirmed in the scoped pathway.

claim.celiac.gluten-testing-boundary.statement: Starting gluten avoidance before diagnostic testing can alter serologic and biopsy results.
claim.celiac.gluten-testing-boundary.limitation: The content does not prescribe a gluten challenge.
claim.celiac.gluten-testing-boundary.applicablePopulation: People undergoing evaluation for possible celiac disease.

claim.celiac.igg-tests-in-iga-deficiency.statement: IgG-based celiac serology has a limited diagnostic role when IgA deficiency makes IgA-based tests unreliable.
claim.celiac.igg-tests-in-iga-deficiency.limitation: This does not make an IgG panel the preferred routine first test before total IgA context is known.
claim.celiac.igg-tests-in-iga-deficiency.applicablePopulation: People evaluated for celiac disease when IgA deficiency is present or suspected.

claim.celiac.hla-susceptibility-not-acti.statement: HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 typing addresses genetic susceptibility and does not by itself establish active celiac disease.
claim.celiac.hla-susceptibility-not-acti.limitation: This claim does not specify test performance or every clinical use of HLA typing.
claim.celiac.hla-susceptibility-not-acti.applicablePopulation: People undergoing evaluation for possible celiac disease.

claim.colorectal.positive-fit-colonoscop.statement: A positive screening FIT requires diagnostic colonoscopy; FIT alone does not diagnose colorectal cancer.
claim.colorectal.positive-fit-colonoscop.limitation: Suitability and the management of incomplete examination remain individualized.
claim.colorectal.positive-fit-colonoscop.applicablePopulation: Adults with a positive colorectal-cancer screening FIT who are suitable for outpatient diagnostic evaluation.

claim.colorectal.histology-confirms.statement: Histologic examination of tissue sampled from a suspicious colorectal lesion provides confirming evidence of cancer.
claim.colorectal.histology-confirms.limitation: Gross appearance and cross-sectional imaging can be suspicious but do not substitute for tissue diagnosis or assign stage here.
claim.colorectal.histology-confirms.applicablePopulation: Adults with a suspicious colorectal lesion sampled during colonoscopy.

claim.iron-deficiency.iron-studies.statement: Iron studies are used to confirm iron deficiency in an already anemic patient, and low ferritin supports depleted iron stores.
claim.iron-deficiency.iron-studies.limitation: A normal ferritin can be misleading with inflammation; this content uses no numeric threshold and does not claim isolated low ferritin proves anemia.
claim.iron-deficiency.iron-studies.applicablePopulation: Adults with established anemia undergoing evaluation for iron deficiency.

claim.iron-deficiency.bidirectional-endo.statement: New unexplained confirmed iron-deficiency anemia in adult men or postmenopausal patients generally warrants gastrointestinal evaluation with upper endoscopy and colonoscopy when suitable.
claim.iron-deficiency.bidirectional-endo.limitation: Suitability, individual context, and alternative established causes must be considered; no referral deadline is taught.
claim.iron-deficiency.bidirectional-endo.applicablePopulation: Adult men and explicitly postmenopausal patients with newly confirmed otherwise unexplained iron-deficiency anemia.

claim.soft-tissue-mass.mri.statement: MRI is appropriate for local characterization of a deep, enlarging, or ultrasound-indeterminate extremity soft-tissue mass before biopsy.
claim.soft-tissue-mass.mri.limitation: MRI can characterize and guide planning but cannot by itself prove sarcoma.
claim.soft-tissue-mass.mri.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a deep, enlarging, or ultrasound-indeterminate extremity soft-tissue mass.

claim.soft-tissue-mass.planned-biopsy.statement: A suspicious extremity soft-tissue mass should reach an experienced sarcoma team before a planned image-guided core biopsy so the biopsy path respects a future surgical approach.
claim.soft-tissue-mass.planned-biopsy.limitation: Biopsy technique and selected incisional approaches remain specialist decisions; imaging suspicion is not a tissue diagnosis.
claim.soft-tissue-mass.planned-biopsy.applicablePopulation: Adults whose extremity mass remains suspicious after local MRI characterization.

claim.variety3.diastasis.midline-separat.statement: Rectus diastasis is widening of the midline connective tissue between the rectus muscles.
claim.variety3.diastasis.midline-separat.limitation: EHS KQ1 and current NHS leaflet. No numerical separation cutoff, demographic probability or treatment rule is used; EHS describes limited evidence.
claim.variety3.diastasis.midline-separat.applicablePopulation: Adults with supplied abdominal-wall examination findings.

claim.variety3.diastasis.broad-doming.statement: Rectus separation can produce a broad midline dome when the abdominal wall is engaged.
claim.variety3.diastasis.broad-doming.limitation: Current NHS leaflet is the sole direct source for the dome description. A clinical pattern, not a pathognomonic sign or proof from appearance alone.
claim.variety3.diastasis.broad-doming.applicablePopulation: Adults with broad midline doming during a supplied examination.

claim.variety3.diastasis.clinical-assess.statement: Clinical examination is generally sufficient to identify rectus diastasis.
claim.variety3.diastasis.clinical-assess.limitation: EHS KQ2, low-quality evidence. Imaging may be useful when another question, including a coexisting hernia, needs assessment. These recognition cases do not establish a universal no-imaging rule.
claim.variety3.diastasis.clinical-assess.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing clinical assessment of rectus separation.

claim.variety3.diastasis.hernia-distinct.statement: A focal abdominal-wall hernia involves protrusion through a gap or weak area rather than rectus separation alone.
claim.variety3.diastasis.hernia-distinct.limitation: Independent synthesis of NHS hernia definition and EHS diastasis definition/coexisting-hernia discussion. The two can coexist; the supplied examination identifies no focal defect. No assertion that examination excludes all hernias.
claim.variety3.diastasis.hernia-distinct.applicablePopulation: Adults distinguishing a supplied separation pattern from a focal hernia.

claim.variety3.epidermoid.slow-punctum-p.statement: An epidermoid cyst often presents as a slowly growing cutaneous lump with a central punctum.
claim.variety3.epidermoid.slow-punctum-p.limitation: Hoang clinical/pathophysiology sections plus broad NHS skin-cyst corroboration. Presumptive recognition, not histologic confirmation. The NHS displayed review date is 2023 with an overdue 2026 review marker.
claim.variety3.epidermoid.slow-punctum-p.applicablePopulation: Adults with an uncomplicated slowly enlarging skin lump.

claim.variety3.epidermoid.differential-p.statement: A central punctum supports epidermoid cyst over the described lipoma and trichilemmal-cyst differentials.
claim.variety3.epidermoid.differential-p.limitation: Sole direct descriptive source, section 4. Not an absolute diagnostic exclusion rule: the case supplies a punctum-bearing lesion, and the learner selects the best fit rather than confirming pathology.
claim.variety3.epidermoid.differential-p.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing proposed diagnoses for a supplied cutaneous lump.

claim.variety3.epidermoid.inflammation-c.statement: A skin cyst can become inflamed and painful, so tenderness alone does not define every cyst as an abscess.
claim.variety3.epidermoid.inflammation-c.limitation: Sources support possible inflammation; the cases supply no redness, tenderness or draining collection. No infection probability, antibiotic indication or drainage/excision protocol is inferred.
claim.variety3.epidermoid.inflammation-c.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied noninflamed punctum-bearing lump.

claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.external-throm.statement: A blood clot within an external hemorrhoid produces a thrombosed external hemorrhoid.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.external-throm.limitation: Sole direct clot-definition source is undated public ASCRS education, not a formal management guideline. No fixed symptom window or automatic excision recommendation.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.external-throm.applicablePopulation: Adults with an examined clot-filled external anal-margin lump.

claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.tender-margin-.statement: External hemorrhoids can present as a tender, painful lump at the anal margin.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.tender-margin-.limitation: Independent specialist/government recognition sources. NIDDK review date is 2016. Pain is nonspecific; supplied examination shows the external clot and excludes a visible tear or draining collection.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.tender-margin-.applicablePopulation: Adults with an acutely painful external anal-margin lump.

claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.internal-locat.statement: Internal hemorrhoids arise within the anal canal and may protrude through the anus.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.internal-locat.limitation: Anatomic distinction only. Internal prolapse can also hurt; pain alone does not distinguish internal and external disease. The cases explicitly locate the clot under external anal skin, without protruding mucosal tissue.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.internal-locat.applicablePopulation: Adults distinguishing a supplied external lesion from internal prolapse.

claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.assessment-bou.statement: Anal symptoms require assessment rather than automatic attribution to hemorrhoids.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.assessment-bou.limitation: Sources emphasize other possible causes. The draft supplies an examination, not a rule to diagnose from a patient's complaint or to ignore bleeding. No treatment decision is tested.
claim.variety3.hemorrhoid.assessment-bou.applicablePopulation: Adults with anal pain or a perianal lump.

claim.variety3.pruritus.irritant-cleanin.statement: Repeated vigorous cleansing can irritate perianal skin and worsen anal itching.
claim.variety3.pruritus.irritant-cleanin.limitation: Society/government patient guidance; not a diagnostic accuracy claim or proof of the cause in every person. Cases supply examination and irritant exposure, without a focal lesion requiring different care.
claim.variety3.pruritus.irritant-cleanin.applicablePopulation: Adults with assessed perianal irritation and excessive cleansing.

claim.variety3.pruritus.gentle-water-dry.statement: Gentle water cleansing followed by patting the area dry is an appropriate basic skin-care measure for pruritus ani.
claim.variety3.pruritus.gentle-water-dry.limitation: Two independent guidance sources, but neither a current formal management guideline. Limited to assessed uncomplicated irritation; no medication, prescribed device or guaranteed response is claimed.
claim.variety3.pruritus.gentle-water-dry.applicablePopulation: Adults with assessed uncomplicated anal itching.

claim.variety3.pruritus.avoid-irritants.statement: Avoiding fragranced products and abrasive cleaning helps reduce perianal irritation.
claim.variety3.pruritus.avoid-irritants.limitation: Sources agree on avoiding irritation. ASCRS mentions some gentle wiping options; this is not interpreted as endorsing fragranced wipes. No blanket claim that every wipe or every cleanser is harmful.
claim.variety3.pruritus.avoid-irritants.applicablePopulation: Adults with perianal itching while using irritating products.

claim.variety3.pruritus.reassessment-bou.statement: Persistent or otherwise concerning anal itching warrants reassessment for an underlying cause.
claim.variety3.pruritus.reassessment-bou.limitation: No fixed follow-up interval or red-flag algorithm is authored. The initial skin-care choice is not a substitute for examining a lesion or reassessing ongoing symptoms.
claim.variety3.pruritus.reassessment-bou.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving basic skin-care counseling for anal itching.

claim.variety3.preparation.inadequate-as.statement: Colonoscopy with inadequate cleansing may fail to assess the colonic lining adequately.
claim.variety3.preparation.inadequate-as.limitation: Official ESGE guideline plus directly read 2025 society summary; the latter is not the full USMSTF guideline. Cases specify inadequate assessment throughout the colon after attempted cleaning, excluding the partial-distal-examination exception.
claim.variety3.preparation.inadequate-as.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a colonoscopy that cannot support a standard screening assessment.

claim.variety3.preparation.repeat-examin.statement: An inadequately prepared colonoscopy that cannot support the intended assessment should be repeated with adequate preparation.
claim.variety3.preparation.repeat-examin.limitation: Current society summary corroborates guideline direction. No universal numerical interval or mandatory same/next-day schedule; timing, contraindications and urgency require the treating team's assessment. Alternative screening proposals do not complete the inadequate examination in these cases.
claim.variety3.preparation.repeat-examin.applicablePopulation: Adults suitable for repeat colonoscopy after an entirely inadequate screening examination.

claim.variety3.preparation.review-failur.statement: Reviewing why preparation failed can guide improved instructions and an individualized repeat-preparation plan.
claim.variety3.preparation.review-failur.limitation: Source-supported planning only. No specific laxative formulation, dose, diet duration, split-dose timetable or contraindication protocol is authored.
claim.variety3.preparation.review-failur.applicablePopulation: Adults planning repeat colonoscopy after inadequate bowel cleansing.

claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-snare-di.statement: Cold snare is the preferred removal technique for an accessible diminutive nonpedunculated colorectal polyp without invasive features.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-snare-di.limitation: Sole adequate directly read guideline, ESGE 2024 section 7.1, strong recommendation/high-quality evidence for polyps at most 5 mm; the synthetic example is 4 mm. No technique algorithm, margin width, risk estimate or difficult-access exception is authored.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-snare-di.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied accessible 4 mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyp selected for removal.

claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-snare-sm.statement: Cold snare is the preferred removal technique for a small nonpedunculated colorectal polyp without invasive features.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-snare-sm.limitation: Sole adequate directly read guideline, ESGE 2024 section 7.2, strong recommendation/high-quality evidence for 6-9 mm polyps; the example is 7 mm. Excludes pedunculated, invasive-appearing and complex lesions and medication-specific planning.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-snare-sm.applicablePopulation: Adults with a supplied accessible 7 mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyp selected for removal.

claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-forceps-.statement: Cold forceps are not the preferred excision method for the supplied 4 mm or 7 mm polyps because complete resection is less reliable.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-forceps-.limitation: Sole adequate guideline, sections 7.1/7.2 and recommendation against routine cold-forceps excision. Very tiny or difficult-access exceptions are outside these cases; no numerical recurrence estimate.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.cold-forceps-.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing techniques for the supplied accessible 4 mm or 7 mm lesions.

claim.variety3.polypectomy.hot-forceps-l.statement: Hot biopsy forceps are discouraged for diminutive colorectal-polyp excision because of resection, specimen and thermal-injury concerns.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.hot-forceps-l.limitation: Sole adequate direct guideline, section 7.1, strong/high-quality recommendation. No exact risk estimate or categorical prohibition on all electrosurgical techniques. For the 7 mm case, the cold-snare preference supplies the direct rejection basis.
claim.variety3.polypectomy.hot-forceps-l.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing forceps and snare plans for the supplied small lesions.

claim.variety3.barrett.surveillance-plan.statement: Endoscopic surveillance is an appropriate follow-up strategy for established nondysplastic Barrett esophagus in a suitable patient.
claim.variety3.barrett.surveillance-plan.limitation: Official ESGE guideline plus independent current government surveillance explanation. Cases supply established segments, no dysplasia/visible lesion and suitability for follow-up/treatment. No interval, zero-risk claim or prophylactic surgery indication.
claim.variety3.barrett.surveillance-plan.applicablePopulation: Adults with established nondysplastic Barrett who are suitable for surveillance.

claim.variety3.barrett.no-prophylactic-a.statement: Prophylactic endoscopic ablation is not recommended for Barrett esophagus without dysplasia.
claim.variety3.barrett.no-prophylactic-a.limitation: Sole direct guideline for this negative recommendation; NIDDK only corroborates surveillance. This is not applied to confirmed dysplasia or cancer. No promise that Barrett has no cancer risk.
claim.variety3.barrett.no-prophylactic-a.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed nondysplastic Barrett and no visible neoplastic lesion.

claim.variety3.barrett.surveillance-suit.statement: Barrett surveillance planning depends on the established segment and the patient's suitability for surveillance and possible treatment.
claim.variety3.barrett.surveillance-suit.limitation: Do not extrapolate to an irregular Z-line, limited life expectancy, confirmed dysplasia or visible neoplasia. All numerical surveillance/cessation schedules are withheld in this batch.
claim.variety3.barrett.surveillance-suit.applicablePopulation: Adults planning follow-up for established nondysplastic Barrett.

claim.variety3.sedation.no-self-driving.statement: A patient receiving endoscopic sedation should arrange transport home rather than plan to drive immediately afterward.
claim.variety3.sedation.no-self-driving.limitation: Current gastroscopy-specific NHS advice and independent NIDDK colonoscopy transport boundary. Cases use planned gastroscopy with sedation. No universal elapsed-time clearance or substitution for formal discharge criteria.
claim.variety3.sedation.no-self-driving.applicablePopulation: Adults arranging discharge after planned sedated gastroscopy.

claim.variety3.sedation.adult-collection.statement: A responsible adult should collect and support the patient after gastroscopy with sedation.
claim.variety3.sedation.adult-collection.limitation: Sole direct source for collection plus ongoing adult support is the current trust leaflet. Government colonoscopy advice corroborates the ride, not this entire support arrangement. Local discharge policy and clinical readiness remain separate.
claim.variety3.sedation.adult-collection.applicablePopulation: Adults preparing for gastroscopy with sedation and an available responsible adult.

claim.variety3.sedation.residual-effects.statement: Sedation can affect judgment and reactions despite the patient feeling awake after the procedure.
claim.variety3.sedation.residual-effects.limitation: Sole direct current gastroscopy discharge source. Subjective wakefulness is not driving clearance; no duration, test score or claim that adult accompaniment alone establishes discharge fitness.
claim.variety3.sedation.residual-effects.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing travel after gastroscopy with sedation.

claim.variety3.allergy.label-not-confirm.statement: A penicillin-allergy label does not by itself confirm an immune-mediated penicillin reaction.
claim.variety3.allergy.label-not-confirm.limitation: Current CDC guidance and eligible perioperative review. Labels can reflect incomplete or nonallergic histories; this does not mean every label is false or authorize automatic removal. No prevalence or cross-reactivity percentage.
claim.variety3.allergy.label-not-confirm.applicablePopulation: Adults with an incompletely characterized penicillin-allergy entry before ASC care.

claim.variety3.allergy.characterize-reac.statement: Characterizing the original drug, reaction symptoms, timing, severity and subsequent exposures is an initial step in evaluating a penicillin-allergy label.
claim.variety3.allergy.characterize-reac.limitation: Current CDC clinical questions plus perioperative history/risk-assessment discussion. The draft asks for history first, without choosing a prophylactic drug, skin-test protocol or oral-challenge procedure.
claim.variety3.allergy.characterize-reac.applicablePopulation: Adults whose preoperative allergy record lacks a detailed reaction history.

claim.variety3.allergy.assessment-before.statement: Reaction history and risk assessment should guide whether further penicillin-allergy testing or referral is appropriate.
claim.variety3.allergy.assessment-before.limitation: Not everyone is eligible for the same testing pathway, and severe delayed reactions require a different approach. No unsupervised challenge, universal skin testing, automatic delabeling or cefazolin-selection rule is taught.
claim.variety3.allergy.assessment-before.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment of an uncertain preoperative penicillin label.

claim.variety3.hair.no-routine-removal.statement: Surgical-site hair need not be removed when it does not interfere with the operation.
claim.variety3.hair.no-routine-removal.limitation: Sole adequate direct guideline, essential-practices section 4.5. Acute-care hospital recommendation applied to a supplied non-genital ambulatory preparation plan; clinician review of that application is required. No routine-removal benefit or exact SSI probability is claimed.
claim.variety3.hair.no-routine-removal.applicablePopulation: Adults preparing for a non-genital ambulatory procedure with noninterfering hair.

claim.variety3.hair.clippers-if-needed.statement: When surgical-site hair must be removed, clippers are an appropriate method for the supplied non-genital operative field.
claim.variety3.hair.clippers-if-needed.limitation: Sole adequate guideline, section 4.5. Depilatory agents are another guideline option and are not presented as incorrect when removal is needed. Clippers are available in the case; no precise preparation timetable, device protocol or genital-field extrapolation.
claim.variety3.hair.clippers-if-needed.applicablePopulation: Adults with hair interfering with preparation of a non-genital ambulatory operative field.

claim.variety3.hair.depilatory-alternati.statement: A depilatory agent is another guideline-supported option when surgical-site hair removal is needed.
claim.variety3.hair.depilatory-alternati.limitation: Sole adequate guideline, section 4.5. This acknowledges an alternative rather than prescribing a formulation or declaring every product appropriate. No depilatory is required when hair does not interfere; non-genital fields only.
claim.variety3.hair.depilatory-alternati.applicablePopulation: Adults discussing necessary non-genital surgical-site hair removal.

claim.variety3.hair.avoid-razor-nongenit.statement: Razor shaving is avoided for routine hair preparation of the supplied non-genital surgical field.
claim.variety3.hair.avoid-razor-nongenit.limitation: Sole adequate guideline. The guideline includes a genital/scrotal exception; those operations are explicitly outside this objective. No universal statement about every procedure or exact infection-risk multiplier.
claim.variety3.hair.avoid-razor-nongenit.applicablePopulation: Adults comparing preparation plans for a non-genital operative field.
